觀賢王之訓刑，惟欲詳明法意而盡乎心力也。甚矣，刑罰之用，不可不致其謹也！苟於比罪之際，不能詳明法意而盡乎心力，又何以致刑罰之當也哉？昔穆王訓刑以告有邦有土，而言及乎此。謂夫五刑之屬三千，載之刑書，有定法也。然天下之情無窮，刑書所載有限，故罪無正律，則以上下刑而比附其罪也。善用法者，可不致
translation_en:
… Yue. In later days, when Gaozong became an exemplary king of Shang and Fu Yue a worthy coadjutor of Shang, they truly had no cause to feel ashamed before Cheng Tang and Yi Yin—and rightly so!

"Look carefully to the laws, and deal with them with meticulous care."
Chen Liang 陳良
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: Among those in the examination hall who wrote on this topic, most erred on the side of vagueness. This essay elucidates the meaning of adjudicating offenses by analogy, leaving almost nothing unexpressed; it deserves to be selected.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳 comments: It brings out King Mu's 穆王 compassionate and generous intent in instructing on punishments—truly a fine piece.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: Other papers largely failed to elaborate on carefully clarifying the intent of the law; for genuine insight and fluent prose, none surpasses this composition.
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zheng 鄭 comments: Its grasp of the topic's meaning is clear; commendable.

Observing the worthy king's instructions on punishments, one sees that he desired only that they carefully clarify the intent of the law and exhaust the strength of their minds. Indeed, in the application of punishments and penalties, one cannot but exercise the utmost caution! If, when adjudicating offenses by analogy, one cannot carefully clarify the intent of the law and exhaust the strength of one's mind, how then can one achieve appropriateness in punishments and penalties? In antiquity, when King Mu gave instructions on punishments to inform the lords of states and territories, he spoke of this. He meant that the statutory offenses under the Five Punishments number three thousand, and as recorded in the books of punishments, they have fixed laws. Yet the circumstances of the world are boundless, whereas what is recorded in the books of punishments is finite; therefore, when an offense has no exact statute, one compares it against heavier and lighter punishments to adjudicate the offense by analogy. For those who are skilled at applying the law, how could they not exercise…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其謹哉是故僭亂之辭固不可因之以比附也
爾必詳明法意而裁度於上下之間不妄比附
以差誤於僭亂之辭可也不行之法亦不可用
之以比附也爾必詳明律意而斟酌於輕重之
際不強比附於今所不行之法可也夫惟察惟
法若可以即罰矣然猶恐其有或差也又當研
精覃思而詳審密察之盡其心詳明法意亦可
以即罰矣然猶慮其有或惑也尤當竭其才能
而叅錯考求之盡其力則上下比附無不宜輕
===
重比附無不當矣吁既詳明法意而求以合於
法尤盡已心力而求無愧於心則刑罰之用焉
有不中者哉抑考穆王訓刑以誥四方一篇專
訓贖刑而上文言之尤詳然大辟皆贖誠非舜
典金作贖刑之意但其哀矜惻怛猶可以想見
三代忠厚之遺意而此與上文言其審克之者
三又見其丁寧忠厚之至此夫子所以錄之於
書也歟
詩義
punctuated:
其謹哉？是故僭亂之辭，固不可因之以比附也；爾必詳明法意，而裁度於上下之間，不妄比附以差誤於僭亂之辭可也。不行之法，亦不可用之以比附也；爾必詳明律意，而斟酌於輕重之際，不強比附於今所不行之法可也。夫「惟察惟法」，若可以即罰矣，然猶恐其有或差也，又當研精覃思而詳審密察之。盡其心，詳明法意，亦可以即罰矣，然猶慮其有或惑也，尤當竭其才能而叅錯考求之。盡其力，則上下比附無不宜，輕重比附無不當矣。吁！既詳明法意而求以合於法，尤盡已心力而求無愧於心，則刑罰之用，焉有不中者哉？抑考穆王訓刑以誥四方，一篇專訓贖刑，而上文言之尤詳。然大辟皆贖，誠非《舜典》「金作贖刑」之意。但其哀矜惻怛，猶可以想見三代忠厚之遺意；而此與上文言「其審克之」者三，又見其丁寧忠厚之至。此夫子所以錄之於《書》也歟！

詩義
translation_en:
… the utmost caution? Therefore, presumptuous and disorderly pleas certainly must not be relied upon to make analogies; you must carefully clarify the intent of the law and weigh matters between the heavier and lighter penalties, so that you do not rashly draw analogies and fall into error through presumptuous and disorderly pleas. Laws no longer in force likewise must not be used to make analogies; you must carefully clarify the intent of the statutes and deliberate over the degree of severity, so that you do not forcibly draw analogies to laws that are no longer practiced today. Now, "by discerning examination and by adherence to the law," it would seem that one could proceed directly to punishment; yet, still fearing that there might be some error, one must further apply deep and focused thought to examine the case with thorough care and close scrutiny. Having exhausted one's mind to carefully clarify the intent of the law, one could likewise proceed directly to punishment; yet, still worrying that there might be some confusion, one must all the more exert one's full abilities to cross-examine and investigate the facts. When one's strength is thus exhausted, analogies to higher or lower penalties will never fail to be suitable, and analogies between lighter and heavier offenses will never fail to be appropriate. Ah! Having both carefully clarified the intent of the law in seeking to conform to the law, and moreover exhausted one's own mind and strength in seeking to have a clear conscience, how could the application of punishments ever fail to hit the mark? Yet if we examine how King Mu gave instructions on punishments to proclaim them to the four quarters, the entire chapter specifically teaches the redemption of punishments, which the preceding passage discusses in particular detail. That even capital offenses could all be redeemed is truly not the meaning of "metal is used for redeemable punishments" in the Canon of Shun (Shundian). However, from his compassion and sympathetic grief, one can still envision the surviving spirit of the loyal generosity of the Three Dynasties; and the fact that here and in the preceding text he says "examine into it and attain the truth" three times further shows the utmost earnestness of his benevolent care. Is this not why the Master [Confucius] recorded it in the Book of Documents (Shu)?

Expositions on the Classic of Poetry (Shiyi)

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
迨天之未陰雨徹彼桑土綢繆牖户
姚鈇
同考試官教授劉批周公忠愛王室之心能
盖𤼵越之宜在所録
考試官教授劉批詞理俱稱宜冠本經
考試官教授鄭批此篇說出周公忠愛王室之
意足見學識
當無事之時為防患之計此聖臣託喻告君之
深意也盖思患預防為國之道當然也周公當
===
國家無事而為預防之計其忠愛之意不既深
乎昔周公作詩貽王託為鳥言以自比意若曰
彼雲未有渰雨未既零斯時也居室固無事矣
殊不知天道陰晴互為變化今日雖無事寧保
後日之無事乎故我及天未陰雨之時則徹彼
桑土而牖户是葺取彼桑根而隙穴是補則居
室完固庶可以備陰雨之患矣然周公豈徒為
物評哉正以喻己深愛王室而預防其患難之
意耳彼其治隆於上俗美於下斯時也國家固
punctuated:
「迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖户。」
姚鈇
同考試官教授劉批：周公忠愛王室之心，能盡𤼵越之，宜在所録。
考試官教授劉批：詞理俱稱，宜冠本經。
考試官教授鄭批：此篇說出周公忠愛王室之意，足見學識。
當無事之時，為防患之計，此聖臣託喻告君之深意也。盖思患預防，為國之道當然也。周公當國家無事而為預防之計，其忠愛之意不既深乎？昔周公作詩貽王，託為鳥言以自比，意若曰：彼雲未有渰，雨未既零，斯時也，居室固無事矣。殊不知天道陰晴，互為變化，今日雖無事，寧保後日之無事乎？故我及天未陰雨之時，則徹彼桑土而牖户是葺，取彼桑根而隙穴是補，則居室完固，庶可以備陰雨之患矣。然周公豈徒為物評哉？正以喻己深愛王室，而預防其患難之意耳。彼其治隆於上，俗美於下，斯時也，國家固
translation_en:
"Before the sky grows dark with rain, I stripped that mulberry-root bark, and bound fast my window and door."
Yao Fu 姚鈇
Comment by Associate Examiner, Confucian School Instructor Liu: The Duke of Zhou's heart of loyalty and love for the royal house is fully [盖 for 盡?] brought out and expressed here; it deserves to be selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner, Confucian School Instructor Liu: Both the diction and the reasoning are well-matched; it deserves to top the essays on this Classic.
Comment by Examiner, Confucian School Instructor Zheng: This essay brings out the Duke of Zhou's intention of loyalty and love for the royal house, which is sufficient to show the candidate's learning and insight.

In times of peace, to make plans for guarding against calamity—this was the profound intention of the sage minister in using an allegory to advise his lord. Indeed, anticipating calamity and taking precautions beforehand is naturally the proper way to govern a state. When the Duke of Zhou made plans for precaution while the state was at peace, was not his intention of loyalty and love profound indeed?

Long ago, when the Duke of Zhou composed this poem to present to the King, he spoke in the persona of a bird to compare himself to it, as if to say: When those clouds have not yet gathered darkly and the rain has not yet fallen, at such a time one's dwelling is certainly free from trouble. Yet one fails to realize that in the Way of Heaven, overcast and clear weather alternate and change into one another; although today is free from trouble, how can one guarantee that future days will also be free from trouble? Therefore, before the sky grows dark with rain, I strip that mulberry-root bark to repair my window and door, taking those mulberry roots to mend the cracks and holes; then the dwelling will be whole and secure, and perhaps ready to withstand the calamity of dark rain.

Yet how could the Duke of Zhou merely be commenting on creatures? He used this precisely to illustrate his own deep love for the royal house and his intention to take precautions against its troubles and difficulties. When governance flourishes above and customs are admirable below, at such a time the state is certainly…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
無虞矣殊不知世道治亂相為倚伏今日雖無
虞寧保後日之無虞乎故我及國未多難之際
則制作服勞毅然以王事為己任吐握盡悴恍
然以國計為己憂則國家鞏固庶乎可以免意
外之虞矣噫保邦於未危則危不至制治於未
亂則亂不生此周公忠愛之深意宜其拳拳喻
之以為成王告也抑論之消息盈虛之相盪安
危治亂之相承理之常然苟不預為之計逮難
至而為之備患生而為之防則為計晚矣故古
===
人當泰和盛治之時必思患而預防之也大易
亦曰君子思患而豫防之治國家者宜鑒於斯
式固爾猶淮夷卒獲翩彼飛鴞集于泮林
食我桑黮懷我好音憬彼淮夷来獻其琛
元龜象齒大賂南金
司馬𡌦
同考試官教授劉批此題場中作者多以式
固爾猶為脩文教殊失本旨是篇體認既真文亦
脫腐其深於詩學者歟
punctuated:
無虞矣。殊不知世道治亂，相為倚伏，今日雖無虞，寧保後日之無虞乎？故我及國未多難之際，則制作服勞，毅然以王事為己任；吐握盡悴，恍然以國計為己憂。則國家鞏固，庶乎可以免意外之虞矣。噫！保邦於未危，則危不至；制治於未亂，則亂不生。此周公忠愛之深意，宜其拳拳喻之以為成王告也。抑論之，消息盈虛之相盪，安危治亂之相承，理之常然。苟不預為之計，逮難至而為之備，患生而為之防，則為計晚矣。故古人當泰和盛治之時，必思患而預防之也。《大易》亦曰：「君子思患而豫防之。」治國家者，宜鑒於斯。

「式固爾猶，淮夷卒獲。翩彼飛鴞，集于泮林。食我桑黮，懷我好音。憬彼淮夷，来獻其琛。元龜象齒，大賂南金。」
司馬𡌦
同考試官教授劉批：此題場中作者，多以「式固爾猶」為脩文教，殊失本旨。是篇體認既真，文亦脫腐，其深於《詩》學者歟！
translation_en:
…free from cause for anxiety. Yet little do people realize that in the course of human affairs, order and disorder lean upon and give rise to each other. Even if there is no cause for anxiety today, how can one guarantee there will be none in days to come? Therefore, while the state is not yet beset by many difficulties, I institute rites and laws and toil in service, resolutely taking the king's business as my own responsibility; I spit out my food and grasp my hair to receive the worthy, exhausting myself in care and anxiously taking the plans of the state as my own concern. Thus the state will be consolidated, and perhaps it may be spared unforeseen perils."

Alas! If one secures the state before danger arrives, danger will not come; if one establishes order before disorder arises, disorder will not be born. This was the profound intent of the Duke of Zhou's loyal affection, and it was fitting that he earnestly used this metaphor to admonish King Cheng. Moreover, if we consider the matter further, the mutual alternation of waxing and waning, fullness and emptiness, and the succession of safety and danger, order and disorder, are constant principles. If one does not plan in advance, waiting until difficulties arrive before preparing for them, or until calamities arise before guarding against them, then one's planning is too late. Therefore, when the ancients were in an era of great harmony and flourishing governance, they invariably reflected on potential calamities and guarded against them in advance. The Great Changes (Yijing) likewise says: "The superior man reflects on potential calamity and guards against it in advance." Those who govern a state ought to take this as a mirror.

"Make firm your plans, and the Huai Yi will finally be captured. Fluttering are those flying owls, settling in the forest by the semicircular water; they eat our mulberries and cherish us with their good notes. Awakened are those Huai Yi, coming to present their treasures: great tortoises and elephant tusks, and grand gifts of southern metal." [Book of Odes, Mao 299, "Panshui"]

Sima Yan 司馬𡌦

Associate Examiner and Prefectural Instructor Liu commented: Among the candidates in the examination hall writing on this topic, most took "make firm your plans" to mean cultivating civil education, which quite misses the original purport. This essay not only grasps the true meaning, its prose also sheds all staleness. Surely its author is deeply versed in the study of the Odes!

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授劉批理明詞婉得詩人之旨
考試官教授鄭批理有定見文有發揮真絕經
之傑作者
詩人頌願魯侯善兵謀而終以服乎遠必興遠
人化文教而有以厚其貢盖遠人雖服於兵謀
之善而尤化於文教之脩也魯人以是頌願其
君其忠愛之意至矣昔詩人因魯侯飲於泮宫
而致頌禱之辭其意若曰淮夷之為魯患也久
矣勢不得以不伐然伐之徒恃其武孰若審固
===
其謀乎必使兵甲素蘊於胸中籌策常閑於意
外□勝而動不輕舉而妄動也好謀而成不蓄
疑以敗謀也果能審固謀猶如是吾知淮夷始
雖未服終必稽首來庭所謂孔淑不逆者有焉
今雖未從後必帖耳聽命所謂莫不率從者有
焉然服遠之道雖貴於兵謀之善尤在於文教
之脩故詩人又託興而言曰翩彼飛鴞既集於
泮林矣于焉食我桑黮則懷其好音矣物止泮
宫禮義之地尚有以變其音人感泮宫禮義之
punctuated:
考試官教授劉批：理明詞婉，得詩人之旨。
考試官教授鄭批：理有定見，文有發揮，真絕經之傑作者。
詩人頌願魯侯善兵謀而終以服乎遠，必興遠人化文教而有以厚其貢。盖遠人雖服於兵謀之善，而尤化於文教之脩也。魯人以是頌願其君，其忠愛之意至矣。昔詩人因魯侯飲於泮宫，而致頌禱之辭，其意若曰：淮夷之為魯患也久矣，勢不得以不伐。然伐之徒恃其武，孰若審固其謀乎？必使兵甲素蘊於胸中，籌策常閑於意外；□勝而動，不輕舉而妄動也；好謀而成，不蓄疑以敗謀也。果能審固謀猶如是，吾知淮夷始雖未服，終必稽首來庭，所謂「孔淑不逆」者有焉；今雖未從，後必帖耳聽命，所謂「莫不率從」者有焉。然服遠之道，雖貴於兵謀之善，尤在於文教之脩。故詩人又託興而言曰：翩彼飛鴞，既集於泮林矣；于焉食我桑黮，則懷其好音矣。物止泮宫禮義之地，尚有以變其音；人感泮宫禮義之…
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Liu: The reasoning is clear and the phrasing graceful; it captures the intent of the poet.
Comment by Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zheng: The reasoning shows settled insight and the writing displays thorough elaboration; truly an outstanding author who excels in the Classic.
The poet praises and wishes that the Marquis of Lu will excel in military strategy so as ultimately to bring distant peoples into submission, and he goes on to evoke by metaphor how those distant peoples, transformed by civil teaching, will generously present their tribute. For although distant peoples may submit to excellence in military strategy, they are above all transformed by the cultivation of civil teaching. In praising and wishing this for their lord, the people of Lu showed the utmost loyalty and affection. Of old, on the occasion of the Marquis of Lu feasting at the Pan Palace, the poet offered words of praise and prayer, the purport of which was as follows: The Huai Yi tribes have long been a menace to Lu, and circumstances leave us no choice but to mount a campaign against them. Yet in campaigning against them, how can merely relying on martial force compare with making our plans deliberate and firm? We must ensure that armor and weaponry are long stored within the breast, and that stratagems are constantly practiced for the unexpected; that we move only after [calculating?] victory, neither acting rashly nor moving recklessly; and that we succeed through a fondness for planning, never harboring doubts that would ruin our plans. If indeed we can make our plans and counsels deliberate and firm like this, I know that although the Huai Yi have not yet submitted at the outset, in the end they will surely bow their heads to the ground and come to court—what the ode calls "very good and not rebellious" will come to pass; although they do not obey now, later they will surely droop their ears and heed our commands—what the ode calls "none failing to follow and obey" will come to pass. Even so, while the way to bring distant peoples into submission values excellence in military strategy, it lies still more in the cultivation of civil teaching. Therefore the poet again uses an evocative metaphor, saying: Fluttering are those flying owls, which have already gathered in the grove by the Pan waters; once they eat our mulberries there, they comfort us with their pleasant notes. If creatures resting in the Pan Palace, a place of ritual and righteousness, are still able to change their harsh cries, then when men are moved by the [transformation] of ritual and righteousness at the Pan Palace…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
化寧不有以革其心哉吾見蠢爾無知之淮夷
不但不逆而已將變惡為善憬然覺悟而来獻
其琛焉不但率從而已將轉逆為順幡然慕義
而来貢其寳焉彼元亀象齒至貴之琛也来獻
于我于以表其敬君之禮荆揚之金至重之寳
也大遺於我于以將其奉上之誠夫善兵謀則
遠人服其威脩文教則遠人服其德德威並著
文武兼資詩人以是頌願魯侯何其至哉抑考
淮夷自伯禽以来世為魯患故詩人頌禱其君
===
必欲其克服以無愧於烈祖伯禽也然其事不
見於春秋豈淮夷嘗病杞鄫僖公從齊桓謀以
攘斥之歟是詩之頌禱或過其實而明德服遠
之意自足以垂訓也孔子亦曰遠人不服則脩
文德以来之服遠者當以為法
春秋義
公會齊侯盟于柯〔莊公十三年〕齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕
公會齊侯宋公陳世子欵鄭世子華盟于
寗母〔僖公七年〕公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯
punctuated:
化，寧不有以革其心哉？吾見蠢爾無知之淮夷，不但不逆而已，將變惡為善，憬然覺悟而来獻其琛焉；不但率從而已，將轉逆為順，幡然慕義而来貢其寳焉。彼元亀、象齒，至貴之琛也，来獻于我，于以表其敬君之禮；荆揚之金，至重之寳也，大遺於我，于以將其奉上之誠。夫善兵謀則遠人服其威，脩文教則遠人服其德。德威並著，文武兼資，詩人以是頌願魯侯，何其至哉！抑考淮夷自伯禽以来，世為魯患，故詩人頌禱其君，必欲其克服，以無愧於烈祖伯禽也。然其事不見於《春秋》，豈淮夷嘗病杞、鄫，僖公從齊桓謀以攘斥之歟？是詩之頌禱或過其實，而明德服遠之意，自足以垂訓也。孔子亦曰：「遠人不服，則脩文德以来之。」服遠者當以為法。

春秋義
公會齊侯盟于柯〔莊公十三年〕；齊人救邢〔閔公元年〕；公會齊侯、宋公、陳世子欵、鄭世子華盟于寗母〔僖公七年〕；公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、
translation_en:
…transformation, how could they not reform their hearts? I see that the foolish and ignorant Huai Yi will not only cease to rebel, but will turn from evil to good, awaken to realization, and come to offer their treasures; they will not only follow in obedience, but will turn from defiance to submission, be moved to admire righteousness, and come to present their valuables as tribute. Those great tortoises and elephant tusks are the most precious of treasures—they come to offer them to us in order to express the ritual of honoring the ruler. The metal of Jing and Yang is the most valuable of riches—they present it to us in abundance in order to convey the sincerity of serving their superior. Now, when military strategy is sound, distant peoples submit to one's majesty; when civil教 (education and culture) is cultivated, distant peoples submit to one's virtue. With virtue and majesty both manifest, and civil and military capacities combined, how supreme is the poet's praise and wish for the Marquis of Lu in these terms! Yet if we examine the history, the Huai Yi had been a hereditary menace to Lu ever since the time of Boqin; therefore, in praising and praying for his ruler, the poet обязательно wished for him to conquer and subdue them so as to bring no shame upon his illustrious ancestor Boqin. However, this affair does not appear in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). Could it be that the Huai Yi had once harassed Qi and Zeng, and Duke Xi followed the counsels of Duke Huan of Qi to repel them? The praise and prayers of this ode may exceed the reality, yet the principle of illuminating virtue to win over distant peoples is in itself sufficient to hand down as a lesson. Confucius also said: "If distant people do not submit, then cultivate civil virtue to attract them." Those who seek to win over the distant ought to take this as their model.

Exposition on the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"The Duke met the Marquis of Qi and made a covenant at Ke" [Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang]; "Men of Qi rescued Xing" [First year of Duke Min]; "The Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, Heir Apparent Kuan of Chen, and Heir Apparent Hua of Zheng, and made a covenant at Ningmu" [Seventh year of Duke Xi]; "The Duke met the Grand宰 Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
鄭伯許男曹伯于葵丘諸侯盟于葵丘
僖公九年宋人圍曹僖公十九年宋人齊人楚人
盟于鹿上宋公楚子陳侯蔡侯鄭伯許
男曹伯會于盂僖公二十一年宋公及楚人戰
于泓宋師敗績僖公二十二年
程愈
同考試官訓導張批管仲子魚盡忠言於桓
襄皆出本傳場中作者鮮有全德其旨此篇考據詳
明措詞簡當宜置前列
===
考試官教授劉批筆力老健宜在魁選
考試官教授鄭批說出桓襄成敗之由超出衆作
創霸者屢從忠言而業盛繼霸者屢違忠言而
業隳甚矣為國不可不用忠言也觀齊桓從管
仲之言以興宋襄違子魚之諫以敗可驗矣夫
功之成非成於成之日盖必有所由起齊桓欲
成九合一匡之功而民卒受賜者無他由用忠
言而不自用也是故于柯盟魯魯臣可讐也乃
從管仲許諾之言而捐汶陽以收魯狄人伐邢
punctuated:
鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘，諸侯盟于葵丘。僖公九年。宋人圍曹。僖公十九年。宋人、齊人、楚人盟于鹿上，宋公、楚子、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會于盂。僖公二十一年。宋公及楚人戰于泓，宋師敗績。僖公二十二年。
程愈
同考試官訓導張批：管仲、子魚盡忠言於桓、襄，皆出本傳。場中作者鮮有全德其旨，此篇考據詳明，措詞簡當，宜置前列。
考試官教授劉批：筆力老健，宜在魁選。
考試官教授鄭批：說出桓、襄成敗之由，超出衆作。
創霸者屢從忠言而業盛，繼霸者屢違忠言而業隳。甚矣，為國不可不用忠言也！觀齊桓從管仲之言以興，宋襄違子魚之諫以敗，可驗矣。夫功之成，非成於成之日，盖必有所由起。齊桓欲成九合一匡之功，而民卒受賜者，無他，由用忠言而不自用也。是故于柯盟魯，魯臣可讐也，乃從管仲許諾之言，而捐汶陽以收魯；狄人伐邢，

… the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu; the feudal lords made a covenant at Kuiqiu (ninth year of Duke Xi). The men of Song besieged Cao (nineteenth year of Duke Xi). The men of Song, the men of Qi, and the men of Chu made a covenant at Lushang; the Duke of Song, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao met at Yu (twenty-first year of Duke Xi). The Duke of Song and the men of Chu fought a battle at the Hong River; the army of Song was utterly defeated (twenty-second year of Duke Xi).

Cheng Yu 程愈

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang: That Guan Zhong 管仲 and Ziyu 子魚 offered their utmost loyal counsel to Dukes Huan 桓 and Xiang 襄 all comes from the standard commentaries. Among the candidates in the examination hall, few have fully grasped [text has 德 for 得?] this import. This essay's textual grounding is detailed and clear, and its wording is concise and fitting; it should be placed in the front ranks.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu: The brushwork is seasoned and vigorous; it belongs among the top selections.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: It articulates the reasons for the success of Duke Huan and the failure of Duke Xiang, surpassing the rest of the compositions.

He who founded the hegemony repeatedly followed loyal counsel and his enterprise flourished; he who sought to succeed to the hegemony repeatedly defied loyal counsel and his enterprise collapsed. Crucial indeed it is that in governing a state one cannot fail to employ loyal counsel! When we observe how Duke Huan of Qi rose by following the words of Guan Zhong, and how Duke Xiang of Song met defeat by defying the remonstrances of Ziyu, this can be verified. Now, the achievement of merit is not accomplished on the day it is consummated; rather, it must have that from which it originates. That Duke Huan of Qi wished to achieve the merit of nine times assembling the lords and once rectifying the realm, and that the people ultimately received the benefit of it, was due to nothing else than his employing loyal counsel and not relying solely on himself. Therefore, when making a covenant with Lu at Ke, the minister of Lu might well have been treated as an enemy, yet he followed Guan Zhong's advice to honor his promise and relinquished the lands of Wenyang in order to win over Lu. When the Di barbarians attacked Xing, …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
邢患可憫也乃從管仲簡書之諫而遣偏師以
救邢子華請臣寗母仲曰當却也即却其内臣
之請宰孔賜胙葵丘仲曰當拜也即致天下拜
之恭從善如流若此是以宰孔返駕葵丘有盟
王朝五禁大明當時天下諸侯咸喻其志霸業
於是乎盛矣噫管仲忠於齊者也桓公一則仲
父二則仲父其盛也宜哉經曰好問則裕桓其
有焉至若禍之作不作於作之日亦必有所由
兆宋襄欲繼齊桓之烈而卒不克終者無他由
===
自用而不用忠言也彼其圍曹之役既不聴子
魚省德之諫而逞私忿於曹鹿上之盟又不鑒
子魚後敗之戒而求諸侯於楚盂之會也子魚
兵車之謀善矣而必以乗車之會往泓之戰也
子魚請擊之計得矣而必俟濟險而後擊聞諫
愈甚如此是以楚師既濟宋遂不支一皷而兵
敗再皷而身傷霸事於是乎隳矣噫子魚忠於
宋者也襄公有一子魚而不能用其敗也宜哉
經曰自用則小襄實以之嗟夫忠言逆耳利於
punctuated: 邢患可憫也，乃從管仲簡書之諫，而遣偏師以救邢。子華請臣寗母，仲曰當却也，即却其内臣之請；宰孔賜胙葵丘，仲曰當拜也，即致天下拜之恭。從善如流若此，是以宰孔返駕，葵丘有盟，王朝五禁，大明當時，天下諸侯咸喻其志，霸業於是乎盛矣。噫！管仲忠於齊者也，桓公一則仲父，二則仲父，其盛也宜哉！《經》曰：「好問則裕。」桓其有焉。至若禍之作，不作於作之日，亦必有所由兆。宋襄欲繼齊桓之烈，而卒不克終者，無他，由自用而不用忠言也。彼其圍曹之役，既不聴子魚省德之諫，而逞私忿於曹；鹿上之盟，又不鑒子魚後敗之戒，而求諸侯於楚。盂之會也，子魚兵車之謀善矣，而必以乗車之會往；泓之戰也，子魚請擊之計得矣，而必俟濟險而後擊。聞諫愈甚如此，是以楚師既濟，宋遂不支，一皷而兵敗，再皷而身傷，霸事於是乎隳矣。噫！子魚忠於宋者也，襄公有一子魚而不能用，其敗也宜哉！《經》曰：「自用則小。」襄實以之。嗟夫！忠言逆耳利於
translation_en:
…the distress of Xing was pitiable, so he followed Guan Zhong's remonstrance regarding the bamboo-slip dispatches and sent a detachment of troops to rescue Xing. When Zihua requested to submit as a subject at Ningmu, Zhong said he ought to be rebuffed, and Duke Huan immediately rejected his request to become an internal subject. When Zai Kong bestowed the sacrificial meat at Kuiqiu, Zhong said he ought to bow in receipt, and Duke Huan immediately showed the reverence of bowing from the foot of the hall. Because he followed good counsel as naturally as water flows downhill like this, upon Zai Kong's return from his journey, the covenant at Kuiqiu was concluded, the five prohibitions of the royal court were made brightly manifest in that age, the feudal lords of the realm all understood his aims, and his hegemonic enterprise thereupon flourished! Alas, Guan Zhong was loyal to Qi, and Duke Huan addressed him at every turn as "Uncle Zhong"—that he flourished was fitting indeed! The Classic says, "He who delights in questioning becomes abundant." Huan possessed this quality.

As for the outbreak of calamity, it does not arise on the day it breaks out, for it too must have its omens from which it begins. That Duke Xiang of Song wished to continue the meritorious achievements of Huan of Qi, yet ultimately failed to bring them to completion, was for no other reason than that he relied on his own judgment and did not employ loyal words. In his campaign besieging Cao, he did not listen to Ziyu's remonstrance to examine his own virtue, but vented his private resentment against Cao; in the covenant at Lushang, he again failed to heed Ziyu's warning of subsequent defeat, and sought the feudal lords from Chu. At the meeting at Yu, Ziyu's counsel to go with war chariots was sound, yet Duke Xiang insisted on attending as a meeting with ceremonial carriages; at the battle of the Hong River, Ziyu's plan requesting to attack was well-conceived, yet Duke Xiang insisted on waiting until they had crossed the difficult ford before attacking. Because he grew ever more obstinate upon hearing remonstrance like this, once the Chu army had crossed, Song consequently could not hold out; at the first roll of the drums his troops were defeated, at the second roll of the drums he himself was wounded, and his hegemonic undertaking was thereupon ruined! Alas, Ziyu was loyal to Song; that Duke Xiang had a single Ziyu and could not make use of him—that he was defeated was fitting indeed! The Classic says, "He who relies on himself becomes small." Xiang truly exemplified this. Alas! Loyal words grate on the ear yet are beneficial to…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
行賢者有益於人國也尚矣莫聖於堯舜而必
資命岳牧莫聖於湯武而必師尊伊呂帝王且
爾况霸者乎雖然襄公之於子魚不必論矣獨
惜夫桓公之任管仲最專且久而仲無誠意正
心格君之學以致主於王道也使其得聞聖賢
大學之道其功烈豈止是哉
公及齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯
會王世子于首止僖公五年公會晉侯齊侯
宋公蔡侯鄭伯衛子莒子盟于踐土公
===
朝于王所公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭
伯陳子莒子邾子秦人于溫天王狩于
河陽公朝于王所僖公二十八年
姚綱
同考試官訓導張批桓文尊奬王室迹雖同
而心則異作者多無定見此篇說出二公心術之正譎
殆無餘蘊可嘉
考試官教授劉批得春秋謹嚴之旨
考試官教授鄭批詞嚴誼正可取
punctuated:
行，賢者有益於人國也尚矣。莫聖於堯、舜，而必資命岳牧；莫聖於湯、武，而必師尊伊、呂。帝王且爾，况霸者乎？雖然，襄公之於子魚不必論矣；獨惜夫桓公之任管仲最專且久，而仲無誠意、正心、格君之學以致主於王道也。使其得聞聖賢大學之道，其功烈豈止是哉！

「公及齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會王世子于首止。」〔僖公五年〕「公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衛子、莒子盟于踐土。公朝于王所。」「公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、陳子、莒子、邾子、秦人于溫。天王狩于河陽。公朝于王所。」〔僖公二十八年〕
姚綱
同考試官訓導張批：桓、文尊奬王室，迹雖同而心則異，作者多無定見。此篇說出二公心術之正譎，殆無餘蘊，可嘉。
考試官教授劉批：得《春秋》謹嚴之旨。
考試官教授鄭批：詞嚴誼正，可取。
translation_en:
… conduct; that worthy men are beneficial to a state has long been true. None were more sagely than Yao and Shun, yet they necessarily relied upon and gave charges to the Four Peaks and Twelve Pastors; none were more sagely than Tang and Wu, yet they necessarily honored Yi Yin and Lü Shang as teachers. If even emperors and kings were thus, how much more so a hegemon? Even so, Duke Xiang’s treatment of Ziyu need not be discussed; one only regrets that although Duke Huan’s employment of Guan Zhong was most exclusive and enduring, Zhong lacked the learning of making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, and correcting the ruler so as to bring his lord to the Kingly Way. Had he been able to hear the Way of the Great Learning of the sages and worthies, how would his achievements and glory have stopped merely at this!

“The Duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met with the King’s Heir Apparent at Shouzhi.” [Fifth year of Duke Xi] “The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and made a covenant at Jiantu. The Duke had an audience at the King’s residence.” “The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Chen, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and a man of Qin at Wen. The Heavenly King hunted at Heyang. The Duke had an audience at the King’s residence.” [Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi]

Yao Gang 姚綱
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Zhang: Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin both honored and supported the royal house; although their outward actions were similar, their intentions were different, and writers mostly lack a settled view on this. This essay brings out the uprightness and craftiness of the two dukes’ states of mind, leaving almost nothing unexpressed; it is commendable.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Liu: It grasps the rigorous and strict purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu).
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng: The diction is rigorous and the principles are upright; it is worthy of selection.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
尊王之禮出於變春秋美其心之正覲王之禮
似乎正春秋著其心之譎夫霸者之行事不惟
其跡惟其心觀春秋書齊桓殊會世子晉文兩
致天王而二公之心術見矣且齊桓自召陵服
楚以来乃心罔不在王室今也惠王寵愛庶孽
子鄭之位危疑桓公因前星之照臨講首止之
大會控大扶小使天下咸知儲副之當尊辨名
定分使列國咸知樹子之難易然世子君也而
下會諸侯則陵諸侯臣也而上會世子則抗是
===
禮之變而不可訓矣殊不知桓之心則以為王
室不寧大國之憂與其後勤諸侯以靖大難不
若預定大本以窒亂源初非假是以要人心也
是一舉而君臣父子之道皆得矣春秋於首止
殊會世子豈非美其正乎若夫晉文自城濮敗
楚以来志亦在於獎王於是踐土有盟作宮獻
捷致王下勞既率諸侯為衡雍之朝于溫之會
自嫌強大請王出狩復率列辟展河陽之覲夫
以天子再臨彷彿巡狩四方之制諸侯再朝庶
punctuated:
尊王之禮出於變，《春秋》美其心之正；覲王之禮似乎正，《春秋》著其心之譎。夫霸者之行事，不惟其跡，惟其心。觀《春秋》書齊桓殊會世子，晉文兩致天王，而二公之心術見矣。

且齊桓自召陵服楚以来，乃心罔不在王室。今也惠王寵愛庶孽，子鄭之位危疑，桓公因前星之照臨，講首止之大會，控大扶小，使天下咸知儲副之當尊；辨名定分，使列國咸知樹子之難易。然世子，君也，而下會諸侯，則陵；諸侯，臣也，而上會世子，則抗。是禮之變，而不可訓矣。殊不知桓之心，則以為王室不寧，大國之憂，與其後勤諸侯以靖大難，不若預定大本以窒亂源，初非假是以要人心也。是一舉而君臣父子之道皆得矣。《春秋》於首止殊會世子，豈非美其正乎？

若夫晉文自城濮敗楚以来，志亦在於獎王。於是踐土有盟，作宮獻捷，致王下勞，既率諸侯為衡雍之朝；于溫之會，自嫌強大，請王出狩，復率列辟展河陽之覲。夫以天子再臨，彷彿巡狩四方之制；諸侯再朝，庶…
translation_en:
When the ritual of honoring the King arose from an extraordinary expedient, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) praised the uprightness of the actor's intentions; when the ritual of having an audience with the King appeared to be orthodox, the Spring and Autumn Annals exposed the craftiness of the actor's intentions. In the actions of the hegemons, one should examine not merely their outward traces, but their underlying intentions. Observing how the Spring and Autumn Annals records Duke Huan of Qi (Qi Huan) separately meeting the Royal Heir Apparent, and Duke Wen of Jin (Jin Wen) twice summoning the Heavenly King, the mental motivations of the two dukes become evident.

Moreover, ever since Duke Huan of Qi forced Chu into submission at Shaoling, his heart had never ceased to be with the Royal House. Now, King Hui favored a son born of a concubine, rendering Prince Zheng's position as heir precarious and doubtful. Availing himself of the shining presence of the Fore-star [the Heir Apparent], Duke Huan convened the great assembly at Shouzhi, restraining the great and supporting the weak so that all under Heaven would know that the Heir Apparent must be honored, and distinguishing names and fixing statuses so that the feudal states would all know that an appointed heir cannot easily be replaced. Yet the Heir Apparent is a ruler in status, and for him to descend to meet with the feudal lords is a degradation; the feudal lords are subjects, and for them to ascend to meet with the Heir Apparent is presumptuous. This was an extraordinary alteration of ritual propriety and could not serve as a standard teaching. Little did people realize that in Duke Huan's mind, he considered the instability of the Royal House to be the concern of a great state: rather than later mobilizing the feudal lords to quell a great catastrophe, it was better to establish the fundamental succession in advance so as to stop up the source of disorder. From the beginning, he was not using this as a pretext to win over people's hearts. Thus, by this single act, the proper Way of ruler and subject, father and son, was altogether fulfilled. When the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded the separate meeting with the Heir Apparent at Shouzhi, was it not praising his uprightness?

As for Duke Wen of Jin, ever since he defeated Chu at Chengpu, his ambition likewise lay in upholding the King. Thereupon there was the covenant at Jiantu, where he built a palace and presented spoils of war, causing the King to come down to reward his toil, after which he led the feudal lords to hold court at Hengyong. At the assembly at Wen, feeling uneasy about his own overwhelming power, he requested the King to go out on a hunting inspection, and once again led the assembled rulers to perform an audience at Heyang. Now, with the Son of Heaven twice descending in person, it resembled the institution of touring the four quarters on inspection; with the feudal lords twice paying court, it almost…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
幾朝于方岳之典似禮之正不足以為異矣殊
不知文之心則以為周室雖衰威靈猶在致之
於會足以夸示諸侯託之以朝足以號召天下
初非有尊獎之誠也是再舉而君臣父子之名
實紊矣春秋於踐土于溫之下書王所之兩朝
又非著其譎乎厥後盟洮序王人於諸侯之上
葵丘不盟宰孔桓之正可知翟泉使諸侯大夫
盟子虎於王城之內文之譎愈甚雖然桓文正
譎孔子嘗辨之明矣然晉文踐土一盟猶有齊
===
桓尊王餘意而召王之事亦未必不由首止積
習之漸也此又讀經者所當知
禮記義
及夫禮樂之極乎天而蟠乎地行乎陰陽
而通乎鬼神窮高極遠而測深厚樂著太
始而禮居成物著不息者天也著不動者
地也一動一靜者天地之間也故聖人曰
禮樂云
黃珣
punctuated:
幾朝于方岳之典，似禮之正，不足以為異矣。殊不知文之心，則以為周室雖衰，威靈猶在，致之於會，足以夸示諸侯，託之以朝，足以號召天下，初非有尊獎之誠也。是再舉而君臣父子之名實紊矣。《春秋》於踐土、于溫之下，書「王所」之兩朝，又非著其譎乎？厥後盟洮，序王人於諸侯之上；葵丘，不盟宰孔，桓之正可知。翟泉，使諸侯大夫盟子虎於王城之內，文之譎愈甚。雖然，桓、文正譎，孔子嘗辨之明矣。然晉文踐土一盟，猶有齊桓尊王餘意，而召王之事，亦未必不由首止積習之漸也。此又讀經者所當知。

禮記義

及夫禮樂之極乎天而蟠乎地，行乎陰陽而通乎鬼神，窮高極遠而測深厚。樂著太始，而禮居成物。著不息者，天也；著不動者，地也。一動一靜者，天地之間也。故聖人曰「禮樂」云。

黃珣
translation_en:
…nearly matching the canon of audiences at the Four Peaks, which seemed to accord with ritual rectitude and gave no cause for wonder. Yet little did one realize that in the mind of Duke Wen of Jin, although the house of Zhou had declined, its august prestige still lingered; bringing the King to the assembly sufficed to boast before the feudal lords, and using the pretext of paying court sufficed to rally the realm—there was never any sincere intent to honor and support him. Thus, by these two acts, both the name and the reality of the relationship between ruler and minister, father and son, were thrown into disorder. In the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), under the entries for Jiantu and Wen, does not the recording of the two audiences at "the King's residence" expose his craftiness? Thereafter, in the covenant at Tao, the King's man was ranked above the feudal lords, and at Kuiqiu, Duke Huan did not require Zai Kong to swear the covenant—from this, Duke Huan's rectitude can be seen. At Diquan, however, having the grandees of the feudal lords swear a covenant with Zihu inside the Royal Capital showed Duke Wen's craftiness growing even more extreme. Even so, Confucius once clearly distinguished the rectitude of Duke Huan and the craftiness of Duke Wen. Yet the single covenant of Duke Wen of Jin at Jiantu still retained a lingering trace of Duke Huan of Qi's spirit of honoring the King, whereas the affair of summoning the King did not necessarily fail to arise from the gradual accumulation of practice begun at Shouzhi. This, too, is what readers of the Classic ought to know.

Exposition on the Record of Rites (Liji)

"When it comes to rites and music reaching to the height of heaven and coiling across the earth, operating through yin and yang and communicating with ghosts and spirits, exhausting the highest and furthest and fathoming the deep and thick: music manifests the Great Beginning, and rites abide in completed things. What manifests unceasingness is heaven; what manifests immobility is earth. Alternation between movement and stillness takes place between heaven and earth. Therefore the sages spoke of 'rites and music.'"

Huang Xun 黃珣

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官學正陳批塲中作者多以禮樂分
配造化為說間有知者又踈於分截惟此作能以成功所
合為主一破便合題意且文理俱到宜置高選
考試官教授劉批發明經旨透徹無餘
考試官教授鄭批說出禮樂之功用有合於造
化文理明白可取
論禮樂之成功充塞妙運於兩間故聖人必昭
揭其名以示夫人也盖聖人禮樂之功用充塞
流行於天地間者也苟不昭揭以示人又何以
===
顯名於天下也哉樂記君子謂夫聖人之作樂
出於天地自然之和制禮出於天地自然之序
及其成功之所合則充塞流行於天地之間彼
高明上浮者為天博厚下凝者為地而禮樂則
峻極乎天而蟠委乎地焉天地之氣分而為陰
陽造化之迹妙而為鬼神而禮樂則行乎陰陽
而通乎鬼神焉以至高遠者難於窮極深厚者
難於測度而禮樂則於天道星辰之高遠皆有
所窮極地道河海之深厚皆有所測度焉如此
punctuated:
〔同考試官學正陳批：塲中作者多以禮樂分配造化為說，間有知者，又踈於分截。惟此作能以成功所合為主，一破便合題意，且文理俱到，宜置高選。〕
〔考試官教授劉批：發明經旨，透徹無餘。〕
〔考試官教授鄭批：說出禮樂之功用有合於造化，文理明白，可取。〕
論禮樂之成功，充塞妙運於兩間，故聖人必昭揭其名以示夫人也。盖聖人禮樂之功用，充塞流行於天地間者也。苟不昭揭以示人，又何以顯名於天下也哉？《樂記》君子謂夫聖人之作樂，出於天地自然之和；制禮，出於天地自然之序。及其成功之所合，則充塞流行於天地之間。彼高明上浮者為天，博厚下凝者為地，而禮樂則峻極乎天而蟠委乎地焉。天地之氣分而為陰陽，造化之迹妙而為鬼神，而禮樂則行乎陰陽而通乎鬼神焉。以至高遠者難於窮極，深厚者難於測度，而禮樂則於天道星辰之高遠皆有所窮極，地道河海之深厚皆有所測度焉。如此，
translation_en:
[Comment by Associate Examiner and Subprefectural/Departmental Director of Studies (xuezheng) Chen: Most writers in the examination hall explained the passage by matching rites and music separately with the creative forces of nature; among the few who understood it, they were careless in dividing the sections. Only this essay takes the convergence of their perfected achievements as its main theme. From the very opening statement, it matches the meaning of the topic, and since both its style and reasoning are fully realized, it deserves to be placed in a high rank.]
[Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies (jiaoshou) Liu: It elucidates the purport of the Classic thoroughly and exhaustively.]
[Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zheng: It brings out how the functions of rites and music accord with the creative forces of nature; its style and reasoning are clear, making it worthy of selection.]

Discussing how the perfected achievements of rites and music fill and wondrously operate between heaven and earth, the sages therefore necessarily proclaimed their names brightly to show them to humankind. For the functions of the sages' rites and music are what fill and flow between heaven and earth. If they were not brightly proclaimed and shown to people, how then could their names be made manifest throughout the world? The superior man in the Record of Music (Yueji) meant that the sages' creation of music arises from the natural harmony of heaven and earth, and their institution of rites arises from the natural order of heaven and earth. When their perfected achievements converge, they fill and flow between heaven and earth. That which is lofty, bright, and floats above is heaven; that which is broad, thick, and congeals below is earth—and rites and music reach up to the heights of heaven and coil across the expanse of earth. The vital energy of heaven and earth divides to become yin and yang, and the traces of the creative forces operate wondrously to become ghosts and spirits—and rites and music move through yin and yang and communicate with ghosts and spirits. Even to the point where what is high and distant is difficult to exhaust to its limit, and what is deep and thick is difficult to fathom—yet rites and music exhaust all the height and distance of the heavenly way and the stars, and fathom all the depth and thickness of the earthly way and the rivers and seas. Thus, …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則禮樂之功用無顯不至無幽不格無高不届
無深不入而充塞天地矣是則樂之為樂已居
乎乾知太始之初而與大哉乾元同一資始之
德也禮之為禮已居乎坤作成物之位而與至
哉坤元同一資生之德也昭著不息者天之行
健所以為天而顯諸仁也昭著不動者地之載
物所以為地而藏諸用也惟其顯諸仁而藏諸
用是以一動一靜循環不已見於天地之間歲
功已成一陰一陽妙運不息著於六合之内生
===
化無窮焉聖人於此所以昭揭以示人而名之
曰禮樂吾見天下之人向未知有所謂禮樂也
今則洞然無不達焉禮樂之功用大矣論而坐
是則知天地乃禮樂運行之郛廓禮樂乃天地
自然之和序其全體呈露禮樂之本也妙用顯
行禮樂之用也苟非聖人心識乎情文之妙身
任乎制作之重則禮樂何自而興行哉故曰大
人舉禮樂則天地將為昭焉
百日之蜡一日之澤非爾所知也張而不
punctuated:
則禮樂之功用，無顯不至，無幽不格，無高不届，無深不入，而充塞天地矣。是則樂之為樂，已居乎乾知太始之初，而與大哉乾元同一資始之德也；禮之為禮，已居乎坤作成物之位，而與至哉坤元同一資生之德也。昭著不息者，天之行健，所以為天而顯諸仁也；昭著不動者，地之載物，所以為地而藏諸用也。惟其顯諸仁而藏諸用，是以一動一靜，循環不已，見於天地之間，歲功已成；一陰一陽，妙運不息，著於六合之内，生化無窮焉。聖人於此，所以昭揭以示人，而名之曰禮樂。吾見天下之人，向未知有所謂禮樂也，今則洞然無不達焉。禮樂之功用大矣！論而坐是，則知天地乃禮樂運行之郛廓，禮樂乃天地自然之和序。其全體呈露，禮樂之本也；妙用顯行，禮樂之用也。苟非聖人心識乎情文之妙，身任乎制作之重，則禮樂何自而興行哉？故曰：「大人舉禮樂，則天地將為昭焉。」
「百日之蜡，一日之澤，非爾所知也。張而不
translation_en:
…then in the efficacy and function of rites and music, there is nothing manifest that they do not reach, nothing obscure that they do not penetrate, nothing high that they do not attain, and nothing deep that they do not enter, filling heaven and earth. Thus, music as music already resides in the beginning where the Creative (Qian) knows the great inception, sharing the same virtue of initiating all things as the great Primal Creative (Qian yuan); rites as rites already reside in the position where the Receptive (Kun) brings things to completion, sharing the same virtue of giving birth to all things as the完美 Primal Receptive (Kun yuan). That which is luminously manifest and ceaseless is the vigorous motion of heaven, whereby it is heaven and manifests itself in benevolence; that which is luminously manifest and unmoving is the bearing of things by earth, whereby it is earth and conceals its functions. Because it manifests itself in benevolence and conceals its functions, one movement and one stillness alternate in an endless cycle, appearing between heaven and earth so that the work of the year is accomplished; one yin and one yang operate wondrously without cease, becoming manifest within the six directions so that generation and transformation are无穷. Because of this, the sages clearly held them up to show to humanity and named them "rites and music." I see that the people of the world, who previously did not know of what are called rites and music, now thoroughly understand them without exception. Great indeed are the efficacy and function of rites and music! Discussing it up to this point [? 坐是, perhaps a graphic error for 至是], one knows that heaven and earth are the outer enclosure within which rites and music operate, and rites and music are the natural harmony and order of heaven and earth. Their entire substance revealed is the foundation of rites and music; their wondrous function manifestly operating is the application of rites and music. Were it not that the sages understood in their minds the subtleties of emotional disposition and cultural form, and personally took upon themselves the weighty responsibility of creating and instituting them, how then could rites and music arise and prevail? Therefore it is said: "When the great man institutes rites and music, heaven and earth will become brightly manifest because of them."

"The zha festival after a hundred days of labor gives a single day of beneficence; this is not something you understand. To keep the bowstring taut and never…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
弛文武弗能也
黄瑜
同考試官學正陳批此題本平易作者紛紛
臆說惟此篇前後能以勞逸之義立意况措辭蒼古宜
冠本經
考試官教授劉批詞達理備可見學識
考試官教授鄭批文簡而理明宜表而出之
聖人言久勞暫逸之恩非賢者所能識其義必
喻以久勞不息之政雖聖王不能致其治盖蜡
===
祭所以報神澤民也聖人因賢者未知其義得
不取喻以明之哉昔子貢觀於蜡未知其樂聖
人故告之曰古之君子使之必報之蜡之為祭
所以報神之有功於田而因以勞農之致力於
田者也彼百日勞苦而有此蜡農民服終嵗畎
畝之勤今僅使之為一日飲酒之歡是乃人君
之恩澤斯舉也幽足以報神明足以澤乎民其
其義之大豈女所能知乎方其勞之之初猶弓
之張而有為也及其息之之後猶弓之弛而無
punctuated:
弛，文武弗能也。
黄瑜
同考試官學正陳批：此題本平易，作者紛紛臆說。惟此篇前後能以勞逸之義立意，况措辭蒼古，宜冠本經。
考試官教授劉批：詞達理備，可見學識。
考試官教授鄭批：文簡而理明，宜表而出之。
聖人言久勞暫逸之恩，非賢者所能識其義，必喻以久勞不息之政，雖聖王不能致其治。盖蜡祭所以報神澤民也，聖人因賢者未知其義，得不取喻以明之哉？昔子貢觀於蜡，未知其樂，聖人故告之曰：古之君子，使之必報之。蜡之為祭，所以報神之有功於田，而因以勞農之致力於田者也。彼百日勞苦而有此蜡，農民服終嵗畎畝之勤，今僅使之為一日飲酒之歡，是乃人君之恩澤。斯舉也，幽足以報神，明足以澤乎民，其其義之大，豈女所能知乎？方其勞之之初，猶弓之張而有為也；及其息之之後，猶弓之弛而無…
translation_en:
… unstrung, even Kings Wen and Wu could not do it.”

Huang Yu 黃瑜

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen 陳 comments: This topic is inherently plain and straightforward, yet candidates offered all sorts of arbitrary conjectures. Only this essay establishes its main theme throughout on the meaning of toil and rest; moreover, its diction is vigorous and archaic, so it deserves to head the candidates in this Classic.

Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉 comments: The words are expressive and the principles complete; one can see his learning and insight.

Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zheng 鄭 comments: The style is concise and the reasoning clear; it ought to be singled out for publication.

The Sage speaks of the grace of brief rest after long toil, the meaning of which a worthy cannot fathom, and so he must illustrate it with the metaphor that governance of unceasing toil is something by which even sage kings could not achieve order. For the year-end Zha 蜡 sacrifice is the means of repaying the spirits and bestowing favor upon the people. Since the worthy did not yet understand its meaning, how could the Sage not draw an analogy to clarify it?

Of old, when Zigong 子貢 observed the Zha festival, he did not understand the joy in it, and so the Sage told him: When the noble men of antiquity employed things, they invariably repaid them. As a sacrifice, the Zha is the means to repay the spirits that have performed meritorious service in the fields, and thereby to reward the farmers who have exerted their strength in the fields. Through the toil and hardship of a hundred days there comes this Zha sacrifice: the farmers submit to a full year of diligence in the furrows and fields, and now they are merely granted the joy of a single day of drinking wine—this is the gracious bounty of the ruler of men. By this act, in the unseen realm it suffices to repay the spirits, and in the visible realm it suffices to bestow favor upon the people. So great is its [its] meaning—how could it be something that you are able to understand?

At the beginning, when they are set to toil, it is like a bow that is strung and put to action; afterward, when they are given rest, it is like a bow that is unstrung and without …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
作也使或乆張而不弛則力必絶猶民乆勞而
不息則力必憊弓必有時而張有時而弛可也
民必有時而勞有時而息可也使民常勞而不
息則民將不堪雖曰聖如文武亦不能為治也
吁此先王之於民所以使之雖勞而不怨也歟
大抵萬物之所以成者神有以相功於其幽民
有以致力於其明神有功以相其幽則報之民
有力以致其明則勞之相功致力者義也報之
勞之者仁也先王一舉事仁義並行而不悖也
===
如是夫
第貳場
論
君道稽古正學
黃珣
同考試官學正陳批事有考據文亦豐贍其始
終以正心立說盖有識之士也宜冠多士
考試官教授劉批出人意表可嘉
考試官教授鄭批詞氣渾厚真為佳作
punctuated:
作也。使或乆張而不弛，則力必絶；猶民乆勞而不息，則力必憊。弓必有時而張，有時而弛，可也；民必有時而勞，有時而息，可也。使民常勞而不息，則民將不堪，雖曰聖如文、武，亦不能為治也。吁！此先王之於民，所以使之雖勞而不怨也歟！大抵萬物之所以成者，神有以相功於其幽，民有以致力於其明。神有功以相其幽，則報之；民有力以致其明，則勞之。相功致力者，義也；報之勞之者，仁也。先王一舉事，仁義並行而不悖也如是夫！

第貳場
論
君道稽古正學
黃珣
同考試官學正陳批：事有考據，文亦豐贍。其始終以正心立說，盖有識之士也，宜冠多士。
考試官教授劉批：出人意表，可嘉。
考試官教授鄭批：詞氣渾厚，真為佳作。
translation_en:
…action. If perchance a bow is kept strung for a long time without being unstrung, its strength will surely snap; just so, if the people toil for a long time without resting, their strength will surely be exhausted. A bow must have a time to be strung and a time to be unstrung, and only then will it do; the people must have a time to toil and a time to rest, and only then will it do. If one makes the people toil constantly without resting, the people will not be able to bear it, and even sages like King Wen and King Wu would not be able to bring about good governance. Ah! Is this not how the former kings dealt with the people, so that even though they made them toil, the people did not resent it? In general, the reason all things are brought to completion is that the spirits assist with their achievements in the unseen realm, while the people exert their strength in the visible world. Because the spirits have achievements in assisting in the unseen realm, they are repaid; because the people have strength in exerting themselves in the visible world, they are comforted for their toil. Assisting with achievements and exerting strength are matters of righteousness; repaying them and comforting them for their toil are matters of benevolence. When the former kings undertook a single action, benevolence and righteousness operated together without contradiction—just like this!

Second Session
Discourse
"The Way of the Ruler: Examining Antiquity and Rectifying Learning"
Huang Xun 黃珣
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Chen 陳: The historical references are well-grounded, and the prose is also rich and ample. From beginning to end, he establishes his argument on rectifying the mind; he is indeed a scholar of insight and ought to be placed at the head of the many scholars.
Comment by Examiner Professor Liu 劉: Surpasses expectations; commendable.
Comment by Examiner Professor Zheng 鄭: The diction and tone are substantial and deep; truly a fine piece of work.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
論曰人君欲成盛德大業而致雍熈泰和
之治其道何先曰稽古正學而已盖明君
以務學為急聖學以正心為要苟不稽古
先聖王之正學則心術不明心志不定其
何以明善惡之歸辨忠邪之分理天下之
務曉然趨道之正而成天下之治哉請申
程子君道稽古正學之㫖人君以一身而
統天下之大以一心而理萬幾之繁善惡
沓至乎前是非未易明也忠邪並進於世
===
誠偽未易辨也况出入起居紛紜酬酢聲
色貨利皆戕心之斧斤觀逸遊田皆害心
之蟊賊苟不稽古正學以為吾心之權衡
繩墨則義理不明多聽而易惑心志不定
守善而或移矣夫權衡設而不可欺以輕
重者以其平也繩墨設而不可欺以曲直
者以其直也學術明而不可惑以邪忒者
以其正也人君稽古正學則知聖人之訓
為必當從先王之治為必可法心如懸鑑
punctuated:
論曰：人君欲成盛德大業，而致雍熈泰和之治，其道何先？曰：稽古正學而已。盖明君以務學為急，聖學以正心為要。苟不稽古先聖王之正學，則心術不明，心志不定，其何以明善惡之歸，辨忠邪之分，理天下之務，曉然趨道之正，而成天下之治哉？請申程子「君道稽古正學」之㫖。

人君以一身而統天下之大，以一心而理萬幾之繁。善惡沓至乎前，是非未易明也；忠邪並進於世，誠偽未易辨也。况出入起居，紛紜酬酢，聲色貨利，皆戕心之斧斤；觀逸遊田，皆害心之蟊賊。苟不稽古正學，以為吾心之權衡繩墨，則義理不明，多聽而易惑；心志不定，守善而或移矣。夫權衡設而不可欺以輕重者，以其平也；繩墨設而不可欺以曲直者，以其直也；學術明而不可惑以邪忒者，以其正也。人君稽古正學，則知聖人之訓為必當從，先王之治為必可法，心如懸鑑…
translation_en:
The discourse reads: If a ruler wishes to achieve flourishing virtue and great enterprises, and to bring about an era of harmonious and tranquil governance, what should take precedence in his Way? It is simply to examine antiquity and rectify learning. Indeed, an enlightened ruler regards devotion to learning as his urgent task, and sagely learning takes rectifying the mind as its essential point. If he does not examine antiquity for the orthodox learning of the former sage-kings, then the workings of his mind will not be clear and his will and intentions will not be settled. How then could he clarify the distinction between good and evil, discern the boundary between loyalty and wickedness, manage the affairs of the realm, clearly pursue the orthodoxy of the Way, and accomplish the governance of the world? Allow me to elaborate upon the purport of Master Cheng's dictum: "The Way of the ruler lies in examining antiquity and rectifying learning."

The ruler, with his single person, governs the vastness of the realm, and with his single mind, manages the complexity of a myriad affairs. Good and evil crowd before him, so right and wrong are not easily clarified; the loyal and the wicked advance together in the world, so sincerity and falsehood are not easily distinguished. Moreover, in his goings-out and comings-in, his daily life, and his manifold social dealings, sensual pleasures, wealth, and profit are all axes that chop away at the mind; sightseeing, idleness, excursions, and hunting are all pests that harm the mind. If he does not examine antiquity and rectify learning to serve as the steelyard and marking-line for his own mind, then moral principles will be unclear, so that hearing many things he will be easily deluded; his will and intentions will be unsettled, so that even while holding to goodness he may sometimes be swayed. Now, when a steelyard is set up, one cannot be deceived as to light and heavy, because it is level; when a marking-line is set up, one cannot be deceived as to crooked and straight, because it is straight; when scholarship is clarified, one cannot be deluded by perverse errors, because it is orthodox. When the ruler examines antiquity and rectifies learning, he knows that the teachings of the sages must certainly be followed and that the governance of the former kings must certainly be taken as a model; his mind will be like a suspended mirror…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之明志如止水之定權衡在吾胷中繩墨
在吾度內而天下萬事萬物無不可理者
矣夫古之正學何學也堯舜湯禹文武周
孔相傳之心學也非黃老刑名術數異端
之學也其要在一中而已堯之授舜則曰
允執厥中舜之授禹則曰精一執中湯之
建中于民文王之緝熈敬止武王之建其
有極周公之思兼三王孔子之祖述憲章
皆此中也其弘綱奥旨見於易詩書禮春
===
秋之文其大經大法根於性命道德仁義
之實堯舜禹湯文武之盡君道而治功卓
乎不可及者以有是相傳之正學也若周
成王之學有緝熈于光明商高宗之學于
古訓於正學亦庶幾焉漢唐宋之君非不
盡君道而治化不古若者以不能稽古正
學也雖唐太宗有以古為鑑之言宋高宗
喜說命師古之語於正學亦未聞焉人君
稽古正學豈徒窺簡牘之陳言務口耳之
punctuated: 之明，志如止水之定，權衡在吾胷中，繩墨在吾度內，而天下萬事萬物無不可理者矣。夫古之正學，何學也？堯、舜、湯、禹、文、武、周、孔相傳之心學也，非黃、老、刑名、術數、異端之學也。其要在一「中」而已。堯之授舜，則曰「允執厥中」；舜之授禹，則曰「精一執中」；湯之「建中于民」，文王之「緝熈敬止」，武王之「建其有極」，周公之「思兼三王」，孔子之「祖述憲章」，皆此中也。其弘綱奥旨，見於《易》、《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《春秋》之文；其大經大法，根於性命、道德、仁義之實。堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之盡君道而治功卓乎不可及者，以有是相傳之正學也。若周成王之「學有緝熈于光明」，商高宗之「學于古訓」，於正學亦庶幾焉。漢、唐、宋之君，非不盡君道，而治化不古若者，以不能稽古正學也。雖唐太宗有「以古為鑑」之言，宋高宗喜《說命》「師古」之語，於正學亦未聞焉。人君稽古正學，豈徒窺簡牘之陳言，務口耳之
translation_en: …of a suspended mirror, and his will as steady as still water. With the steelyard in his breast and the marking-line within his measure, there will be nothing among all the myriad affairs and myriad things under heaven that cannot be put in order. Now, what learning is the orthodox learning of antiquity? It is the learning of the mind-and-heart transmitted successively by Yao, Shun, Tang, Yu, King Wen, King Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius—not the heterodox learning of Huang-Lao, penal-nominalism (xingming), or numerology and divination (shushu). Its essential point lies simply in a single word: "equilibrium" (zhong). When Yao transmitted it to Shun, he said, "Sincerely hold fast the mean"; when Shun transmitted it to Yu, he said, "Be discerning and single-minded, holding fast the mean." Tang's "establishing the mean among the people," King Wen's "continuing and brightening reverent resting," King Wu's "establishing his supreme standard," the Duke of Zhou's "thinking to combine the Three Kings," and Confucius's "transmitting the doctrines of antiquity and modeling himself on the charters" are all this same equilibrium. Its grand principles and profound purport are seen in the texts of the Changes, the Odes, the Documents, the Rites, and the Spring and Autumn Annals; its great norms and great laws are rooted in the realities of human nature and Heaven's mandate, the Way and its virtue, and benevolence and righteousness. That Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu fulfilled the Way of the ruler and achieved governance so lofty as to be unattainable by others was because they possessed this successively transmitted orthodox learning. Rulers such as King Cheng of Zhou, who "in his learning had continuous brightness unto illumination," and Gaozong of Shang, who "learned from the ancient precepts," also came close to orthodox learning. That the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties—though it was not that they failed to fulfill the Way of the ruler—achieved transformative governance inferior to that of antiquity was because they were unable to examine antiquity and pursue orthodox learning. Even though Emperor Taizong of Tang spoke of "taking antiquity as a mirror," and Emperor Gaozong of Song delighted in the words on "taking antiquity as a teacher" in the "Charge to Yue" (Yue ming), when it came to orthodox learning, they had heard nothing of it. When a ruler examines antiquity and pursues orthodox learning, how could he merely peer at stale words on bamboo slips and wooden tablets, or occupy himself with the…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
粗跡哉要必格物致知以明其理誠意正
心以實其事從容燕閒訓誦箴諫皆聞正
論左右前後朝夕承弼莫匪正人必考古
聖傳心之要典而不遷於流俗因循之論
必求大中至正之所在而不牽於後世駁
雜之政則正學明而吾之心正矣吾心既
正則用人之際必如古聖王之任賢勿貳
去邪勿疑而善惡之歸忠邪之辨明矣心
正則身正而起居之際必如古聖王之允
===
迪厥德慎乃有位而聲色貨利觀逸遊田
之念息矣由是而正朝廷正百官正萬民
而遠近莫不一於正其治化之盛亦可比
隆唐虞三代之黎民於變萬邦咸寧矣大
哉古聖王之正學乎其為君道之標準乎
堯舜禹湯文武遠矣洪惟我
朝
列聖相承皆以正學化成天下而
頒降性理大全五倫書皆首揭是言於君道
punctuated: 粗跡哉？要必格物致知以明其理，誠意正心以實其事。從容燕閒，訓誦箴諫，皆聞正論；左右前後，朝夕承弼，莫匪正人。必考古聖傳心之要典，而不遷於流俗因循之論；必求大中至正之所在，而不牽於後世駁雜之政。則正學明而吾之心正矣。吾心既正，則用人之際，必如古聖王之任賢勿貳、去邪勿疑，而善惡之歸、忠邪之辨明矣。心正則身正，而起居之際，必如古聖王之允迪厥德、慎乃有位，而聲色貨利、觀逸遊田之念息矣。由是而正朝廷，正百官，正萬民，而遠近莫不一於正。其治化之盛，亦可比隆唐、虞、三代之「黎民於變」、「萬邦咸寧」矣。大哉，古聖王之正學乎！其為君道之標準乎！堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武遠矣，洪惟我朝列聖相承，皆以正學化成天下，而頒降《性理大全》、《五倫書》，皆首揭是言於《君道》…
translation_en: …crude traces? Instead, he must investigate things and extend knowledge to clarify their principles, and make his intentions sincere and rectify his mind to substantiate his affairs. In moments of leisurely repose, through instruction, recitation, admonition, and remonstrance, all that he hears will be orthodox discourse; those around him—to the left and right, in front and behind—who attend and assist him morning and evening, will be none other than upright men. He must examine the essential canons by which the ancient sages transmitted the Way of the mind, without being swayed by the routine arguments of vulgar custom; he must seek out where supreme impartiality and ultimate rectitude reside, without being dragged down by the雜 (mixed and impure) governance of later ages. Then orthodox learning will be illuminated, and one's own mind will be rectified. Once one's mind is rectified, in employing men one will certainly act like the ancient sage-kings, who entrusted the worthy without duplicity and cast out the wicked without hesitation; thus the歸 (distinction) between good and evil and the discernment between loyalty and treachery will be clear. When the mind is rectified, the person is rectified, and in one's daily conduct and movements one will certainly act like the ancient sage-kings, who sincerely pursued their virtue and were cautious in holding their positions; thus thoughts of sensual pleasures and material profit, of sightseeing, idleness, and hunting excursions, will cease. From this, one rectifies the court, rectifies the hundred officials, and rectifies the myriad people, so that far and near there is none who is not unified in rectitude. The flourishing of such transformative governance can rival the grandeur of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, when "the black-haired people were transformed" and "the myriad states were all at peace." Great indeed is the orthodox learning of the ancient sage-kings! Is it not the standard for the Way of the ruler? Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu are distant now. Yet I humbly reflect upon how the successive sacred emperors of our Dynasty have inherited the throne one after another, all transforming and perfecting the realm through orthodox learning; and in promulgating the Great Compendium of Nature and Principle (Xingli daquan) and the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu), both works place these very words at the head of their chapters on "The Way of the Ruler"…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
篇大哉
皇心乎其所以垂裕
聖子神孫曷有已乎今
聖天子日御經筵集儒臣講明二帝三王之道
於所謂正學知之明信之篤行之力愚何
々幸親逢唐虞三代之盛治於
今日
表
擬進
===
大明一統志表
王鑑之
同考試官訓導張批駢儷可取
考試官教授劉批表佳
考試官教授鄭批表得體
伏以
鳌立坤維肇億萬年之土宇
龍飛淮甸開大一統之山河下陋四野遠超三
代宜有傳於永世可無紀於當時夙廑
punctuated:
篇。大哉皇心乎！其所以垂裕聖子神孫，曷有已乎！今聖天子日御經筵，集儒臣講明二帝三王之道，於所謂正學，知之明，信之篤，行之力。愚何々幸，親逢唐虞三代之盛治於今日！

表

擬進《大明一統志》表

王鑑之

同考試官訓導張批：駢儷可取。
考試官教授劉批：表佳。
考試官教授鄭批：表得體。

伏以：鳌立坤維，肇億萬年之土宇；龍飛淮甸，開大一統之山河。下陋四野，遠超三代。宜有傳於永世，可無紀於當時？夙廑
translation_en:
… section. Great indeed is the August Mind! How could the way in which it bequeaths abundance to sacred sons and divine grandsons ever come to an end? Now the Sacred Son of Heaven daily attends the Classics Colloquium, gathering Confucian officials to expound and clarify the Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. Regarding what is called orthodox learning, he knows it clearly, believes in it篤ly, and practices it vigorously. How fortunate [?] am I, in my simplicity, to personally witness the flourishing governance of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties today!

Memorial (Biao)

Draft Memorial Presenting the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi)

Wang Jianzhi 王鑑之

Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: A fine memorial.

Your servant humbly observes: Setting the great sea-turtle pillars to support the corners of the earth, our dynasty founded a territory for hundreds of millions of years; as the dragon took flight from the Huai region, it opened up the mountains and rivers of a grand unification. Looking down upon the four wildernesses as humble, it far surpasses the Three Dynasties. Since this ought to be transmitted to eternal generations, how could it go unrecorded in the present time? Long ago, it engaged the solicitous concern …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖祖之留心志将垂遠既
命儒臣而效力績未究成事竟集茲時應有
待恭惟
〇〇〇〇
聰明睿智
中正齊莊作之君作之師為群生之共主繼
其志述其事纘
列聖之洪圖混車書文軌於八埏来玉帛衣冠
於萬國道已至而猶以為未至德愈崇而
===
猶以為未崇總攬
乾綱勤政常臨於日昃緝熈
聖學觀書每至於夜分披禹貢閱職方備見
前朝之疆域渙
綸音啓
宸斷聿新
盛代之典章遂簡及於庸愚俾職司於脩纂
上以成
祖宗欲為之志下以垂子孫不拔之基
punctuated: 聖祖之留心，志将垂遠；既命儒臣而效力，績未究成。事竟集茲，時應有待。恭惟〇〇〇〇，聰明睿智，中正齊莊。作之君、作之師，為群生之共主；繼其志、述其事，纘列聖之洪圖。混車書文軌於八埏，来玉帛衣冠於萬國。道已至而猶以為未至，德愈崇而猶以為未崇。總攬乾綱，勤政常臨於日昃；緝熈聖學，觀書每至於夜分。披《禹貢》、閱《職方》，備見前朝之疆域；渙綸音、啓宸斷，聿新盛代之典章。遂簡及於庸愚，俾職司於脩纂。上以成祖宗欲為之志，下以垂子孫不拔之基。
translation_en: … occupied the mind of the Sacred Ancestor, whose ambition was to hand a legacy down to distant ages; yet although he commanded Confucian officials to exert their efforts, the achievement was not brought to full completion. That the enterprise is finally accomplished now shows that the time had to be awaited. Reverently we reflect that [His Majesty the Emperor], intelligent, perspicacious, and wise, is central, upright, reverent, and dignified. Made their ruler and made their teacher, he is the common lord of all living beings; continuing their aspirations and carrying forward their enterprises, he succeeds to the grand design of the Successive Sages. He unifies cart-axle gauges and written characters across the eight farthest bounds, and draws jade, silk, and ceremonial attire from a myriad states. Though the Way has already reached its utmost, he still regards it as not yet having reached the utmost; though his virtue grows ever more lofty, he still regards it as not yet lofty enough. Holding firm the sovereign reins of Heaven, he is diligent in governance, regularly attending to affairs until the sun declines; continuing and illuminating the sacred learning, he reads books every night until midnight. Unrolling the Tribute of Yu (Yugong) and perusing the職方 Direction of the Regions (Zhifang), he thoroughly surveyed the territories of former dynasties; issuing silken proclamations and exercising his imperial judgment, he thereupon renewed the institutions and records of a flourishing age. Thus his selection reached even to us, the mediocre and foolish, charging us with the official duty of compilation—above, to fulfill the aspirations that the Imperial Ancestors wished to accomplish, and below, to bequeath an unshakable foundation to descendants. …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
渙汗自
天震驚無地庸敬偕於寮寀特致謹於編摩文
物衣冠表
京畿為四方之極山川形勝列方嶽為諸郡
之先曰館榭曰亭臺雖微必錄曰人情曰
土俗無遠不書列其目必揭其綱詳乎今
不略乎古彼于闐占城之境悉在包荒若
高麗百濟之區咸歸統載允陋昔人之九
域卓為
===
今代之全書誠
聖朝萬萬世無疆之基業也臣等才慚襪線學
愧榛蕪鋪張曠古之規模詞非班馬揚厲
無前之功績文乏歐蘇惟願
帝德日新祝
一人之有慶
皇圖固鞏祈
萬壽之無疆臣等無任瞻
天仰
punctuated: 渙汗自天，震驚無地。庸敬偕於寮寀，特致謹於編摩。文物衣冠，表京畿為四方之極；山川形勝，列方嶽為諸郡之先。曰館榭、曰亭臺，雖微必錄；曰人情、曰土俗，無遠不書。列其目必揭其綱，詳乎今不略乎古。彼于闐、占城之境，悉在包荒；若高麗、百濟之區，咸歸統載。允陋昔人之《九域》，卓為今代之全書，誠聖朝萬萬世無疆之基業也。臣等才慚襪線，學愧榛蕪，鋪張曠古之規模，詞非班、馬；揚厲無前之功績，文乏歐、蘇。惟願帝德日新，祝一人之有慶；皇圖固鞏，祈萬壽之無疆。臣等無任瞻天仰
translation_en: When the imperial edict poured forth from Heaven, we were so awestruck that we had nowhere to stand. We have therefore reverently joined with our colleagues and devoted special care to the compilation and editing. In culture, institutions, and ceremonial attire, we have set forth the Metropolitan Area as the standard for the four quarters; in mountains, rivers, and strategic topography, we have ranked the Sacred Peaks ahead of the various commanderies. Whether lodges and terraces or pavilions and towers, even the smallest are recorded without fail; whether human sentiments or local customs, even the most distant are written down without omission. In listing the subheadings we never fail to set forth the main principles, and in detailing the present we do not neglect the past. Those territories of Khotan (Yutian) and Champa (Zhancheng) are all encompassed within Your Majesty's vast embrace; regions such as Korea (Gaoli) and Paekche (Baiji) are all brought into this unified record. Truly it makes the Nine Regions (Jiuyu) of men of the past seem narrow and stands preeminent as the comprehensive work of the present dynasty; it is indeed the boundless foundation of our Sacred Dynasty for myriad generations to come. Your servants are ashamed that our talents are as paltry as threads pulled from a sock and that our learning is as overgrown as brambles and weeds. To display this scale unprecedented since antiquity, our words are not those of Ban Gu and Sima Qian; to extol these achievements without parallel before, our prose lacks the skill of Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi. We only wish that the Imperial Virtue be daily renewed, praying for blessings upon the One Man; and that the August Domain be firmly consolidated, praying for Your Majesty's boundless longevity. Your servants are beyond measure in gazing toward Heaven and looking up to…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
聖激切屏營之至謹以纂脩
大明一統志若干卷隨表上
進以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
程愈
同考試官訓導張批此卷前場七篇俱純五
===
策皆善條答而此尤詳悉不宜在魁選
考試官教授劉批策得事實
考試官教授鄭批不為問目所窘可嘉可嘉
上天佑民必以綏猷之責付之君人君奉
天必以立極之訓示之民盖有一代之隆
興必有一代之制作遠而堯舜湯武之典
謨訓誥所以道民為善固此道也近而我
朝
一祖二宗之大誥三書所以道民為善亦此道
punctuated:
聖，激切屏營之至。謹以纂脩《大明一統志》若干卷，隨表上進以聞。

第叁場
策
第一問
程愈
同考試官訓導張批：此卷前場七篇俱純，五策皆善條答，而此尤詳悉，不宜在魁選？
考試官教授劉批：策得事實。
考試官教授鄭批：不為問目所窘，可嘉，可嘉。

上天佑民，必以綏猷之責付之君；人君奉天，必以立極之訓示之民。盖有一代之隆興，必有一代之制作。遠而堯、舜、湯、武之典、謨、訓、誥，所以道民為善，固此道也；近而我朝一祖二宗之《大誥》三書，所以道民為善，亦此道
translation_en:
… the Sacred One, in utmost trepidation and awe. Your servants reverently submit the compiled Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Great Ming (Da Ming yitong zhi) in a certain number of juan along with this memorial for His Majesty's information.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Cheng Yu 程愈

Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: The policy essay grasps the factual realities.
Examiner and Instructor Zheng comments: Not constrained by the sub-questions—commendable, commendable!

When High Heaven blesses the people, it invariably entrusts the responsibility of securing them in the Way to the ruler; when the ruler serves Heaven, he invariably displays the teachings of establishing the standard of perfection to the people. For whenever there is the flourishing rise of an era, there must be the institutions and creations of that era. In distant antiquity, the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, by which they guided the people to do good, were indeed this Way; in recent times, the Grand Pronouncements (Da gao) and the three books of the One Founder and Two Ancestors [the Hongwu, Yongle, and Xuanzong emperors] of our dynasty, by which they guided the people to do good, are also this Way…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
也又何彼此之間哉書曰惟皇上帝降衷
于下民若有恒性克綏厥猷惟后是言人
性本善而不能不壞於人欲所以脩道立
教使之各安其道以復於善則頼乎君也
稽之於古若堯舜之勞来匡直教以人倫
成湯之肇脩人紀武王之重民五教所以
道民於善而充盡綏猷之責者非有他術
也亦惟因其所固有者而道之耳是以當
時人人士行比屋可封非後世所能及也
===
迨至漢唐宋其間願治之君非不欲道民
為善然其所以道之之術則與此異如宋
太宗親書孝經於碑陰高宗親書孟子於
屏障不過為文具美觀而已烏能道民於
善哉洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝條成大誥三編昭示天下褒善之
言藹乎春温誠有以感發人之善心矣觀
其申明五常知報獲福之條與夫正婚姻
punctuated: 也，又何彼此之間哉？《書》曰：「惟皇上帝，降衷于下民，若有恒性，克綏厥猷惟后。」是言人性本善，而不能不壞於人欲，所以脩道立教，使之各安其道以復於善，則頼乎君也。稽之於古，若堯、舜之勞来匡直、教以人倫，成湯之肇脩人紀，武王之重民五教，所以道民於善而充盡綏猷之責者，非有他術也，亦惟因其所固有者而道之耳。是以當時人人士行，比屋可封，非後世所能及也。迨至漢、唐、宋，其間願治之君，非不欲道民為善，然其所以道之之術則與此異。如宋太宗親書《孝經》於碑陰，高宗親書《孟子》於屏障，不過為文具美觀而已，烏能道民於善哉！洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝，條成《大誥》三編，昭示天下。褒善之言，藹乎春温，誠有以感發人之善心矣。觀其申明五常、知報獲福之條，與夫正婚姻、
translation_en: … What gap, then, could there be between the one and the other? The Classic of History (Shu) says: "Great Heaven has conferred its moral sense upon the people below; to comply with their constant nature and enable them to tranquilize their way—that belongs to the sovereign alone." This means that although human nature is originally good, it cannot help being corrupted by human desires; therefore, cultivating the Way and establishing instruction so that everyone may rest securely in their proper path and return to goodness depends entirely upon the ruler. Examining antiquity, we find that when Yao and Shun encouraged their coming, straightened the crooked, and taught the human relationships; when Tang the Successful first cultivated the human bonds; and when King Wu attached prime importance to the five teachings among the people—that whereby they guided the people toward goodness and fully discharged the responsibility of tranquilizing their way involved no other artifice, but merely followed what the people inherently possessed and guided them accordingly. For this reason, in those times everyone had the conduct of a gentleman, and house after house was worthy of enfeoffment—something later ages could never match. Coming down to the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, rulers during those eras who desired good governance did not lack the wish to guide the people toward goodness, yet the methods by which they guided them differed from this. For instance, Emperor Taizong of the Song personally transcribed the Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing) on the reverse of stone steles, and Emperor Gaozong personally transcribed the Mencius (Mengzi) onto screens. These were nothing more than ornamental formalities for fine appearance—how could they truly guide the people toward goodness? Let us reverently reflect upon how our dynasty's Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi), compiled the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) in detailed articles and proclaimed them to all under Heaven. His words praising goodness were as genial as the warmth of spring, truly capable of stirring and awakening the good hearts of men. title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
行鄉飲之數則所以道民之要亦不出乎
民生日用彛倫之外其克綏厥猷豈不與
堯舜湯武同一揆歟
太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒慮民之逸居而無教也
著為善陰隲孝順事實二書拳拳勸人為
善行孝而申之以報應之理其間所載如
鄧禹之不殺而子孫繼封公侯作配宫闈
韓琦之德政而子孫繼登台鼎光榮累世
蕭固孝謹而子芝仕至尚書郎黄香行孝
===
而子瓊仕為僕射是為善行孝之獲報也
豈不與大誥為善獲報之效同條而共貫
歟
宣宗章皇帝嗣大歷服慮民之忽於倫理也著
五倫一書備人倫之道而各舉其善行其
間所載若洪皓盡忠而三子竝中詞科趙
善應純孝而一子卒登相位是其盡臣子
之善行而獲報也又豈不與為善孝順二
書一軌而合轍歟
punctuated: 行鄉飲之數，則所以道民之要，亦不出乎民生日用彛倫之外。其克綏厥猷，豈不與堯、舜、湯、武同一揆歟？太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒，慮民之逸居而無教也，著《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書，拳拳勸人為善行孝，而申之以報應之理。其間所載，如鄧禹之不殺，而子孫繼封公侯，作配宫闈；韓琦之德政，而子孫繼登台鼎，光榮累世；蕭固孝謹，而子芝仕至尚書郎；黄香行孝，而子瓊仕為僕射，是為善行孝之獲報也。豈不與《大誥》為善獲報之效同條而共貫歟？宣宗章皇帝嗣大歷服，慮民之忽於倫理也，著《五倫》一書，備人倫之道，而各舉其善行。其間所載，若洪皓盡忠，而三子竝中詞科；趙善應純孝，而一子卒登相位，是其盡臣子之善行而獲報也。又豈不與《為善》、《孝順》二書一軌而合轍歟？
translation_en:
… and the regulations for conducting the District Symposium, the essentials by which he guided the people likewise did not go beyond the invariant human relationships of the people’s daily lives. In being able to tranquilize their moral course, was his way not identical to that of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu?

Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor [the Yongle Emperor], succeeded to the great patrimony. Concerned lest the people dwell in idleness without instruction, he composed two books, Unseen Rewards for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Exemplars of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi), earnestly exhorting people to do good and practice filial piety while expounding the principle of moral retribution. Among the accounts recorded therein: because Deng Yu 鄧禹 refrained from killing, his descendants were successively enfeoffed as dukes and marquises and became consorts in the imperial palace; because of Han Qi’s 韓琦 virtuous governance, his descendants successively ascended to the highest ministerial posts, bringing glory for generations; because Xiao Gu 蕭固 was filial and reverent, his son Xiao Zhi 芝 rose in office to become a Vice Director in the Imperial Secretariat (shangshu lang); and because Huang Xiang 黄香 practiced filial piety, his son Huang Qiong 瓊 served in office as a Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs (puye). Such are the rewards obtained for doing good and practicing filial piety. Do these not share the same principles and form a single thread with the efficacy of doing good and obtaining rewards set forth in the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao)?

Emperor Zhang, the Sovereign Ancestor [the Xuande Emperor], inherited the great dynastic mandate. Concerned lest the people neglect moral principles, he composed the book on the Five Relationships (Wulun shu), setting forth in full the way of human relationships and citing exemplary deeds under each. Among the accounts recorded therein: because Hong Hao 洪皓 exhausted his loyalty, his three sons all passed the examination in literary composition (cike); and because Zhao Shanying 趙善應 was purely filial, one of his sons eventually ascended to the post of Grand Councilor. Such are the rewards obtained for fulfilling the virtuous conduct of a minister and a son. And do these not follow the exact same track as the two books on Doing Good and Filial Piety?

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
三聖四書掀揭宇宙
宸章奎翰照耀簡策皆道民於善而盡克綏
厥猷之責者也是以四海之內家傳人誦
風移俗易煕煕然相安相樂於雍煕之世
皞皞乎相親相愛於泰和之天於戲盛矣
然先聖後聖本同一心典謨四書實相表
裏大誥之君臣同遊即虞書之元首明哉
股肱良哉也陰隲書之為善獲報即謨訓
之惠迪吉作善降祥也孝順事實之虞舜
===
大孝非堯典克諧以孝之謂乎五倫書之
紀載善行非二典九族既睦五典克從之
意乎愚也生長於鳶飛魚躍之天涵泳於
鳳儀獸舞之治服膺
聖訓於茲有年謹掇拾所聞以對
第二問
吳嵩
同考試官教授劉批大小學策人多忽畧
此作綱目畢張文義縝密宜在選列
punctuated:
三聖四書，掀揭宇宙，宸章奎翰，照耀簡策，皆道民於善，而盡克綏厥猷之責者也。是以四海之內，家傳人誦，風移俗易，煕煕然相安相樂於雍煕之世，皞皞乎相親相愛於泰和之天。於戲，盛矣！然先聖後聖，本同一心；典謨四書，實相表裏。《大誥》之「君臣同遊」，即《虞書》之「元首明哉，股肱良哉」也；《陰隲書》之為善獲報，即謨訓之「惠迪吉」、「作善降祥」也；《孝順事實》之虞舜大孝，非《堯典》「克諧以孝」之謂乎？《五倫書》之紀載善行，非二典「九族既睦，五典克從」之意乎？愚也生長於鳶飛魚躍之天，涵泳於鳳儀獸舞之治，服膺聖訓，於茲有年，謹掇拾所聞以對。

第二問
吳嵩
同考試官、教授劉批：大小學策，人多忽畧。此作綱目畢張，文義縝密，宜在選列。
translation_en:
The four books of the Three Sage Emperors are held aloft throughout the universe, their imperial compositions and starry brush-work illuminating the bamboo slips and tablets. All of them guide the people toward goodness and fulfill the responsibility of "being able to tranquillize them in their moral ways." Therefore, within the four seas, every family transmits them and every person recites them; customs are transformed and habits changed, so that people live in peaceful and joyful harmony in an age of concord and prosperity, and in contented, affectionate amity beneath a heaven of supreme peace. Oh, how magnificent!

Yet the Former Sages and Latter Sages originally share a single mind, and the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents and these four imperial books truly form the outer and inner aspects of one another. "Ruler and ministers roaming together" in the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) is none other than "The head is intelligent, the limbs are good" in the Book of Yu; doing good and receiving recompense in the Book of Secret Virtue (Yinzhi shu) is none other than "Following the right way brings good fortune" and "On the doer of good, Heaven sends down all blessings" in the Counsels and Instructions; the great filial piety of Yu Shun in the True Records of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi)—is this not what the Canon of Yao calls "being able by filial piety to live in harmony"? And the recording of good deeds in the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu)—is this not the meaning of "The nine branches of the family having become harmonious" and "The five cardinal duties being universally observed" in the Two Canons?

Humble though I am, having grown up beneath a heaven where hawks fly and fishes leap, and having been steeped in an era of good governance where phoenixes come with stately儀 and beasts dance, I have cherished the Sacred Instructions in my heart for years now, and respectfully gather up what I have heard in order to reply.

Second Question
Wu Song
Comment by Associate Examiner and Prefectural Instructor Liu: Most candidates treat the policy question on the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and the Great Learning (Daxue) with neglect. In this piece, the overarching principles and specific details are fully laid out, and the phrasing and meaning are closely reasoned and meticulous; it deserves to be placed among the selected essays.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授劉批五策皆有議論此作尤優
考試官敎授鄭批此策敷答詳明又以敬之一言
貫二書之㫖蓋熟於窮理之學者
聖賢敎人之法有小學焉有大學焉始之
以小學所以收其放心養其德性而立大
學之根本終之以大學所以察夫義理措
之事業而收小學之成功二書相因其道
一而已矣且小學一書乃子朱子蒐輯傳
記纂成有內篇以立本原有外篇以衍支
===
流內篇則立敎明倫敬身稽古是也外篇
則嘉言善行是也內篇首之以立敎而所
敎者洒掃應對之節愛親敬長之道焉次
之以明倫而所明者父子之親君臣之義
夫婦之別長幼之序朋友之交焉次之以
敬身所以明心術之要威儀之則衣服之
制飲食之節也又次之以稽古所以考三
代聖賢已然之迹以證立敎明倫敬身之
言也外篇則述自漢以来賢者則嘉言所
punctuated:
考試官敎授劉批：五策皆有議論，此作尤優。
考試官敎授鄭批：此策敷答詳明，又以「敬」之一言貫二書之㫖，蓋熟於窮理之學者。
聖賢敎人之法，有《小學》焉，有《大學》焉。始之以《小學》，所以收其放心，養其德性，而立《大學》之根本；終之以《大學》，所以察夫義理，措之事業，而收《小學》之成功。二書相因，其道一而已矣。且《小學》一書，乃子朱子蒐輯傳記纂成，有〈內篇〉以立本原，有〈外篇〉以衍支流。〈內篇〉則〈立敎〉、〈明倫〉、〈敬身〉、〈稽古〉是也；〈外篇〉則〈嘉言〉、〈善行〉是也。〈內篇〉首之以〈立敎〉，而所敎者洒掃應對之節、愛親敬長之道焉；次之以〈明倫〉，而所明者父子之親、君臣之義、夫婦之別、長幼之序、朋友之交焉；次之以〈敬身〉，所以明心術之要、威儀之則、衣服之制、飲食之節也；又次之以〈稽古〉，所以考三代聖賢已然之迹，以證〈立敎〉、〈明倫〉、〈敬身〉之言也。〈外篇〉則述自漢以来賢者則〈嘉言〉，所
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Liu comments: All five policy essays contain substantive arguments, and this composition is especially superior.

Examiner and Instructor Zheng comments: This policy essay sets forth its response in detailed and clear fashion, and moreover uses the single word "reverence" (jing) to thread together the purport of the two books; he is surely a scholar well-versed in the exhaustive investigation of principle.

In the method by which the sages and worthies taught people, there is the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and there is the Great Learning (Daxue). Beginning with the Elementary Learning is the means to recover one's strayed mind, nourish one's moral nature, and establish the foundation for the Great Learning; concluding with the Great Learning is the means to investigate moral principles, put them into practice in affairs and undertakings, and reap the completed achievement of the Elementary Learning. The two books build upon one another, and their Way is simply one.

Moreover, the book Elementary Learning was compiled by Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹], who gathered and edited materials from commentaries and records. It has "Inner Chapters" (Neipian) to establish the fundamental source, and "Outer Chapters" (Waipian) to extend the branching streams. The "Inner Chapters" are "Establishing Instruction" (Lijiao), "Clarifying Human Relationships" (Minglun), "Revering the Person" (Jingshen), and "Investigating Antiquity" (Jigu); the "Outer Chapters" are "Fine Words" (Jiayan) and "Good Deeds" (Shanxing). The "Inner Chapters" begin with "Establishing Instruction," and what is taught therein are the etiquette of sprinkling and sweeping and of responding to inquiries, as well as the way of loving one's parents and respecting one's elders. Next comes "Clarifying Human Relationships," and what is clarified therein are the affection between father and son, the righteousness between ruler and minister, the distinction between husband and wife, the precedence between old and young, and the trust between friends. Next comes "Revering the Person," which is the means to clarify the essentials of mental disposition, the rules of dignified demeanor, the regulations of clothing, and the moderation of food and drink. Next after that comes "Investigating Antiquity," which is the means to examine the accomplished traces of the sages and worthies of the Three Dynasties in order to verify the teachings of "Establishing Instruction," "Clarifying Human Relationships," and "Revering the Person."
