title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以廣立教明倫敬身之義又記自漢以来
賢人之善行所以實立教明倫敬身之事
此小學教人之法以為大學脩齊治平之
本三代以後不知此義至先儒北溪陳氏
謂此書綱領甚好切於日用魯齋許氏謂
此書吾信之如神明敬之如父母盖欲學
者篤信而尊崇之也大學則子曾子述孔
子之經傳十章之義外有三綱領內有八
條目三綱領則明德新民止至善是也而
===
明明德一言又為綱領中之綱領焉八條
目則格物致知誠意正心脩身齊家治國
平天下是也而明明德於天下一言又有
以該體用而無遺焉傳者釋綱領外又有
本末章者釋經文物有本末之義也他章
皆以二事相承而誠意自為一章者以誠
意為自脩之首也此大學教人之方而為
小學入德之門漢儒以来鮮有能知之者
至唐韓愈原道篇止及於正心誠意而無
punctuated: 以廣立教、明倫、敬身之義；又記自漢以来賢人之善行，所以實立教、明倫、敬身之事。此《小學》教人之法，以為《大學》脩、齊、治、平之本。三代以後，不知此義。至先儒北溪陳氏謂：「此書綱領甚好，切於日用。」魯齋許氏謂：「此書吾信之如神明，敬之如父母。」盖欲學者篤信而尊崇之也。《大學》則子曾子述孔子之經、傳十章之義。外有三綱領，內有八條目。三綱領，則明德、新民、止至善是也；而「明明德」一言，又為綱領中之綱領焉。八條目，則格物、致知、誠意、正心、脩身、齊家、治國、平天下是也；而「明明德於天下」一言，又有以該體用而無遺焉。傳者釋綱領外，又有本末章者，釋經文「物有本末」之義也；他章皆以二事相承，而「誠意」自為一章者，以誠意為自脩之首也。此《大學》教人之方，而為《小學》入德之門。漢儒以来，鮮有能知之者。至唐韓愈《原道》篇，止及於正心、誠意，而無
translation_en: … in order to broaden the meaning of establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self; and they also record the virtuous deeds of worthy men since the Han dynasty, in order to substantiate the practice of establishing instruction, clarifying human relationships, and revering the self. This is the method by which the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) instructs people, serving as the foundation for self-cultivation, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world in the Great Learning (Daxue). After the Three Dynasties, this meaning was no longer understood. Coming to the former Confucian master Chen of Beixi [Chen Chun 陳淳], he said: "The guiding principles of this book are excellent and closely relevant to daily life." Xu of Luzhai [Xu Heng 許衡] said: "I believe in this book as I do in the divine spirits, and revere it as I do my parents." Indeed, they wished for students to firmly believe in and venerate it. As for the Great Learning, it comprises Master Zeng's transmission of the Classic of Confucius and the meaning of the ten chapters of commentary. Externally it has the Three Guiding Principles, and internally it has the Eight Steps. The Three Guiding Principles are manifesting luminous virtue, renewing the people, and resting in the highest good; and the single phrase "manifesting luminous virtue" is furthermore the guiding principle within the guiding principles. The Eight Steps are investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating the self, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world; and the single phrase "manifesting luminous virtue throughout the world" furthermore encompasses both substance and function without omission. In the commentary, besides explaining the guiding principles, there is also a chapter on roots and branches, which explains the meaning of the Classic's text that "things have their roots and branches." All the other chapters link two items together in sequence, whereas "making the intentions sincere" forms a chapter of its own because making the intentions sincere is the beginning of self-cultivation. This is the method by which the Great Learning instructs people, serving as the gateway to virtue following the Elementary Learning. Since the Han Confucians, few have been able to understand it. Down to Han Yu 韓愈 of the Tang dynasty, his essay "On the Origin of the Way" (Yuan Dao) reached only as far as rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere, while lacking …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所謂格物致知宋朱子進講是書於寧宗
之前則動以格物致知誠意為言者一則
語道之未詳一則愛君之盡誠也然小學
大學教人之術與夫次第節目雖有不同
而為道豈有二致哉明問又謂二書可一
言以蔽之嘗聞之先儒曰敬者聖學之所
以成始而成終者也為小學而不由乎此
則無以涵養本原而謹夫立藝之教為大
學而不由乎此則無以開發聰明以進德
===
而脩業則敬者二書之要領也愚生雖由
小學而入大學然於道未知嚮方姑摭所
聞以對惟進而教之
第三問
陳謙
同考試官教諭王批此策有考據有斷制非胸中素有定論者不能允宜高薦
同考試官教諭吳批薦舉一策塲中荅者率多遺漏惟此作随問随荅盖留心於策學者也
punctuated:
所謂格物、致知，宋朱子進講是書於寧宗之前，則動以格物、致知、誠意為言者，一則語道之未詳，一則愛君之盡誠也。然《小學》、《大學》教人之術，與夫次第、節目雖有不同，而為道豈有二致哉？明問又謂二書可一言以蔽之。嘗聞之先儒曰：「敬者，聖學之所以成始而成終者也。為小學而不由乎此，則無以涵養本原而謹夫立藝之教；為大學而不由乎此，則無以開發聰明以進德而脩業。」則敬者，二書之要領也。愚生雖由小學而入大學，然於道未知嚮方，姑摭所聞以對，惟進而教之。

第三問
陳謙
同考試官教諭王批：此策有考據，有斷制，非胸中素有定論者不能，允宜高薦。
同考試官教諭吳批：薦舉一策，塲中荅者率多遺漏，惟此作随問随荅，盖留心於策學者也。
translation_en:
… anything of what is called the investigation of things and the extension of knowledge; whereas when Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] of the Song expounded this book before Emperor Ningzong (寧宗), he invariably spoke of the investigation of things, the extension of knowledge, and making the intentions sincere—in the one case, the discussion of the Way was not yet thorough; in the other, love for his sovereign was utterly sincere. Yet although the methods of teaching people in the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue 小學) and the Great Learning (Daxue 大學), along with their sequence and specific items, differ, how could there be two different paths in pursuing the Way? Your enlightened question further asks how the two books may be summed up in a single word. I have heard a former Confucian scholar say: "Reverent seriousness (jing 敬) is that by which the learning of the sages completes both its beginning and its end. If one engages in the Elementary Learning without proceeding from this, there is no way to nurture the fundamental source and be attentive to the instruction in establishing arts; if one engages in the Great Learning without proceeding from this, there is no way to open up intelligence and discernment so as to advance in virtue and cultivate one's work." Thus, reverent seriousness is the essential principle of both books. Although this foolish student has entered the Great Learning from the Elementary Learning, I do not yet know the direction toward the Way; I merely gather what I have heard to reply, and pray that you will admit me and instruct me.

Question Three
Chen Qian 陳謙
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Wang: This policy essay has both evidentiary grounding and decisive judgment; none could have written it who did not already hold settled views in his mind. It truly deserves high recommendation.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Wu: On the policy question concerning recommendation of talent, those answering in the examination compound generally had many omissions; only this composition answers each point as asked, showing that he has paid careful attention to the study of policy questions.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授劉批文勢滔滔事實不遺策
塲之優者
考試官教授鄭批策詳贍明白
為國莫先於薦賢薦賢惟在於至公盖為
國而不薦賢非所以愛其國薦賢而不以
至公豈能得夫賢哉知乎此則可以復明
問矣粤自三代以前俊乂在官薦舉之名
未立成周之時舉能其官而薦舉之名始
聞自是薦者非一人舉者非一途苟材之
===
可用雖親亦薦如祁奚之薦祁午吕蒙正
之薦夷簡而人不以為疑者公也雖讐亦
舉如觧狐之舉荆伯柳吕夷簡之舉范仲
淹而人不以為嫌者亦公也漢張釋之之
善聽獄訟于定國之練習法令而袁盎丙
吉薦之唐張九齡之學問該博韓休之行
誼純篤而張說蕭嵩舉之宋吕文靖之薦
包拯非以其同巷不求見乎司馬光之薦
劉元城非以其無書抵政府乎之數君子
punctuated:
考試官教授劉批：文勢滔滔，事實不遺，策塲之優者。
考試官教授鄭批：策詳贍明白。
為國莫先於薦賢，薦賢惟在於至公。盖為國而不薦賢，非所以愛其國；薦賢而不以至公，豈能得夫賢哉？知乎此，則可以復明問矣。粤自三代以前，俊乂在官，薦舉之名未立；成周之時，舉能其官，而薦舉之名始聞。自是薦者非一人，舉者非一途。苟材之可用，雖親亦薦，如祁奚之薦祁午，吕蒙正之薦夷簡，而人不以為疑者，公也；雖讐亦舉，如觧狐之舉荆伯柳，吕夷簡之舉范仲淹，而人不以為嫌者，亦公也。漢張釋之之善聽獄訟，于定國之練習法令，而袁盎、丙吉薦之；唐張九齡之學問該博，韓休之行誼純篤，而張說、蕭嵩舉之；宋吕文靖之薦包拯，非以其同巷不求見乎？司馬光之薦劉元城，非以其無書抵政府乎？之數君子
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner and Confucian School Professor Liu: The momentum of the writing flows like a torrent, and no historical facts are omitted; it is an outstanding piece from the policy essay session.
Comment by Examiner and Confucian School Professor Zheng: The policy essay is detailed, rich, and clear.
In governing a state, nothing takes precedence over recommending the worthy, and recommending the worthy lies solely in utmost impartiality. Indeed, to govern a state without recommending the worthy is no way to love that state; and to recommend the worthy without utmost impartiality—how could one ever obtain those who are truly worthy? Understanding this, one can answer the perceptive question. Before the Three Dynasties, men of eminent talent served in office, and the term "recommendation and promotion" (jianju) had not yet been established. In the time of the glorious Zhou, those capable of fulfilling their offices were promoted, and the term "recommendation and promotion" was first heard. From then on, those who recommended were not a single person, and the avenues of promotion were not a single path. Provided that a man's talent was usable, even a relative would be recommended—as when Qi Xi 祁奚 recommended Qi Wu 祁午, and Lü Mengzheng 呂蒙正 recommended [Lü] Yijian 呂夷簡—and people did not regard it with suspicion, because it was impartial. Even a personal enemy would be promoted—as when Xie Hu 解狐 promoted Jing Boliu 荊伯柳, and Lü Yijian promoted Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹—and people did not regard it as cause for misgiving, because that too was impartial. In the Han dynasty, Zhang Shizhi 張釋之 was skilled at hearing lawsuits and Yu Dingguo 于定國 was well-versed in laws and ordinances, and Yuan Ang 袁盎 and Bing Ji 丙吉 recommended them. In the Tang dynasty, Zhang Jiuling 張九齡 possessed broad and comprehensive learning and Han Xiu 韓休 had pure and earnest conduct, and Zhang Yue 張說 and Xiao Song 蕭嵩 promoted them. In the Song dynasty, when Lü Wenjing 呂文靖 [Lü Yijian] recommended Bao Zheng 包拯, was it not because, though living in the same lane, Bao never sought an audience with him? When Sima Guang 司馬光 recommended Liu Yuancheng 劉元城 [Liu Anshi 劉安世], was it not because Liu never sent a letter to the Administration Chamber? What these several gentlemen…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之所薦雖不同而同出於公也至若李師
錫乃王德用之甥也以德用故而薦者三
十餘人陳琪乃龐籍之婿也以龐籍故而
舉者二十四人是皆貴要之私耳如公道
何王安國荆公之親弟也託荆公以力薦
之吕惠卿荆公之同已也犯衆怒而力舉
之是皆親故之私耳如公道何此所以不
能無譏於人也他如自謂我為相無能但
有一能善用人者吕文穆也自言我輔政
===
何功惟薦二臺官無愧非唐質肅乎二公
之急於薦人如此其公可知矣身為諫議
未嘗妄薦一人者謝泌也官居執政不敢
私薦一士者非陳升之乎二公之謹於薦
人如此則其公又可知矣方今
聖皇馭極賢路大開當途推轂者皆忠君憂國
之臣拔茅彙征者悉秉德守正之士朝無
倖位而野無遺賢矣執事猶謂山林泉石
尚有遺逸之士百司庶府不無淹滯之才
punctuated: 之所薦雖不同，而同出於公也。至若李師錫乃王德用之甥也，以德用故而薦者三十餘人；陳琪乃龐籍之婿也，以龐籍故而舉者二十四人，是皆貴要之私耳，如公道何？王安國，荆公之親弟也，託荆公以力薦之；吕惠卿，荆公之同已也，犯衆怒而力舉之，是皆親故之私耳，如公道何？此所以不能無譏於人也。他如自謂「我為相無能，但有一能，善用人」者，吕文穆也；自言「我輔政何功？惟薦二臺官無愧」，非唐質肅乎？二公之急於薦人如此，其公可知矣。身為諫議，未嘗妄薦一人者，謝泌也；官居執政，不敢私薦一士者，非陳升之乎？二公之謹於薦人如此，則其公又可知矣。方今聖皇馭極，賢路大開，當途推轂者皆忠君憂國之臣，拔茅彙征者悉秉德守正之士，朝無倖位而野無遺賢矣。執事猶謂山林泉石尚有遺逸之士，百司庶府不無淹滯之才，
translation_en: …what [these several gentlemen] recommended differed, yet all stemmed alike from impartiality. As for cases like Li Shixi 李師錫, who was the nephew of Wang Deyong 王德用, and on Wang Deyong's account had more than thirty people recommend him; or Chen Qi 陳琪, who was the son-in-law of Pang Ji 龐籍, and on Pang Ji's account had twenty-four people nominate him—these were all merely the private favoritism of the noble and powerful. What did they have to do with the way of impartiality? Wang Anguo 王安國 was the biological younger brother of the Duke of Jing 荆公 [Wang Anshi 王安石], who relied on the Duke of Jing to forcefully recommend him; Lü Huiqing 吕惠卿 was a partisan of the Duke of Jing, who braved public anger to forcefully nominate him—these were all merely the private favoritism of relatives and old acquaintances. What did they have to do with the way of impartiality? This is why they could not escape criticism from others. As for other examples: the one who said of himself, "As Grand Councilor I have no abilities, save for one ability—being good at employing men," was Lü Wenmu 吕文穆 [Lü Mengzheng 吕蒙正]; and the one who declared of himself, "In assisting the administration, what merit have I? Only in recommending two Censors have I nothing to be ashamed of"—was that not Tang Zhisu 唐質肅 [Tang Jie 唐介]? Since these two dukes were so eager in recommending men, their impartiality can be known. The one who, serving as Policy Critic-Adviser, never recklessly recommended a single person was Xie Bi 謝泌; and the one who, holding office as an Administration Vice-Councilor, dared not privately recommend a single scholar—was that not Chen Shengzhi 陳升之? Since these two dukes were so cautious in recommending men, their impartiality can likewise be known. At present, the Sage Emperor reigns on the throne, and the pathway for the worthy is wide open. Those in power who push the wheel hubs [to advance talent] are all ministers loyal to the ruler and concerned for the state; those who are drawn forth in groups like pulled-up couch grass are all scholars who uphold virtue and guard rectitude. The court has no positions gained by unearned fortune, and the wilderness has no overlooked worthies. Yet Your Reverence still says that among the mountain forests and spring-fed rocks there remain overlooked and recluse scholars, and that across the hundred offices and myriad bureaus there is no lack of talent languishing in obscurity…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
誠過慮也茲欲屈在下僚者悉得擢用誠
如近者臺憲大臣所言在京廷臣各舉所
知在外風憲監司各舉所屬之廉能則才
無淹滯矣欲隱於巖穴者咸得彙進誠如
明詔所言山林懷材抱德之士有司舉送銓
曹擢用則士無遺逸矣然又在於司薦舉
者之各秉至公而後可富鄭公嘗曰有德
者然後知人之德有才者然後知人之才
歐陽公亦曰廉者舉清廉贓者舉貪濁然
===
則薦舉不公當嚴連坐之法請以是為執
事獻
第四問
楊茂元
同考試官訓導張批敷演畧無凝滯必博
洽之士也高薦何忝
同考試官教諭周批五策文采爛然首論文
章一策尤有考據他日所就未可量也宜寘魁選
考試官教授劉批敷荅豐贍優於衆作
punctuated:
誠過慮也。茲欲屈在下僚者悉得擢用，誠如近者臺憲大臣所言，在京廷臣各舉所知，在外風憲監司各舉所屬之廉能，則才無淹滯矣。欲隱於巖穴者咸得彙進，誠如明詔所言，山林懷材抱德之士，有司舉送銓曹擢用，則士無遺逸矣。然又在於司薦舉者之各秉至公而後可。富鄭公嘗曰：「有德者然後知人之德，有才者然後知人之才。」歐陽公亦曰：「廉者舉清廉，贓者舉貪濁。」然則薦舉不公，當嚴連坐之法。請以是為執事獻。

第四問
楊茂元
同考試官訓導張批：敷演畧無凝滯，必博洽之士也，高薦何忝。
同考試官教諭周批：五策文采爛然，首論文章一策，尤有考據，他日所就未可量也，宜寘魁選。
考試官教授劉批：敷荅豐贍，優於衆作。
translation_en:
… is truly an excessive concern. Now, if we wish for all those bending in lowly subordinate posts to be promoted and employed, it should truly be as the Censorial officials and grand ministers recently proposed: let the court officials in the capital each recommend those whom they know, and let the風憲 (censorial) and監司 (surveillance) officials in the provinces each recommend the incorrupt and capable among their subordinates; then no talent will languish in obscurity. If we wish for all those living in seclusion among cliffs and caves to advance together as a group, it should truly be as the Emperor's luminous edicts have stated: let the local authorities recommend and send scholars of the mountains and forests who cherish talent and embrace virtue to the Ministry of Personnel for promotion and employment; then no worthy scholar will be left behind in retirement. Yet this also depends upon those in charge of recommendations each upholding the utmost impartiality before it can succeed. Duke Fu of Zheng (Fu Bi 富弼) once said: "Only one who possesses virtue knows the virtue of others; only one who possesses talent knows the talent of others." Master Ouyang (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修) likewise said: "The incorrupt recommend the pure and incorrupt; the venal recommend the greedy and corrupt." This being so, when recommendations are not impartial, the law of joint liability for the recommender must be strictly enforced. I beg to offer this to Your Excellency.

Fourth Policy Question
Yang Maoyuan 楊茂元
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Zhang: The exposition has not the slightest stagnation or obstruction; he must be a scholar of broad and thorough learning. How could a high recommendation bring any shame?
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhou: All five policy essays shine with literary brilliance, and the first essay discussing literature is especially well-grounded in historical evidence. His future achievements cannot be measured; he ought to be placed among the top selections.
Comment by Examiner Confucian School Comparisons Instructor (Director of Studies) Liu: The exposition and answers are rich and abundant, superior to the work of the crowd.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授鄭批考究詳明必本古能文之士
有義理之文有詞章之文繪章繪句錦心
繍口詞章之文也義本六經文關世敎義
理之文也詞章之文膾炙於人口才士皆
可能之義理之文浸漬於人心非有德者
莫之能也三代以上莫非義理之文三代
以下純於義理者盖鮮矣有如孔明韓杜
之流豈非百鳥中之孤鳳歟是故晉之文
章非不多也而歐陽公謂晉無文章惟陶
===
淵明歸去來辭豈非以其蕭然物外高潔
簡古乎唐之文章非不富也而蘇東坡謂
唐無文章惟李愿歸盤谷序豈非以其善
狀物態宛轉新竒乎孔明出師一表其忠
肝義膽凛乎其不可犯蘇東坡謂其與伊
訓說命相表裏信矣杜子美平生詩集其
忠君愛國藹然見於言外黃山谷謂其得
三百篇之㫖宜矣韓子之文若捕龍蛇急
與之角而不暇豈無所自而然歟良由有
punctuated:
考試官教授鄭批：考究詳明，必本古能文之士。

有義理之文，有詞章之文。繪章繪句，錦心繍口，詞章之文也；義本六經，文關世敎，義理之文也。詞章之文，膾炙於人口，才士皆可能之；義理之文，浸漬於人心，非有德者莫之能也。三代以上，莫非義理之文；三代以下，純於義理者盖鮮矣。有如孔明、韓、杜之流，豈非百鳥中之孤鳳歟？是故晉之文章非不多也，而歐陽公謂晉無文章，惟陶淵明《歸去來辭》，豈非以其蕭然物外、高潔簡古乎？唐之文章非不富也，而蘇東坡謂唐無文章，惟《李愿歸盤谷序》，豈非以其善狀物態、宛轉新竒乎？孔明《出師》一表，其忠肝義膽，凛乎其不可犯，蘇東坡謂其與《伊訓》、《說命》相表裏，信矣；杜子美平生詩集，其忠君愛國，藹然見於言外，黃山谷謂其得三百篇之㫖，宜矣。韓子之文，若捕龍蛇，急與之角而不暇，豈無所自而然歟？良由有
translation_en:
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zheng comments: The investigation is detailed and clear; he must be a scholar capable in prose whose learning is rooted in antiquity.

There is writing of moral principle, and there is writing of literary flourish. Adorning chapters and embellishing sentences, with a brocade heart and embroidered mouth—this is writing of literary flourish. Having principles rooted in the Six Classics and writing that bears upon the moral instruction of the age—this is writing of moral principle. Writing of literary flourish is relished on people's lips, and any man of talent may be capable of it; writing of moral principle steeps into people's hearts, and none without virtue is capable of it. During the Three Dynasties and earlier, all writing was writing of moral principle; since the Three Dynasties, those pure in moral principle have been few indeed. That there were such figures as Zhuge Liang [Kongming 孔明], Han Yu [韓], and Du Fu [杜]—were they not lone phoenixes among a hundred birds? Therefore, the literary works of the Jin dynasty were by no means few, yet Ouyang Xiu [Ouyang Gong 歐陽公] said that the Jin had no literature except Tao Yuanming's 陶淵明 "Rhapsody on Returning Home" (Guiqulai ci 歸去來辭); was this not because of its serene detachment beyond material things, its lofty purity and simple antiquity? The literary works of the Tang dynasty were by no means scarce, yet Su Shi [Su Dongpo 蘇東坡] said that the Tang had no literature except the "Preface Seeing Off Li Yuan on His Return to Pan Valley" (Li Yuan gui Pangu xu 李愿歸盤谷序); was this not because of its skill in depicting the forms of things, its supple turns and fresh originality? As for Zhuge Liang's single "Memorial on Deploying the Troops" (Chushi biao 出師表), its loyal heart and righteous courage are so awe-inspiring as to be inviolable; Su Dongpo's statement that it stands as outer and inner counterparts to the "Instructions of Yi" (Yi xun 伊訓) and the "Charge to Yue" (Yue ming 說命) is truly credible. As for Du Fu's [Du Zimei 杜子美] lifelong collection of poetry, his loyalty to his ruler and love for his state appear genially beyond the words themselves; Huang Tingjian's [Huang Shangu 黃山谷] statement that he grasped the purport of the Three Hundred Odes is fitting indeed. The prose of Master Han [Han Yu] is like seizing dragons and serpents, urgently grappling with them without a moment's pause; how could it be so without having a source from which it came? Truly it is because he…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
得於詩葩易竒盤誥詰屈春秋謹嚴之趣
也柳子之文軋漢周而陵晉宋凛然一王
之法豈無自而爾歟良由上學詩易春秋
下得左氏國語之妙也讀歐之文如遊帝
舜之庭而聆簫韶之樂姑舉一篇以見其
他如本論序所以麾異端之道雍容閒雅
不勞寸兵尺鐵而聞風逺遁真竒文矣讀
蘇之文如駕千里之駒而御以王良造父
姑舉一篇以例其餘如上神宗書所獻三
===
事廣譬博喻直欲致其君為堯舜湯武而
不犯逆鱗之怒真妙文矣至若制誥之文
得六經簡嚴之體者錢穆父作章子厚之
謫詞范純仁之遺表焉記述之文得六經
紀實之旨者王元之之記待漏院張伯玉
之記六經閣焉奏議之文如頴濱之言條
例張方平之諫用兵皆得伊訓吕誥之意
詩章之文如歐公之詠春帖蘇公之諷水
利皆得周雅商頌之體他如進士之文王
punctuated: 得於《詩》葩、《易》竒、盤誥詰屈、《春秋》謹嚴之趣也。柳子之文，軋漢、周而陵晉、宋，凛然一王之法，豈無自而爾歟？良由上學《詩》、《易》、《春秋》，下得左氏、《國語》之妙也。讀歐之文，如遊帝舜之庭而聆《簫韶》之樂，姑舉一篇以見其他：如《本論》，序所以麾異端之道，雍容閒雅，不勞寸兵尺鐵而聞風逺遁，真竒文矣。讀蘇之文，如駕千里之駒而御以王良、造父，姑舉一篇以例其餘：如《上神宗書》所獻三事，廣譬博喻，直欲致其君為堯、舜、湯、武而不犯逆鱗之怒，真妙文矣。至若制誥之文，得六經簡嚴之體者，錢穆父作章子厚之謫詞、范純仁之遺表焉；記述之文，得六經紀實之旨者，王元之之記待漏院、張伯玉之記六經閣焉；奏議之文，如頴濱之言條例、張方平之諫用兵，皆得《伊訓》、《吕誥》之意；詩章之文，如歐公之詠春帖、蘇公之諷水利，皆得周雅、商頌之體。他如進士之文，王
translation_en: …gained the spirit of the luxuriance of the Book of Odes (Shi), the marvels of the Book of Changes (Yi), the abstruse ruggedness of the Pan Geng and the Announcements (Gao), and the strict precision of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). The writings of Master Liu [Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元] rivaled those of the Zhou and Han and surpassed those of the Jin and Song, possessing the awe-inspiring authority of a unified kingly standard—how could they have been so without a source? Truly it was because above he studied the Odes, the Changes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals, and below he grasped the subtleties of the Zuo Tradition (Zuoshi) and the Discourses of the States (Guoyu). Reading the writings of Ouyang [Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修] is like wandering in the court of Emperor Shun and listening to the Xiaoshao music. Let us tentatively cite one piece to illustrate the rest: for instance, his Discourse on Fundamentals (Ben lun), which sets forth the way to repel heterodoxy in a poised, serene, and refined manner, causing it to flee afar at the mere rumor without expending an inch of blade or a foot of iron—truly a marvelous piece of writing! Reading the writings of Su [Su Shi 蘇軾] is like driving a thousand-li colt with Wang Liang 王良 or Zaofu 造父 at the reins. Let us tentatively cite one piece to exemplify the remainder: for instance, the three matters presented in his Letter Submitted to Emperor Shenzong (Shang Shenzong shu), which employs wide-ranging analogies and broad metaphors, directly seeking to make his ruler like Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu without provoking the wrath of the dragon's inverted scale—truly a wondrous piece of writing! As for imperial decrees and proclamations (zhigao) that captured the concise and stern style of the Six Classics, there were the edict of demotion for Zhang Zihou 章子厚 [Zhang Dun 章惇] composed by Qian Mufu 錢穆父 [Qian勰] and the testamentary memorial of Fan Chunren 范純仁; for narrative and descriptive writings that captured the Six Classics' purport of recording facts, there were Wang Yuanzhi's 王元之 [Wang Yucheng 王禹偁] Record of the Courtyard of Awaiting the Clepsydra (Dailou yuan ji) and Zhang Boyu's 張伯玉 Record of the Pavilion of the Six Classics (Liujing ge ji); for memorials and deliberations, such as Yingbin's 潁濱 [Su Zhe 蘇轍] words on the Finance Planning Commission regulations and Zhang Fangping's 張方平 remonstrances against the use of military force, all captured the meaning of the Instructions of Yi (Yi xun) and the Announcements of Lü (Lü gao) [Critical Marquis of Lü on Punishments (Lü xing)]; and for poetic compositions, such as Lord Ouyang's verses for the Spring Placards and Lord Su's satirical poems on water conservancy, all captured the form of the Odes of Zhou and the Hymns of Shang. As for other works, such as the writings of metropolitan graduates (jinshi), Wang…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曾以賦策第而為賢相張庭堅以經義進
而為名臣豈可以科舉輕視之乎序述之
文程伊川自序易傳游定夫為孫莘老序
周易傳豈可以序體槩論乎之數子者立
言雖不同其所以精乎詞章而根於義理
則一也豈可專以詞章之文目之哉愚也
學古為文未聆其要惟執事恕其狂妄而
教之
第五問
===
黃珣
同考試官學正陳批時務一策正觀士子變
通之學場中答者多臆說令人厭觀惟此策有考
據有措置足見學識宜冠多士
考試官教授劉批策有定見真識時務者也
考試官教授鄭批時務一策足見有用之學
天下無不可用之人在勸懲之有道天下
無不可為之事在任用之得人盖勸懲有
道則守令將校之繼來新任者皆可盡其
punctuated:
曾以賦策第而為賢相，張庭堅以經義進而為名臣，豈可以科舉輕視之乎？序述之文，程伊川自序《易傳》，游定夫為孫莘老序《周易傳》，豈可以序體槩論乎？之數子者，立言雖不同，其所以精乎詞章而根於義理則一也，豈可專以詞章之文目之哉？愚也學古為文，未聆其要，惟執事恕其狂妄而教之。

第五問
黃珣
同考試官學正陳批：〔時務一策，正觀士子變通之學。場中答者多臆說，令人厭觀；惟此策有考據，有措置，足見學識，宜冠多士。〕
考試官教授劉批：〔策有定見，真識時務者也。〕
考試官教授鄭批：〔時務一策，足見有用之學。〕

天下無不可用之人，在勸懲之有道；天下無不可為之事，在任用之得人。盖勸懲有道，則守令、將校之繼來新任者，皆可盡其
translation_en:
… Wang Zeng 王曾 passed the examinations through rhapsodies and policy essays and became a worthy minister, while Zhang Tingjian 張庭堅 advanced through expositions on the Classics and became a renowned official—how could one belittle them on account of the civil service examinations? As for prefaces and expository writings, Cheng Yichuan 程伊川 (Cheng Yi 程頤) wrote his own preface to his Commentary on the Changes (Yi zhuan 易傳), and You Dingfu 游定夫 (You Zuo 游酢) wrote a preface for Sun Xinlao's 孫莘老 (Sun Jue 孫覺) Commentary on the Zhou Changes (Zhouyi zhuan 周易傳)—how could one lump them together merely as examples of the preface genre? Although these several gentlemen differed in how they established their words, they were one and the same in that their writings were refined in literary form while rooted in moral principle. How could one regard them solely as mere belletristic writing? In my ignorance, I study antiquity to compose literature, yet I have not grasped its essentials; I only pray that Your Honors will pardon my rashness and instruct me.

Fifth Question
By Huang Xun 黃珣
Comment by Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen 陳: [This policy question on current affairs is precisely meant to observe the candidates' learning in adapting to changing circumstances. Most respondents in the examination hall offered mere conjecture, which is tiresome to read; only this policy essay possesses both evidential grounding and practical measures, amply demonstrating scholarship and insight, and deserves to be placed first among the many scholars.]
Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu 劉: [The policy essay displays settled views; he is truly one who understands current affairs.]
Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zheng 鄭: [This policy essay on current affairs amply demonstrates practical and useful learning.]

In the realm, there is no person who cannot be employed—it lies in having the proper way to encourage and punish; in the realm, there is no affair that cannot be accomplished—it lies in obtaining the right men for appointment. For if there is a proper way to encourage and punish, then the prefects, magistrates, commanders, and officers who succeed one another in new appointments can all fulfill their…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
用任用得人則風俗水利儲蓄賦役之事
皆可得而理矣執事先生發策而以浙之
切務所宜變通者下詢承學愚何足以知
之然一事不知儒者所恥執事以儒者俊
傑侍承學敢不罄一得之愚以復乎夫守
令將校之不得其人在監司之勸懲有道
而風俗水利儲蓄賦役之咸得其理又在
藩臬令守之得人也蓋監司所以肅百僚
而貞百度也藩司所以承流而宣化而守
===
令則民之師帥也彼守令所以牧民當秉
廉潔之操將校所以領軍當有撫馭之才
今守令之貪墨者已罷黜之矣而繼來者
猶未端其操以執守之未定也將校之奸
貪者已更選之矣而新任者猶或非其才
以素習於膏粱也為監司者誠舉憲綱以
戒勵之嚴法令以訓飭之其能改過自新
者待以禮而不究其遂非不悛者置以法
而不貸則守令將校皆將悔禍懼罪之不
punctuated:
用；任用得人，則風俗、水利、儲蓄、賦役之事，皆可得而理矣。執事先生發策，而以浙之切務所宜變通者下詢承學，愚何足以知之？然一事不知，儒者所恥；執事以儒者俊傑侍承學，敢不罄一得之愚以復乎？

夫守令、將校之不得其人，在監司之勸懲有道；而風俗、水利、儲蓄、賦役之咸得其理，又在藩、臬、令、守之得人也。蓋監司所以肅百僚而貞百度也，藩司所以承流而宣化，而守令則民之師帥也。彼守令所以牧民，當秉廉潔之操；將校所以領軍，當有撫馭之才。今守令之貪墨者已罷黜之矣，而繼來者猶未端其操，以執守之未定也；將校之奸貪者已更選之矣，而新任者猶或非其才，以素習於膏粱也。為監司者，誠舉憲綱以戒勵之，嚴法令以訓飭之，其能改過自新者，待以禮而不究；其遂非不悛者，置以法而不貸，則守令、將校皆將悔禍懼罪之不…
translation_en:
… capacities; and when appointments secure the right men, then matters of popular customs, water control, grain reserves, and land taxes and labor services can all be brought into good order.

You, the examining officials, have posed this policy question, inquiring of us junior scholars about the pressing affairs of Zhejiang that ought to be adapted to changing circumstances. How could an ignorant person like myself be equal to knowing such things? Yet to be ignorant of even a single matter is something a Confucian scholar considers shameful. Since you treat us junior scholars as outstanding Confucian talents [reading 侍 as 待], how dare I not exhaust my humble understanding to offer a reply?

Now, when prefects, magistrates, and military officers are not the right men, the remedy lies in the Surveillance Officials having the proper way to encourage and punish; and for popular customs, water control, grain reserves, and taxes and corvée to all be properly managed, it in turn depends on obtaining the right men as Provincial Administration Commissioners, Surveillance Commissioners, magistrates, and prefects. For the Surveillance Officials exist to impose discipline on all officials and rectify all administrative standards; the Provincial Administration Commission exists to receive the imperial grace and propagate its transforming influence; and prefects and magistrates are the teachers and leaders of the common people.

Those prefects and magistrates, whose duty it is to shepherd the people, ought to hold fast to pure and incorruptible integrity; the military officers, whose duty it is to command the troops, ought to possess the talent to pacify and control them. Nowadays, corrupt and venal prefects and magistrates have already been dismissed, yet those who succeed them still have not rectified their conduct, because their moral resolve is not yet firm; treacherous and greedy military officers have already been replaced, yet those newly appointed sometimes still lack the requisite talent, because they have long been accustomed to a life of luxury and ease. If those who serve as Surveillance Officials truly uphold the disciplinary regulations to warn and encourage them, and strictly enforce the laws and ordinances to instruct and admonish them—treating with courtesy and not prosecuting those who are able to mend their ways and renew themselves, while subjecting to the law without leniency those who persist in wrongdoing and refuse to repent—then prefects, magistrates, and military officers will all have no time to do anything but regret disaster and fear punishment, and…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
暇而變為廉潔有用之才矣民風欲淳也
而刁訟日滋民俗欲儉也而奢侈益甚由
積習之所致也為守令者誠能教以孝弟
道以忠信而強梗弗率者齊以刑食之以
時用之以禮而踰禮過用者禁以法則風
俗自淳儉矣浙西地卑而憂澇浙東地高
而憂旱由預防之無備也為守令者誠於
浙西疏大湖瀦蓄之水浚河港泥茭之積
俾遇澇則水由淞江而下流於海於浙東
===
則浚湮塞之湖藪以瀦水脩廢弛之陂堰
以節流或遇旱則水以桔槔而上運於田
則旱澇可無虞矣自夫水旱之荐臻也民
仰食於公而秋成不足以償之是致倉廩
空虛況今歲水旱相仍何恠乎仰給者道
路相望乎自夫職守之匪人已囊必以富
闤闠而困窮者竭力以供役是致民多貧
乏況比歲軍需悉出於三等之人户又何
恠夫横斂者項背相接乎今欲廣儲蓄以
punctuated: 暇，而變為廉潔有用之才矣。民風欲淳也，而刁訟日滋；民俗欲儉也，而奢侈益甚，由積習之所致也。為守令者，誠能教以孝弟，道以忠信，而強梗弗率者齊以刑；食之以時，用之以禮，而踰禮過用者禁以法，則風俗自淳儉矣。浙西地卑而憂澇，浙東地高而憂旱，由預防之無備也。為守令者，誠於浙西疏大湖瀦蓄之水，浚河港泥茭之積，俾遇澇則水由淞江而下流於海；於浙東則浚湮塞之湖藪以瀦水，脩廢弛之陂堰以節流，或遇旱則水以桔槔而上運於田，則旱澇可無虞矣。自夫水旱之荐臻也，民仰食於公，而秋成不足以償之，是致倉廩空虛；況今歲水旱相仍，何恠乎仰給者道路相望乎？自夫職守之匪人，已囊必以富闤闠，而困窮者竭力以供役，是致民多貧乏；況比歲軍需悉出於三等之人户，又何恠夫横斂者項背相接乎？今欲廣儲蓄以
translation_en: …will not have time enough [to regret misfortune and fear punishment], and will transform into incorruptible and useful talents. We desire the popular ethos to be pure and simple, yet perverse litigation proliferates daily; we desire local customs to be frugal, yet extravagance grows ever more extreme. This is brought about by long-accumulated habits. If those serving as prefects and magistrates can truly instruct the people in filial piety and fraternal respect, guide them with loyalty and trustworthiness, and regulate the obstinate and disobedient with punishments; and if they have the people consume according to the seasons, spend according to ritual propriety, and prohibit with laws those who transgress ritual and overspend, then customs will naturally become pure and frugal. In western Zhejiang the land is low-lying and suffers from waterlogging, while in eastern Zhejiang the land is high and suffers from drought; this is because there are no advance preparations to guard against them. If those serving as prefects and magistrates truly, in western Zhejiang, dredge the waters stored in the great lakes and clear out the accumulated silt and water-grasses in the rivers and channels, so that when waterlogging occurs the water flows down through the Song River (Songjiang) into the sea; and if, in eastern Zhejiang, they dredge the silted-up lakes and marshes to store water, and repair dilapidated dikes and weirs to regulate the flow, so that should drought occur, water can be lifted up into the fields using well-sweeps, then there will be no need to worry about drought or waterlogging. Ever since floods and droughts have repeatedly occurred, the people have relied on the state for food, and the autumn harvest has been insufficient to repay it, resulting in empty granaries. Moreover, with floods and droughts following one upon another this year, what wonder is it that those looking for relief can be seen all along the roads? Ever since prefectural and county posts have been filled by the wrong men, they inevitably line their own pockets by enriching themselves from the marketplaces [?], while the distressed and impoverished exhaust their strength to supply labor services, resulting in many of the people becoming poor and destitute. Moreover, in recent years military supplies have been drawn entirely from the three grades of households; what wonder is it, then, that arbitrary exactions follow closely one after another? Now, if we wish to expand reserves in order to…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
給民必和糴於鄰封或勸助於富室而又
謹出納之令使羨餘不至於侵欺可也欲
均賦役以息民必停不急之徵蠲公上之
賦而又審貧富之徭使軍需仍復於舊額
可也之數者欲增實效不事虛文固在於
為守令者之得其人然防其奸而革其弊
作其怠而董其成又在於為藩臬者之同
其心如此則兩浙之務無難處者矣變通
之術無踰於此愚生風簷寸晷未暇援古
===
以對姑述耳之所聞如此倘與而進焉尚
當以天下之務為執事陳之
punctuated: 給民，必和糴於鄰封，或勸助於富室，而又謹出納之令，使羨餘不至於侵欺，可也。欲均賦役以息民，必停不急之徵，蠲公上之賦，而又審貧富之徭，使軍需仍復於舊額，可也。之數者，欲增實效，不事虛文，固在於為守令者之得其人；然防其奸而革其弊，作其怠而董其成，又在於為藩臬者之同其心。如此則兩浙之務無難處者矣。變通之術，無踰於此。愚生風簷寸晷，未暇援古以對，姑述耳之所聞如此。倘與而進焉，尚當以天下之務為執事陳之。
translation_en: …provide for the people, we must carry out harmonious grain purchases from neighboring jurisdictions or encourage contributions from wealthy households, while also strictly enforcing the regulations on receipts and disbursements so that surplus grain is not embezzled—that will suffice. If we wish to equalize taxes and corvée labor in order to give rest to the people, we must halt non-urgent levies and remit taxes due to the state, while also carefully assessing corvée obligations according to poverty and wealth so that military requisitions are restored to their former quotas—that will suffice. In these several matters, if we wish to increase actual results and not engage in empty formalities, it certainly depends on obtaining the right men to serve as prefects and magistrates; yet preventing their malfeasance and eradicating their abuses, rousing theirindolence and supervising their accomplishments, depends further on those who serve as Provincial Administration Commissioners and Surveillance Commissioners uniting their hearts. If this is done, there will be nothing difficult to manage in the affairs of Western and Eastern Zhejiang. The art of adapting to circumstances does not go beyond this. Under the windswept eaves with only an inch of shadow on the sundial, this foolish student has lacked the leisure to cite antiquity in reply, and has merely recounted what his ears have heard in this manner. Should you approve of me and advance me, I shall yet set forth the affairs of the entire realm before Your Excellencies.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄後序
上天純佑我
皇明文運誕興乃今成化七年歲
當賓興賢能巡按浙江監察
御史郭瑞暨藩臬重臣預期
禮聘儒紳以司考試及期合
十一郡士凡三試之拔其尤
===
者九十人遵
定額也既次第其名氏復集其
文之純雅者為録將以獻于
上僉謂襄宜序其末欽惟
太祖高皇帝肇開文運科目取士
雖以文藝而學校教人必先
德行盖與舜之命司徒以敷
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄後序

上天純佑我皇明，文運誕興。乃今成化七年，歲當賓興賢能，巡按浙江監察御史郭瑞暨藩臬重臣，預期禮聘儒紳以司考試。及期，合十一郡士，凡三試之，拔其尤者九十人，遵定額也。既次第其名氏，復集其文之純雅者為録，將以獻于上。僉謂襄宜序其末。

欽惟太祖高皇帝肇開文運，科目取士雖以文藝，而學校教人必先德行，盖與舜之命司徒以敷
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

Heaven above purely blesses our August Ming, and the fortune of literary culture has grandly flourished. Now, in the seventh year of the Chenghua reign (1471), the year falls due for the ceremonial recommendation of the worthy and capable. The Regional Inspector of Zhejiang and Investigating Censor, Guo Rui 郭瑞, together with the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, in advance courteously invited Confucian scholars and gentry to take charge of the examinations. When the appointed time arrived, they gathered the scholars of the eleven prefectures and tested them in three sessions in all, selecting the ninety most outstanding among them, in compliance with the fixed quota. Having ranked their names in order, they further collected those of their essays that were pure and refined to compile this record, which is about to be presented to the Throne. All said that I, [Wang] Xiang 襄, ought to write a postface at its end.

I reverently reflect that when the Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu 太祖), first opened the fortune of literary culture, although the recruitment of scholars through the examination system was based on literary arts, the instruction of men in schools always put moral conduct first; indeed, just as Shun commanded the Minister of Education (situ 司徒) to propagate …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
五敎命典樂以敎胄子同一
揆也
列聖相承率由是道
皇上嗣位益篤前烈既
勅憲臣提督內外學校復命禮
部申示敎條皆先德行而後
文藝凡師之所以敎弟子之
===
所以學涵育陶鎔無非所以

君子以成德為行，日可見之行也。潜之為言也，隱而未見，行而未成，是以君子弗用也。君子學以聚之，問以辨之，寬以居之，仁以行之。《易》曰：「見龍在田，利見大人。」君德也。
「用見大人，勿恤」，有慶也。「南征吉」，志行也。
夫《易》開物成務，冒天下之道，如斯而已者也。是故聖人以通天下之志，以定天下之業，以斷天下之疑。是故蓍之德員而神，卦之德方以知，六爻之義易以貢。聖人以此洗心，退藏於密。

If indeed he loves the good, then everyone within the Four Seas will think nothing of traveling a thousand li to come and tell him what is good.”

Classic of Changes (Yi)

The noble man takes perfected virtue as his conduct, conduct that can be seen day by day. What is meant by “submerged” is that he is in hiding and not yet visible, and his conduct is not yet perfected; therefore the noble man does not act. The noble man learns in order to gather it, questions in order to discern it, dwells in it with寬magnanimity, and practices it with benevolence. The Changes says: “The dragon appears in the field; it is advantageous to see the great man.” This refers to the virtue of a ruler.

“Proceed to see the great man; do not worry”—there will be cause for celebration. “Going south brings good fortune”—one’s aspirations are carried out.

Now the Changes opens up things, accomplishes affairs, and encompasses all the ways under heaven—this and nothing more. Therefore the sages used it to penetrate the aspirations of all under heaven, to establish the enterprises of all under heaven, and to resolve the doubts of all under heaven. Thus the virtue of the yarrow stalks is round and numinous; the virtue of the hexagrams is square and wise; the meanings of the six lines change in order to present information. With these the sages cleansed their minds and withdrew into secrecy.

Yin and yang combine their virtues, while the firm and the yielding have their forms, thereby embodying the works of Heaven and Earth and penetrating the virtues of the numinous and bright. Its naming of things is varied yet does not overstep.

四海之内，咸仰朕德，時乃風。股肱惟人，良臣惟聖。昔先正保衡，作我先王，乃曰：「予弗克俾厥后惟堯舜，其心愧恥，若撻于市。」一夫不獲，則曰：「時予之辜。」佑我烈祖，格于皇天。爾尚明保予，罔俾阿衡專美有商。

When I think of him, my mind is on him; when I let go of him, my mind is still on him. When I speak of him, my mind is on him; what sincerely comes forth from me is on him.

Within the four seas, all look up to my virtue; this is your transforming influence. As legs and arms make the man, so does a good minister make the sage-king. Formerly, the former worthy Protector and Sustainer (Baoheng, i.e., Yi Yin) raised up our former king and said: "If I cannot make my sovereign like Yao and Shun, my heart feels ashamed, as if beaten in the marketplace." If a single man did not find his place, he would say: "This is my fault." He assisted our illustrious ancestor so that his virtue reached August Heaven. May you brilliantly protect and assist me, and do not let Aheng (Yi Yin) monopolize the glory in the house of Shang!

I for my part will be untiring in the work of tranquilization; do you, Duke, not relax your example, so that the four quarters may enjoy our rule for generations. The Duke of Zhou bowed with his hands to his head and his head to the ground, saying: "The King has commanded me to come, to inherit and protect the people for whom your accomplished grandfather received the Mandate, and to glorify your illustrious father King Wu; I will enlarge my reverent care."

By discerning observation and adherence to the laws, examine into cases with care and carry them through.

楚子、蔡侯次于厥貉。文公十年。公如晉。衛侯會公于沓。公還自晉，鄭伯會公于棐。文公十三年。公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城。文公十四年。叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚屈建、蔡公孫歸生、衛石惡、陳孔奐、鄭良霄、許人、曹人于宋。豹及諸侯之大夫盟于宋。襄公二十七年。楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、鄭伯、許男、徐子、滕子、頓子、胡子、沈子、小邾子、宋世子佐、淮夷會于申。楚子、蔡侯、陳侯、許男、頓子、胡子、沈子、淮夷伐吳。昭公四年。
禮記
天地始肅，不可以贏。

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
及夫禮樂之極乎天而蟠乎地行乎陰陽
而通乎鬼神窮高極遠而測深厚樂
著太始而禮居成物著不息者天也
著不動者地也一動一靜者天地之
間也故聖人曰禮樂云
百日之蜡一日之澤非爾所知也張而不
弛文武弗能也
君子不盡利以遺民
第貳場
===
論
君道稽古正學
詔誥表内科一道
擬漢宣帝下學講五經同異詔甘露三年
擬唐以宋璟為西京留守誥開元四年
擬進
大明一統志表
判語五條
官文書稽程
punctuated:
「及夫禮樂之極乎天而蟠乎地，行乎陰陽而通乎鬼神，窮高極遠而測深厚。樂著太始，而禮居成物。著不息者，天也；著不動者，地也；一動一靜者，天地之間也。故聖人曰：禮樂云。」
「百日之蜡，一日之澤，非爾所知也。張而不弛，文武弗能也。」
「君子不盡利以遺民。」

第貳場
論：
「君道稽古正學」

詔、誥、表内科一道：
擬漢宣帝下學講五經同異詔〔甘露三年〕
擬唐以宋璟為西京留守誥〔開元四年〕
擬進《大明一統志》表

判語五條：
官文書稽程
translation_en:
"When it comes to ritual and music reaching to the heights of Heaven and coiling through the Earth, operating through yin and yang and communicating with spirits and gods, exhausting the highest and furthest and plumbing the deepest and thickest: music manifests the Great Beginning, while ritual resides in completed things. That which manifests ceaselessness is Heaven; that which manifests immobility is Earth; that which alternates between movement and stillness is what lies between Heaven and Earth. Therefore the sages spoke of 'ritual and music.'"
"The labor of a hundred days for the zha festival brings the bounty of a single day's celebration—this is not something you would understand. To keep the bowstring taut and never relax it is something that even King Wen and King Wu could not do."
"The gentleman does not exhaust all profit, so as to leave some behind for the common people."

Second Session
Discourse:
"The Way of the Ruler: Examining Antiquity for Orthodox Learning"

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
出使不復命
不操練軍士
因公擅科斂
造作不如法
第叁場
策五道
問書曰惟皇上帝降衷于下民若有恒性
克綏厥猷惟后是言人性本善而修道
立教使之各安其道以復於善則賴乎
===
君也粤稽諸古為君而道民於善克盡
綏猷之責者堯舜湯武也其所以道之
之術可得而言歟後世有親書孝經於
碑陰者有親書孟子於屏障者何君亦
可以道民於善歟欽惟
太祖高皇帝條成大誥三編昭示天下固有以
感發人之善心而克綏厥猷與堯舜湯
武同一揆矣其所以道民之要亦可得
而言歟
punctuated:
出使不復命。
不操練軍士。
因公擅科斂。
造作不如法。

第叁場
策五道

問：《書》曰：「惟皇上帝，降衷于下民。若有恒性，克綏厥猷惟后。」是言人性本善，而修道立教，使之各安其道以復於善，則賴乎君也。粤稽諸古，為君而道民於善，克盡綏猷之責者，堯、舜、湯、武也，其所以道之之術，可得而言歟？後世有親書《孝經》於碑陰者，有親書《孟子》於屏障者，何君？亦可以道民於善歟？欽惟太祖高皇帝條成《大誥》三編，昭示天下，固有以感發人之善心，而克綏厥猷，與堯、舜、湯、武同一揆矣，其所以道民之要，亦可得而言歟？

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
太宗文皇帝為善陰隲孝順事實二書拳拳勸
人為善行孝而申之以報應之理其感
人尤切然為善行孝而獲報者可詳其
人歟
宣宗章皇帝五倫一書備著人倫之道而各舉
其善行亦有盡善而獲報者亦可言其
人歟
二聖製作皆推廣
聖祖道民為善之意而盡夫克綏猷之責者也
===
而四書之旨果皆同條而共貫歟堯舜
湯武之道載於書我
列聖之立言垂訓其亦與書典謨訓誥誓命之
文相為表裏歟諸生服膺
聖訓有年願明言以對
問小學大學皆聖賢教人之法也其道一
而已小學一書有內篇有外篇何者為
內何者為外首之以立教而所教者何
事次之以明倫而釐為幾條次之以敬
punctuated:
太宗文皇帝《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書，拳拳勸人為善行孝，而申之以報應之理，其感人尤切。然為善行孝而獲報者，可詳其人歟？宣宗章皇帝《五倫》一書，備著人倫之道，而各舉其善行，亦有盡善而獲報者，亦可言其人歟？二聖製作，皆推廣聖祖道民為善之意，而盡夫克綏猷之責者也。而四書之旨，果皆同條而共貫歟？堯、舜、湯、武之道載於《書》，我列聖之立言垂訓，其亦與《書》典、謨、訓、誥、誓、命之文相為表裏歟？諸生服膺聖訓有年，願明言以對。
問：小學、大學，皆聖賢教人之法也，其道一而已。《小學》一書，有內篇，有外篇，何者為內？何者為外？首之以〈立教〉，而所教者何事？次之以〈明倫〉，而釐為幾條？次之以〈敬
translation_en:
The two books by Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor [the Yongle Emperor]—Secret Merits of Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Examples of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi)—earnestly exhort people to do good and practice filial piety, and reinforce this with the principle of moral retribution, moving people all the more deeply. Yet as for those who did good and practiced filial piety and received recompense, can those individuals be recounted in detail? The book on the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) by Emperor Zhang, the Proclaiming Ancestor [the Xuande Emperor], fully sets forth the Way of human relationships and cites good deeds under each; there are also those who achieved perfection in goodness and received recompense—can those individuals likewise be spoken of? The compositions of these two sage emperors both expand upon the Sacred Ancestor's [the Hongwu Emperor's] intention of guiding the people to do good, thereby fulfilling the responsibility of being able to tranquilly guide them in the moral way. And do the purports of these four books indeed all belong to the same framework and share a single thread? The Way of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu is recorded in the Book of Documents (Shu); do the established words and bequeathed instructions of our successive sage emperors also form the exterior and interior counterparts to the texts of the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, Announcements, Oaths, and Commands in the Book of Documents? You students have cherished the imperial instructions in your hearts for years; I hope you will speak clearly in reply.

Question: Lesser Learning and Greater Learning are both methods by which the sages and worthies taught people; their Way is simply one. The book Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) has Inner Chapters and Outer Chapters: which are the Inner, and which are the Outer? It begins with "Establishing Instruction" (Lijiao)—what matters are taught therein? Next comes "Clarifying Human Relationships" (Minglun)—into how many items is it divided? Next comes "Revering [the Body]…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
身而分為幾類次之以稽古而所稽者
何代之迹述嘉言以廣之紀善行以實
之而所廣所實之綱目亦可指言歟先
儒於是書也有言其綱目甚好者有敬
之如神明者其人可得而聞歟大學一
書外有三綱領而有所謂綱領中之
綱領者内有八條目而又謂有一言而
可以該體用之全者果何在歟傳者既
釋三綱領而外又有本末章傳者於他
===
章皆以二事相承獨誠意自為一章又
何歟先儒於是書也有言止於正心誠
意而無所謂格物致知者有條輯是書
而進講于君前而動以誠意為言者其
人又可得而聞之歟且二書之要抑可
一言以蔽之歟諸士子由小學而進於
大學皆盈耳而充腹者也請詳著于篇
問國以賢而治賢以薦而升薦舉之法不
可不講也古人有内舉不避親外舉不
punctuated:
身，而分為幾類？次之以稽古，而所稽者何代之迹？述嘉言以廣之，紀善行以實之，而所廣所實之綱目亦可指言歟？先儒於是書也，有言其綱目甚好者，有敬之如神明者，其人可得而聞歟？《大學》一書，外有三綱領，而有所謂「綱領中之綱領」者；内有八條目，而又謂有「一言而可以該體用之全」者，果何在歟？傳者既釋三綱領，而外又有「本末」章；傳者於他章皆以二事相承，獨「誠意」自為一章，又何歟？先儒於是書也，有言止於正心、誠意而無所謂格物、致知者，有條輯是書而進講于君前，而動以誠意為言者，其人又可得而聞之歟？且二書之要，抑可一言以蔽之歟？諸士子由《小學》而進於《大學》，皆盈耳而充腹者也，請詳著于篇。
問：國以賢而治，賢以薦而升，薦舉之法不可不講也。古人有「内舉不避親，外舉不
translation_en:
… Reverencing the Person (Jingshen), and into how many categories is it divided? Next comes Investigating the Past (Jigu)—traces of which dynasties are investigated? It recounts Noble Words (Jiayan) to broaden them, and records Good Deeds (Shanxing) to substantiate them—can the main headings and sub-items of what is broadened and substantiated also be pointed out and stated? Regarding this book, among former Confucians there was one who said its main headings and sub-items are excellent, and another who revered it like the gods—may we hear who those men were? As for the book Great Learning (Daxue), externally it has the Three Guiding Principles, and yet there is what is called "the guiding principle within the guiding principles"; internally it has the Eight Steps, and yet it is also said that there is "a single word that can encompass the entirety of substance and function"—where, indeed, are these to be found? After the commentator explained the Three Guiding Principles, why is there also a chapter on "Root and Branch" outside of them? In the other chapters, the commentator always links two matters in sequence; why does "Making the Intentions Sincere" alone form a chapter by itself? Regarding this book, among former Confucians there was one who spoke only as far as rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere without mentioning investigating things and extending knowledge, and another who compiled and arranged this book to lecture on it before the ruler, constantly speaking of making the intentions sincere—may we also hear who those men were? Moreover, can the essentials of these two books be summed up in a single word? All you scholars have advanced from the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) to the Great Learning; these are things that fill your ears and satisfy your minds—please set them forth in detail in your essays.

Question: A state is governed through worthy men, and worthy men rise through recommendation; the method of recommendation and promotion cannot go unexamined. Among the ancients, there were those who "in recommending from within did not avoid relatives, and in recommending from outside did not…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
避讐者可得聞歟漢唐宋之臣若袁盎
丙吉張說蕭嵩司馬光吕文靖之徒皆
有所薦其所薦之人與其所以得薦之
實亦可得而知歟慶曆中有薦者三十
餘人至和中有薦者二十四人又有薦
其親弟薦其同巳者果無媿於古歟有
謂我為相無能但有一能善用人吾輔
政何功惟薦二臺官無愧又有身為諫
議未嘗妄薦一人官居執政不敢私薦
===
一士者皆可知其人歟方今
聖皇馭極賢路大開然山林泉石之間百司庶
府之廣豈無遺逸淹滯者歟伊欲上不
蔽賢下無遺賢果何道而致薦舉之公
歟諸生應賓興而來必有能言之者
問三代而後文章之專門名家者不為不
多也說者謂晋無文章惟歸去來辭一
篇而已唐無文章惟送李愿歸盤谷序
一篇而已果何所見而謂其然歟孔明
punctuated:
避讐者，可得聞歟？漢、唐、宋之臣，若袁盎、丙吉、張說、蕭嵩、司馬光、吕文靖之徒，皆有所薦；其所薦之人，與其所以得薦之實，亦可得而知歟？慶曆中有薦者三十餘人，至和中有薦者二十四人，又有薦其親弟、薦其同巳者，果無媿於古歟？有謂「我為相無能，但有一能善用人」，「吾輔政何功，惟薦二臺官無愧」；又有身為諫議，未嘗妄薦一人；官居執政，不敢私薦一士者，皆可知其人歟？方今聖皇馭極，賢路大開，然山林泉石之間、百司庶府之廣，豈無遺逸淹滯者歟？伊欲上不蔽賢，下無遺賢，果何道而致薦舉之公歟？諸生應賓興而來，必有能言之者。

問：三代而後，文章之專門名家者，不為不多也。說者謂晉無文章，惟《歸去來辭》一篇而已；唐無文章，惟《送李愿歸盤谷序》一篇而已。果何所見而謂其然歟？孔明
translation_en:
…refrain from recommending their personal enemies—can we hear about them? Ministers of the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties—such as Yuan Ang 袁盎, Bing Ji 丙吉, Zhang Yue 張說, Xiao Song 蕭嵩, Sima Guang 司馬光, and Lü Wenjing 吕文靖 (Lü Yijian 呂夷簡)—all made recommendations; can the people they recommended and the actual circumstances by which they came to be recommended also be known? During the Qingli 慶曆 era (1041–1048), there was someone who recommended more than thirty men, and during the Zhihe 至和 era (1054–1056), there was someone who recommended twenty-four men; there were also those who recommended their own younger brothers or recommended those who shared their views—did they truly have nothing to be ashamed of before the ancients? There was one who said, "As Grand Councilor, I have no other ability, save the one ability of being good at employing men," and another who said, "What merit have I in assisting the government? Only in recommending two Censorate officials am I without shame." There was also one who, while serving as Policy Critic, never recklessly recommended a single person, and one who, while holding office as a grand councilor, dared not privately recommend a single scholar—can all of these men be identified? At the present time, our Sacred Emperor reigns on the throne, and the pathway for the worthy is wide open. Yet amid the mountains, forests, springs, and rocks, or across the breadth of the hundred bureaus and multitudinous offices, how could there be none who are overlooked in retirement or held back in obscurity? If we wish those above not to block the worthy and those below to leave no worthy man behind, by what way indeed can impartiality in recommendations be achieved? You students have come in response to the call to present the worthy; surely you are able to speak on this.

Question: Since the Three Dynasties, specialists and renowned masters of literary composition have been far from few. Commentators have said that the Jin dynasty had no literature except the single piece "Rhapsody on Returning Home" (Guiqulai ci 歸去來辭), and that the Tang dynasty had no literature except the single piece "Preface Sending Off Li Yuan on His Return to Pan Valley" (Song Li Yuan gui Pangu xu 送李愿歸盤谷序). On what insight did they base such claims? Kongming's 孔明 (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮)…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
出師一表何以謂其與伊訓說命相表
裏杜工部平生詩集何以謂其有三百
篇之旨若捕龍蛇搏虎豹急與之角而
不暇者誰之文歟軋漢周而凌晉宋凛
然為一王之法者又誰之文歟其文如
此其學豈無所自歟讀其文如遊帝舜
之庭而聆簫韶之樂者誰歟讀其文如
駕千里之駒而御以王良造父者又誰
歟其文如此可各舉其一篇以例其他
===
歟外此又有制誥之文得六經簡嚴之
體者記述之文得六經紀實之旨者奏
議之文得伊訓召誥之意者詩章之文
得周雅商頌之體者又有進士之文不
可以科舉輕視者序述之文不可以序
體槩論者其文可悉數歟諸生學古為
文者也試為我評之
問無所不通之謂儒識時務者在俊傑天
下之務可言者多矣姑以浙之切務論
punctuated:
《出師》一表，何以謂其與《伊訓》、《說命》相表裏？杜工部平生詩集，何以謂其有《三百篇》之旨？若捕龍蛇、搏虎豹，急與之角而不暇者，誰之文歟？軋漢周而凌晉宋，凛然為一王之法者，又誰之文歟？其文如此，其學豈無所自歟？讀其文如遊帝舜之庭而聆《簫韶》之樂者，誰歟？讀其文如駕千里之駒而御以王良、造父者，又誰歟？其文如此，可各舉其一篇以例其他歟？外此，又有制誥之文得六經簡嚴之體者，記述之文得六經紀實之旨者，奏議之文得《伊訓》、《召誥》之意者，詩章之文得《周雅》、《商頌》之體者；又有進士之文不可以科舉輕視者，序述之文不可以序體槩論者，其文可悉數歟？諸生學古為文者也，試為我評之。

問：無所不通之謂儒，識時務者在俊傑。天下之務可言者多矣，姑以浙之切務論
translation_en:
… single "Memorial on Dispatching the Troops" (Chushi biao 出師表)—why is it said to stand as outer and inner counterparts to the "Instructions of Yi" (Yi xun 伊訓) and the "Charge to Yue" (Yue ming 說命)? And the lifelong poetry collection of Du of the Ministry of Works (Du Fu 杜甫)—why is it said to possess the purport of the Three Hundred Poems (Book of Odes)? Whose prose is like catching dragons and serpents or wrestling tigers and leopards, urgently locking horns with them without a moment's respite? And whose prose crushes Han and Zhou, towers over Jin and Song, and awe-inspiringly serves as the standard of a true king? Since their writings are like this, how could their learning lack an origin? Who is it whose prose, when read, is like roaming the court of Emperor Shun and listening to the Xiaoshao 簫韶 music? And who is it whose prose, when read, is like driving a thousand-li colt with Wang Liang 王良 and Zao Fu 造父 at the reins? Since their writings are like this, can you cite one piece by each to exemplify the rest? Beyond these, there are also imperial decrees and mandates whose prose attains the concise and austere style of the Six Classics; descriptive and historical accounts whose prose attains the factual purport of the Six Classics; memorials and deliberations whose prose attains the meaning of the "Instructions of Yi" and the "Announcement of Shao" (Shao gao 召誥); and poetic compositions whose prose attains the form of the "Odes of Zhou" (Zhou ya 周雅) and the "Hymns of Shang" (Shang song 商頌). There are also writings of metropolitan graduates (jinshi) that cannot be lightly dismissed as mere examination essays, and prefaces and expositions that cannot be generalized merely by the form of prefaces—can all of these writings be enumerated in full? You students study antiquity in order to compose literature; try to evaluate them for me.

Question: To be conversant with everything is what is called a Confucian scholar (ru 儒); understanding the affairs of the times lies with men of outstanding talent. Among the affairs of the realm there is much that could be spoken of, but let us for the moment discuss the urgent affairs of Zhejiang…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之守令所以牧民也比年行黜罰之典
矣而繼来者猶乏廉潔之士将校所以
領軍也近歲行推選之法矣而新任者
尚欠撫馭之才民風宜淳古也而刁訟
者日滋民俗宜節儉也而奢侈者益甚
浙西之地多卑下遇雨連旬彌漫百里
無由疏泄浙東之地多高仰遇旱彌月
赤地千里無以灌溉儲蓄所當廣也今
郡邑倉廩尚多空虛而仰給於官者道
===
路相望賦役欲其平也今閭閻小民尚
多貧乏而橫斂於鄉者項背相接之數
者皆為政者所欲急聞而變通之也兹
欲守令皆秉廉潔之操将校咸有撫馭
之才刁風禁而侈俗革水利興而災荒
備儲蓄廣而賦役均将何法以處之諸
士子生長於斯耳聞而講之熟矣願詳
著于篇以俟觀風者采焉
punctuated: 之：守令所以牧民也，比年行黜罰之典矣，而繼来者猶乏廉潔之士；将校所以領軍也，近歲行推選之法矣，而新任者尚欠撫馭之才。民風宜淳古也，而刁訟者日滋；民俗宜節儉也，而奢侈者益甚。浙西之地多卑下，遇雨連旬，彌漫百里，無由疏泄；浙東之地多高仰，遇旱彌月，赤地千里，無以灌溉。儲蓄所當廣也，今郡邑倉廩尚多空虛，而仰給於官者道路相望；賦役欲其平也，今閭閻小民尚多貧乏，而橫斂於鄉者項背相接。之數者，皆為政者所欲急聞而變通之也。兹欲守令皆秉廉潔之操，将校咸有撫馭之才，刁風禁而侈俗革，水利興而災荒備，儲蓄廣而賦役均，将何法以處之？諸士子生長於斯，耳聞而講之熟矣，願詳著于篇，以俟觀風者采焉。
translation_en: … them. Prefectural and county magistrates are those by whom the people are shepherded; in recent years, regulations for dismissal and punishment have been enforced, yet those who follow in office still lack men of incorruptible integrity. Military officers are those by whom the troops are commanded; in recent years, methods of recommendation and selection have been implemented, yet those newly appointed still lack the talent to pacify and control. Popular morals ought to be simple and ancient, yet perverse litigants multiply daily; popular customs ought to be frugal, yet extravagance grows ever more extreme. The land of Western Zhejiang is mostly low-lying; when rain falls for weeks on end, floodwaters spread over a hundred li with no means of drainage. The land of Eastern Zhejiang is mostly high and elevated; when drought lasts for a full month, the parched earth stretches for a thousand li with no means of irrigation. Grain reserves ought to be expanded, yet today the granaries of prefectures and counties are still mostly empty, while those who depend on the government for relief look upon one another all along the roads. Taxes and corvée labor are desired to be equitable, yet today the common people in the villages are still mostly impoverished, while those who impose arbitrary levies in the countryside follow closely on one another's heels. These several matters are all things that those who govern urgently wish to hear about and adapt to through reform. If we now wish for prefectural and county magistrates all to uphold incorruptible integrity, for military officers all to possess the talent to pacify and control, for perverse tendencies to be prohibited and extravagant customs reformed, for waterworks to be promoted and preparations made against natural disasters and famine, and for grain reserves to be expanded and taxes and corvée equalized—by what methods shall we manage this? You gentlemen were born and raised in this region; you have heard of these matters with your own ears and discussed them thoroughly. I hope you will set them forth in detail in your essays, awaiting selection by those who observe the local customs.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之為仁也盖仁無往而不在也苟隨所寓而不
違乎理則仁豈外是哉昔聖人因樊遲之問仁
而告之意謂天體物而不遺仁體事而無不在
是故居處謂幽獨之處未應乎事也恭不見於
外則怠惰放肆而欲得以間理非所以為仁也
要必容貌端莊威儀儼恪則私意不容而居處
得乎仁矣執事謂應事之際未涉乎人也敬不
主於中則轇轕紛紜而私得以害公亦非所以
為仁也要必戰兢自持主一無適則此心不放
===
而執事得乎仁矣至若與人則與物接矣與人
不忠則偽得以間誠又豈所以為仁哉必也發
己自盡而表裏如一誠實不欺而物我無間則
天理流行於與人之時仁豈不在是乎故曰随
其身之所寓盡乎理之當然此聖人教賢者之
為仁也抑考聖人荅樊遲問仁者三而此最先
下文又言之夷狄不可棄勉其固守而勿失也
然此雖為樊遲告而聖人之言貫徹上下初無
二理自始學至成德希聖希賢皆不出此先儒
punctuated: 之為仁也。盖仁無往而不在也，苟隨所寓而不違乎理，則仁豈外是哉？昔聖人因樊遲之問仁而告之，意謂天體物而不遺，仁體事而無不在。是故居處，謂幽獨之處，未應乎事也。恭不見於外，則怠惰放肆，而欲得以間理，非所以為仁也；要必容貌端莊，威儀儼恪，則私意不容，而居處得乎仁矣。執事，謂應事之際，未涉乎人也。敬不主於中，則轇轕紛紜，而私得以害公，亦非所以為仁也；要必戰兢自持，主一無適，則此心不放，而執事得乎仁矣。至若與人，則與物接矣。與人不忠，則偽得以間誠，又豈所以為仁哉？必也發己自盡而表裏如一，誠實不欺而物我無間，則天理流行於與人之時，仁豈不在是乎？故曰：随其身之所寓，盡乎理之當然，此聖人教賢者之為仁也。抑考聖人荅樊遲問仁者三，而此最先，下文又言「之夷狄不可棄」，勉其固守而勿失也。然此雖為樊遲告，而聖人之言貫徹上下，初無二理，自始學至成德，希聖希賢，皆不出此。先儒
translation_en: … to practice humaneness. For humaneness is present everywhere; if one conforms to wherever one finds oneself without violating principle, then how could humaneness lie outside of this? In the past, when the Sage answered Fan Chi's question about humaneness, his meaning was that just as Heaven embodies all things without leaving anything out, humaneness embodies all affairs and is nowhere absent. Therefore, "dwelling in retirement" refers to being in seclusion and solitude, before one has responded to affairs. If deferential demeanor is not manifested on the outside, one becomes lazy and unrestrained, allowing selfish desires to disrupt principle; this is not the way to practice humaneness. One must ensure that one's countenance is dignified and one's bearing is grave and respectful; then selfish intentions will find no room, and in dwelling in retirement one will attain humaneness. "Handling affairs" refers to the moment of responding to affairs, before one has interacted with other people. If reverence does not preside within, one becomes entangled and confused, allowing selfishness to harm the public good; this too is not the way to practice humaneness. One must maintain oneself with cautious trepidation and hold to single-minded concentration without straying; then this mind will not be lost, and in handling affairs one will attain humaneness. As for "dealing with others," one is then in contact with the world. If in dealing with others one is not loyal, falsehood can disrupt sincerity; how then could that be the way to practice humaneness? Surely, if in putting oneself forth one does one's utmost so that outside and inside are as one, being sincere and without deceit so that there is no barrier between others and oneself, then Heavenly principle will flow freely when dealing with others—how could humaneness not reside right here? Therefore it is said: following wherever one's person is situated and fulfilling the natural principle of what ought to be—this is how the Sage taught the worthy to practice humaneness. Moreover, if we examine the three occasions on which the Sage answered Fan Chi's questions about humaneness, this one came first; and in the text that follows he further says that "even if one goes among the Yi and Di tribes, these may not be abandoned," urging him to hold fast to them and not lose them. Yet although this was spoken to Fan Chi, the Sage's words penetrate both above and below without any duality of principle. From the beginning of learning to the completion of virtue, aspiring to become a sage or a worthy—none of it goes beyond this. A former Confucian scholar …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
謂充之則睟面盎背推而達之則篤恭而天下
平學者可不勉哉
今天下車同軌書同文行同倫雖有其位
苟無其德不敢作禮樂焉雖有其德苟無
其位亦不敢作禮樂焉子曰吾說夏禮杞
不足徵也吾學殷禮有宋存焉吾學周禮
今用之吾從周
司馬堙
同考試官敎授劉批此篇融會傳註始終以
===
時王之制立說深合題意非他卷所及宜表而出之
考試官敎授劉批析理詳明可取
考試官敎授鄭批發明為下不倍之意明白可觀
大賢言時制一統也既申言有德位斯可任制
作之事復引言雖大聖亦必遵時王之制蓋時
制大同固見天下一統也然非德位兼備固不
敢作禮樂而孔子雖聖亦豈得不遵時制哉昔
子思子論為下不倍之意謂夫周為天下共主
自文武以来王制大同由今日觀之以車則轍
punctuated:
謂「充之則睟面盎背，推而達之則篤恭而天下平」，學者可不勉哉？

「今天下車同軌，書同文，行同倫。雖有其位，苟無其德，不敢作禮樂焉；雖有其德，苟無其位，亦不敢作禮樂焉。子曰：『吾說夏禮，杞不足徵也；吾學殷禮，有宋存焉；吾學周禮，今用之，吾從周。』」
司馬堙
同考試官敎授劉批：此篇融會傳註，始終以時王之制立說，深合題意，非他卷所及，宜表而出之。
考試官敎授劉批：析理詳明，可取。
考試官敎授鄭批：發明「為下不倍」之意，明白可觀。

大賢言時制一統也，既申言有德位斯可任制作之事，復引言雖大聖亦必遵時王之制。蓋時制大同，固見天下一統也；然非德位兼備，固不敢作禮樂，而孔子雖聖，亦豈得不遵時制哉？昔子思子論「為下不倍」之意，謂夫周為天下共主，自文、武以来，王制大同。由今日觀之，以車則轍
translation_en:
…said that "when one fills it out, it appears as a mild harmony in the countenance and a rich fullness in the back; when one extends and carries it out, through earnest reverence the whole world is brought to peace." How could learners not exert themselves!

"Now throughout the world, carriages have wheel-axles of the same width, books are written in the same script, and conduct follows the same ethical norms. Even if one holds the position, if he lacks the virtue, he does not dare to institute rites and music; even if one possesses the virtue, if he lacks the position, he likewise does not dare to institute rites and music. The Master said: 'I can speak of the rites of the Xia, but the state of Qi does not provide sufficient attestation; I have studied the rites of the Yin, and they survive in the state of Song; I have studied the rites of the Zhou, which are now in use—I follow the Zhou.'"

Sima Yin 司馬堙.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: This essay thoroughly integrates the commentaries and annotations, building its argument from beginning to end upon the institutions of the reigning king. It deeply accords with the meaning of the theme, is unmatched by other papers, and ought to be singled out for publication.
Examiner and Instructor Liu 劉 comments: Its analysis of principle is detailed and clear; worthy of selection.
Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: It elucidates the meaning of "occupying a subordinate position and not rebelling" with clarity worth admiring.

When the Great Worthy speaks of the unification of contemporary institutions, he first explains at length that only when one possesses both virtue and position can one undertake the task of creating institutions, and then quotes words to show that even a Great Sage must abide by the institutions of the reigning king. Indeed, the great uniformity of contemporary institutions certainly shows that the world is unified; yet unless one combines both virtue and position, one certainly does not dare to institute rites and music—and although Confucius was a sage, how could he fail to abide by contemporary institutions? Of old, Master Zisi 子思子, in discussing the meaning of "occupying a subordinate position and not rebelling," said that since the Zhou became the common sovereign of the world, from the time of Kings Wen and Wu onward, the royal institutions have been in great uniformity. Viewed from the present day, with regard to carriages, the ruts…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
迹廣狹如一而車同軌也以書則聲音點畫如
一而書同文也以至貴賤親疎相接之體又無
或異豈非行同倫乎三者皆同則天下一統而
無有自用自專反古者矣然此皆我周盛時有
聖人在天子之位制禮作樂垂法至今也彼有
君之位無聖之德則無徵不信不敢作禮樂焉
苟欲作之是愚而自用如禮樂何有聖之德無
君之位則不尊不信不敢作禮樂焉苟欲作之
是賤而自專如禮樂何夫德位不備固不敢作
===
禮樂然則孔子有德無位亦豈敢自專哉故又
引孔子言夏禮吾能言之杞為夏後文獻不足
無可考證之實焉殷禮吾嘗學之宋為殷後文
獻雖存又非當世之法焉惟周禮乃時王之制
實今日所用既生斯世則當遵之而不違既為
斯民則當從之而不倍豈敢反古道而從夏商
哉抑考此章子思承上章為下不倍而言上文
既引孔子言自用自專居今反古之烖必逮身
矣又言非天子不議禮制度考文矣而此又以
punctuated: 迹廣狹如一，而車同軌也；以書則聲音點畫如一，而書同文也；以至貴賤親疎相接之體又無或異，豈非行同倫乎？三者皆同，則天下一統，而無有自用、自專、反古者矣。然此皆我周盛時，有聖人在天子之位，制禮作樂，垂法至今也。彼有君之位，無聖之德，則無徵不信，不敢作禮樂焉；苟欲作之，是愚而自用，如禮樂何？有聖之德，無君之位，則不尊不信，不敢作禮樂焉；苟欲作之，是賤而自專，如禮樂何？夫德位不備，固不敢作禮樂；然則孔子有德無位，亦豈敢自專哉？故又引孔子言：「夏禮吾能言之，杞為夏後，文獻不足，無可考證之實焉。殷禮吾嘗學之，宋為殷後，文獻雖存，又非當世之法焉。惟周禮乃時王之制，實今日所用，既生斯世，則當遵之而不違；既為斯民，則當從之而不倍，豈敢反古道而從夏、商哉？」抑考此章，子思承上章「為下不倍」而言。上文既引孔子言自用、自專、居今反古之烖必逮身矣，又言非天子不議禮、制度、考文矣，而此又以
translation_en:
…the breadth of the wheel-ruts is uniform, so carriages have the same axle-width; as for writing, the sounds and brush-strokes are uniform, so books are written in the same characters; and as for the forms of intercourse between noble and base, near and distant kin, there is likewise no discrepancy—is this not conduct conforming to the same ethical norms? When all three are uniform, All-under-Heaven is united under one rule, and there is no one who acts on his own judgment, presumes on his own authority, or reverts to the ways of antiquity. Yet all this is because, in the flourishing era of our Zhou dynasty, there were sages occupying the position of Son of Heaven who instituted rites and created music, handing down standards that endure to this day.

If one holds the position of ruler without the virtue of a sage, then for lack of attestation he will not command belief and will not dare to create rites and music; were he to attempt to create them, that would be to act on his own judgment out of ignorance—what could he do with rites and music? If one possesses the virtue of a sage without the position of ruler, then for lack of exalted rank he will not command belief and will not dare to create rites and music; were he to attempt to create them, that would be to presume on his own authority from a lowly station—what could he do with rites and music?

Now, when virtue and position are not both present, one certainly does not dare to create rites and music; how, then, could Confucius, who possessed the virtue but lacked the position, dare to presume on his own authority? Therefore, the text goes on to quote Confucius as saying: "I can speak of the rites of the Xia, yet Qi, though the descendant of Xia, lacks sufficient records and worthy men, leaving no substantive evidence by which to verify them. I have studied the rites of the Yin, yet Song, though the descendant of Yin and still preserving its records and worthy men, no longer represents the institutions of the present age. Only the rites of the Zhou are the institutions of the reigning king and what is actually in use today. Having been born in this age, one ought to abide by them without transgression; being a subject of this people, one ought to follow them without rebellion. How could I dare revert to the ways of antiquity and follow the Xia or the Shang?"

Moreover, if we examine this chapter, Master Zisi is continuing the theme from the preceding chapter of "occupying a subordinate position without being rebellious." Above, he has already quoted Confucius as saying that calamity is sure to overtake the person of anyone who acts on his own judgment, presumes on his own authority, or lives in the present while reverting to the ways of antiquity, and he has further stated that none but the Son of Heaven deliberates on rites, fixes measures, or examines the written characters; and here again, with…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
是為言無非以明為下不倍之意而示人道之
標準也然學者誠能脩德凝道而於道之大小
無不體則凡身之所處無不宜豈直為下不倍
哉
樂正子強乎曰否有知慮乎曰否多聞識
乎曰否然則奚為喜而不寐曰其為人也
好善好善足乎曰好善優於天下而況魯
國乎夫苟好善則四海之內皆將輕千里
而來告之以善
===
李楠
同考試官教諭王批此篇能發明章旨組織
成文真傑作也宜置優選
同考試官教諭吳批此題頭緒頗多塲中作

觀大賢屢答門人之問同列見為政不在於用
一己之長而貴於來天下之善盖善取於己則
punctuated:
是為言，無非以明「為下不倍」之意，而示人道之標準也。然學者誠能脩德凝道，而於道之大小無不體，則凡身之所處無不宜，豈直「為下不倍」哉！

「樂正子強乎？」曰：「否。」「有知慮乎？」曰：「否。」「多聞識乎？」曰：「否。」「然則奚為喜而不寐？」曰：「其為人也好善。」「好善足乎？」曰：「好善優於天下，而況魯國乎？夫苟好善，則四海之內，皆將輕千里而來，告之以善。」

translation_en:
… speaks of this simply to clarify the meaning of "being in a subordinate position and not rebelling," thereby setting forth the standard of the human Way. Yet if a scholar can truly cultivate virtue and consolidate the Way, embodying the Way in both its great and small aspects without exception, then whatever situation he finds himself in will be appropriate—how could it merely be a matter of "being in a subordinate position and not rebelling"!

"Is Yuezhengzi a man of vigor?" "No." "Is he wise in counsel?" "No." "Is he of wide information?" "No." "Then why is it that you are so glad that you cannot sleep?" "He is a man who loves what is good." "Is the love of what is good sufficient?" "The love of what is good is more than a sufficient qualification for the government of the Empire, to say nothing of the state of Lu! If a minister sincerely loves what is good, all within the Four Seas will count a thousand li a trifle to come and tell him what is good."
By Li Nan 李楠.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有盡善取諸人則無窮公孫丑疑樂正子之為
政無所長孟子安得不稱其好善之大以荅之
哉昔樂正子善人也魯欲使之為政孟子喜其
道行公孫丑乃疑而問之曰世之所尚者強而
有勇力也知而能慮事也多聞識於前言往行
也夫子聞樂正子為政而喜以其強而有勇力
乎知而能慮事乎抑以其多聞識於前言往行
乎丑屢問而孟子皆荅之曰否者不然之詞以
見三者皆樂正子之所短而為政不在於用一
===
己之所長也丑未達孟子所喜之由又有奚為
喜而不寐之問則告以其為人也好善焉丑又
疑好善不足以為政而有好善足乎之問則又
告以好善優於天下焉誠以善者天下之公理
好善者為政之先務能好夫善則能虛心求道
雖天下之大治之尚有餘力曾謂魯國之小而
不足以為治乎誠好夫善則能舍己從人雖四
海之遠人將不以為難而來告我以善況於國
中之近而有不樂告以善道乎天下之善言至
punctuated: 有盡，善取諸人則無窮。公孫丑疑樂正子之為政無所長，孟子安得不稱其好善之大以荅之哉？昔樂正子，善人也。魯欲使之為政，孟子喜其道行。公孫丑乃疑而問之曰：「世之所尚者，強而有勇力也，知而能慮事也，多聞識於前言往行也。夫子聞樂正子為政而喜，以其強而有勇力乎？知而能慮事乎？抑以其多聞識於前言往行乎？」丑屢問，而孟子皆荅之曰「否」者，不然之詞，以見三者皆樂正子之所短，而為政不在於用一己之所長也。丑未達孟子所喜之由，又有「奚為喜而不寐」之問，則告以「其為人也好善」焉。丑又疑好善不足以為政，而有「好善足乎」之問，則又告以「好善優於天下」焉。誠以善者，天下之公理；好善者，為政之先務。能好夫善，則能虛心求道，雖天下之大，治之尚有餘力，曾謂魯國之小，而不足以為治乎？誠好夫善，則能舍己從人，雖四海之遠，人將不以為難，而來告我以善，況於國中之近，而有不樂告以善道乎？天下之善言至，
translation_en: … has a limit, whereas drawing goodness from others is inexhaustible. When Gongsun Chou 公孫丑 doubted that Yuezhengzi 樂正子 had any particular strengths for governing, how could Mencius 孟子 not praise the greatness of his love of goodness in reply? In the past, Yuezhengzi was a good man. The state of Lu 魯 wished to employ him in governance, and Mencius rejoiced that his Way would be put into practice. Gongsun Chou, however, was doubtful and asked him: "What the world values is being strong and possessing courage and vigor, being wise and able to deliberate on affairs, and having wide learning and knowledge of past words and deeds. Master, when you heard that Yuezhengzi is to govern and rejoiced, was it because he is strong and possesses courage and vigor? Because he is wise and able to deliberate on affairs? Or because he has wide learning and knowledge of past words and deeds?" Chou asked repeatedly, and each time Mencius answered him with "No"—a word of negation—to show that all three were areas in which Yuezhengzi fell short, and that governing does not lie in relying on one's own personal strengths. As Chou still did not understand the reason for Mencius's joy and asked further, "Why then do you rejoice so much that you cannot sleep?", Mencius told him, "He is a man who loves goodness." When Chou again doubted that loving goodness was enough for governing and asked, "Is loving goodness enough?", Mencius further told him, "To love goodness is more than enough for governing the whole Empire." Truly, this is because goodness is the universal principle of the world, and loving goodness is the foremost task in governing. If one can love goodness, one can seek the Way with an open mind; even with the vastness of the Empire, one would have strength to spare in governing it—how could it be said that for a state as small as Lu, it would not be enough to bring about order? If one truly loves goodness, one can set aside oneself to follow others; even from as far away as the Four Seas, people will not count it too difficult to come and tell one what is good—how much more so within the nearness of the state itself: would anyone not gladly tell one the good Way? When the good words of the world arrive, …

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則天下之善皆歸於我而一己之強力知慮聞
識尚足為用乎哉大抵以一己之長為長其用
小以天下之長為長其用大聖如舜禹猶拜昌
言猶取諸人以為善況衆人乎苟不好善而以
訑訑之聲音顏色距人則士止而讒諂面諛之
人至矣烏能治國哉孟子因當時所尚不在於
善而在於他故有取於樂正子之好善其所以
為天下後世慮者深矣
易義
===
君子以成德為行日可見之行也潜之為
言也隱而未見行而未成是以君子弗用
也君子學以聚之問以辨之寬以居之仁
以行之易曰見龍在田利見大人君德也
楊茂元
同考試官訓導張批題本冠冕作者多泛惟
此作體認親切文亦簡當健羡健羡
同考試官教諭周批此題主隱顯而佳作絕少是
篇理明辭潔於日可見之行處發揮極當當是作手
punctuated:
則天下之善皆歸於我，而一己之強力、知慮、聞識，尚足為用乎哉？大抵以一己之長為長，其用小；以天下之長為長，其用大。聖如舜、禹，猶拜昌言，猶取諸人以為善，況衆人乎？苟不好善，而以訑訑之聲音顏色距人，則士止而讒諂面諛之人至矣，烏能治國哉？孟子因當時所尚不在於善而在於他，故有取於樂正子之好善，其所以為天下後世慮者深矣。
易義
「君子以成德為行，日可見之行也。潜之為言也，隱而未見，行而未成，是以君子弗用也。君子學以聚之，問以辨之，寬以居之，仁以行之。《易》曰：『見龍在田，利見大人。』君德也。」
楊茂元

同考試官教諭周批：此題主隱顯，而佳作絕少。是篇理明辭潔，於「日可見之行」處發揮極當，當是作手。
translation_en:
…then all the goodness of the world will accrue to me; how could the physical strength, intellectual calculation, and personal knowledge of a single individual still be worth relying upon? In general, if one takes one's own strengths as the only strengths, their utility is small; if one takes the strengths of the world as one's strengths, their utility is great. Even sages like Shun 舜 and Yu 禹 bowed to splendid words and drew upon others to practice goodness—how much more should ordinary people! If one does not love goodness, and instead repels others with the sound and look of self-conceit, then men of integrity will stay away, and slanderers, sycophants, and flatterers will arrive. How then could one govern a state? Because what was valued in his time did not lie in goodness but in other things, Mencius 孟子 commended Yuezhengzi's 樂正子 love of goodness; how deep was his concern for the world and for future generations!

Expositions on the Classic of Changes (Yiyi 易義)

"The gentleman takes perfected virtue as his conduct, conduct that can be seen daily. The word 'submerged' means hidden and not yet visible, practicing yet not yet perfected; therefore, the gentleman does not employ it. The gentleman studies to gather it, questions to discern it, abides in it with magnanimity, and puts it into practice with benevolence. The Classic of Changes (Yi 易) says: 'The dragon appears in the field; it is advantageous to see the great man.' This refers to the virtue of a ruler."

By Yang Maoyuan 楊茂元

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang 張: The topic itself is grand and dignified, so most writers treated it with vague generalities. Only this piece shows an intimate comprehension, and the writing is also concise and apt—truly admirable, truly admirable!

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhou 周: This topic centers on concealment and manifestation, and fine compositions on it were exceedingly rare. In this essay, the principles are clear and the diction is pure; its elaboration on the phrase "conduct that can be seen daily" is supremely fitting. The writer must be a master hand.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授劉批親切簡當允為佳作
考試官教授鄭批文理純潔可佳
備聖德而隨時隱顯者此文言申乾初二之象
傳也盖聖人與時而偕行爾初九以聖德而隱
九二以聖德而顯何莫非隨其時而處之與文
言聖人申乾初二象傳而推言及此夫乾之初
二皆有聖人之德但爻位有隱顯之不同爾是
故以言乎隱則初九之君子本然之性備於中
事物之理踐其實是以成德為行也德焉已成
===
行焉已立日可見諸世用而行義達道也措諸
事而為建功立業也然而爻辭以潜為言者盖
時當隱處而未見是以晦迹韜光而弗用焉德
行可施而未著是以懷寶遯世而不試焉其隨
時而隱也為何如以言乎顯則九二之君子格
物致知以會聚衆理之精粗親賢取友以辨别
衆理之是非既學聚問辨矣而尤擴本心之量
以居是理而與心為一焉既寬廣以居矣而尤
操本然之天以行是理而與天同運焉德至於
punctuated:
考試官教授劉批：親切簡當，允為佳作。
考試官教授鄭批：文理純潔，可佳。
備聖德而隨時隱顯者，此《文言》申《乾》初、二之《象傳》也。盖聖人與時而偕行爾。初九以聖德而隱，九二以聖德而顯，何莫非隨其時而處之與？《文言》聖人申《乾》初、二《象傳》，而推言及此。夫《乾》之初、二，皆有聖人之德，但爻位有隱顯之不同爾。是故以言乎隱，則初九之君子，本然之性備於中，事物之理踐其實，是以成德為行也。德焉已成，行焉已立，日可見諸世用，而行義達道也；措諸事，而為建功立業也。然而爻辭以「潜」為言者，盖時當隱處而未見，是以晦迹韜光而弗用焉；德行可施而未著，是以懷寶遯世而不試焉。其隨時而隱也為何如！以言乎顯，則九二之君子，格物致知，以會聚衆理之精粗；親賢取友，以辨别衆理之是非。既學聚問辨矣，而尤擴本心之量以居是理，而與心為一焉；既寬廣以居矣，而尤操本然之天以行是理，而與天同運焉。德至於

Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Liu: Intimate, concise, and fitting; truly an excellent piece.
Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Zheng: The style and reasoning are pure and clean; commendable.
Possessing sage virtue and either remaining in obscurity or becoming manifest in accordance with the times—this is how the "Commentary on the Words of the Text" (Wenyan) elaborates upon the "Commentary on the Images" (Xiangzhuan) for the first and second lines of the Qian hexagram. Indeed, the sage moves together with the times. When the Nine at the Beginning remains in obscurity with sage virtue, and the Nine in the Second Place becomes manifest with sage virtue, how is any of this not a matter of conducting oneself in accordance with the times? In the "Commentary on the Words of the Text," the sage elaborates on the "Commentary on the Images" for the first and second lines of Qian and extends his remarks to this point. Now, both the first and second lines of Qian possess the virtue of a sage; it is only that the positions of the lines differ between obscurity and manifestation. Therefore, to speak of obscurity: in the gentleman of the Nine at the Beginning, his original nature is complete within, and the principles of affairs and things are practiced in their reality; thus he takes perfected virtue as his conduct. With his virtue already perfected and his conduct already established, it is conduct that can be seen daily in worldly application, whereby he practices righteousness and extends the Way; when applied to affairs, it becomes the establishment of merit and the founding of achievements. Yet the line statement speaks of "submerged" because the time calls for dwelling in obscurity and he has not yet appeared; therefore he conceals his traces, hides his brilliance, and is not employed. Though his virtuous conduct could be put into practice, it is not yet manifest; therefore he cherishes his treasure, withdraws from the world, and is not tried in office. How profound is his remaining in obscurity in accordance with the times! To speak of manifestation: the gentleman of the Nine in the Second Place investigates things and extends knowledge so as to gather together the subtle and coarse aspects of all principles; he draws near to the worthy and chooses friends so as to distinguish right and wrong among all principles. Having already gathered through learning and distinguished through questioning, he furthermore expands the capacity of his original mind to abide in these principles, becoming one with his mind. Having already abided in them with broad-mindedness, he furthermore holds fast to his innate heavenly nature to put these principles into practice, revolving in harmony with Heaven. title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
仁則大人之德成而時位亦當顯矣故舉爻辭
而申之以君德者豈非君德備於已膏澤及於
民而為物所利見與其隨時而顯也為何如大
抵乾之初二不可岐而二焉初九之成德即九
二之成德二由學問寬仁以成其德而初以成
德為行實本於斯惟時位不同而隱顯異耳先
儒謂有隱顯而无淺深信夫
陰陽合德而剛柔有體以體天地之撰以
通神明之德其稱名也雜而不越
===
陳洵

考試官教授鄭批〔明潔可觀允宜高薦〕
原易卦之體成而顯微无不該論稱卦之名雜
punctuated:
仁，則大人之德成，而時位亦當顯矣。故舉爻辭而申之以君德者，豈非君德備於已、膏澤及於民，而為物所利見與？其隨時而顯也為何如！大抵乾之初、二，不可岐而二焉。初九之成德，即九二之成德。二由學問、寬仁以成其德，而初以成德為行，實本於斯，惟時位不同而隱顯異耳。先儒謂「有隱顯而无淺深」，信夫！
陰陽合德，而剛柔有體，以體天地之撰，以通神明之德。其稱名也，雜而不越。
陳洵

原《易》卦之體成而顯微无不該，論稱卦之名雜
translation_en:
…benevolence, the virtue of the great man is brought to completion, and his time and position likewise ought to become manifest. Therefore, when [Confucius] cites the line text and elaborates on it in terms of the virtue of a ruler, is it not because the virtue of a ruler is complete within oneself and one's rich beneficence extends to the people, so that it is advantageous for all creatures to see him? How great is his becoming manifest in accordance with the time! On the whole, the first and second lines of the Qian hexagram cannot be bifurcated into two separate things. The perfected virtue of the nine at the beginning is none other than the perfected virtue of the nine in the second place. The second line perfects its virtue through learning, inquiry, magnanimity, and benevolence, while the first line's taking perfected virtue as its conduct is in fact rooted in this; it is only because their times and positions are different that their concealment and manifestation differ. When a former Confucian scholar said, "There is concealment and manifestation, not shallowness and depth," how true that is!

"Yin and yang unite their virtues, and the firm and the yielding have their forms, thereby embodying the workings of Heaven and Earth and penetrating the virtues of the spirit-like and明 [luminous]." "Its naming of things is varied yet does not overstep."

By Chen Xun
