考試官教授劉批：策得事實。
考試官教授鄭批：不為問目所窘，可嘉，可嘉。
上天佑民，必以綏猷之責付之君；人君奉天，必以立極之訓示之民。盖有一代之隆興，必有一代之制作。遠而堯、舜、湯、武之典、謨、訓、誥，所以道民為善，固此道也；近而我朝一祖二宗之大誥三書，所以道民為善，亦此道也，又何彼此之間哉！《書》曰：「惟皇上帝，降衷于下民，若有恒性，克綏厥猷惟后。」是言人性本善，而不能不壊於人欲，所以脩道立教，使之各安其道以復於善，則賴乎君也。稽之於古，若堯、舜之「勞来匡直」，教以人倫；成湯之「肇脩人紀」；武王之「重民五教」。所以道民於善而克盡綏猷之責者，非有他術也，亦惟因其所固有者而道之耳。是以當時人人士行，比屋可封，非後世所能及也。
translation_en:
…policy essays all offer fine point-by-point responses, and this one is especially detailed and thorough—should it not be placed among the top selections?
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Liu comments: The policy essay grasps the actual facts.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zheng comments: Not constrained by the prompts of the question; commendable, commendable.

When High Heaven protects the people, It necessarily entrusts the ruler with the responsibility of securing their moral way; when the ruler serves Heaven, he necessarily displays to the people the teachings that establish the standard of perfection. Indeed, whenever there is the flourishing rise of a dynasty, there must be the institutions and creations of that dynasty. In distant antiquity, the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, by which they guided the people to do good, were assuredly this Way; in recent times, the Grand Pronouncements and the three works of the One Founder and Two Ancestors of our Dynasty, by which they guided the people to do good, are also this Way. What difference is there between the one and the other?

The Book of Documents says: "Great Heaven has conferred even on the inferior people a moral sense, compliance with which would show their nature invariably right. To make them tranquilly pursue the course which it would indicate is the work of the sovereign." This means that human nature is originally good, yet it cannot avoid being corrupted by human desires; therefore, cultivating the Way and establishing instruction, so as to cause each person to rest tranquilly in their proper way and return to goodness, depends upon the ruler. Examining antiquity, we see cases such as Yao and Shun "encouraging them, leading them on, rectifying them, and straightening them," teaching them the human relationships; Tang the Successful "first cultivating the moral bonds among men"; and King Wu attaching great importance to the people's "five teachings." That by which they guided the people toward goodness and were able to fulfill the responsibility of securing their moral way was no other technique: they simply followed what the people inherently possessed and guided them accordingly. For this reason, at that time everyone had the conduct of a worthy gentleman and every household was worthy of enfeoffment—something later ages have been unable to match.

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
迨至漢唐宋其間願治之君非不欲道民
為善然其所以道之之術則與此異如宋
太宗親書孝經於碑陰高宗親書孟子於
屏障不過為文具美觀而已烏能道民於
善哉洪惟我
朝
太祖高皇帝條成大誥三編昭示天下褒善之
言藹乎春温誠有以感發人之善心矣觀
其申明五常知報獲福之條與夫正婚姻
===
行鄉飲之數則所以道民之要亦不出乎
民生日用彛倫之外其克綏厥猷豈不與
堯舜湯武同一揆歟
太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒慮民之逸居而無教也
著為善陰隲孝順事實二書拳拳勸人為
善行孝而申之以報應之理其間所載如
鄧禹之不殺而子孫繼封公侯作配宫闈
韓琦之德政而子孫繼登台鼎光榮累世
蕭固孝謹而子芝仕至尚書郎黄香行孝
punctuated: 迨至漢、唐、宋，其間願治之君，非不欲道民為善，然其所以道之之術，則與此異。如宋太宗親書《孝經》於碑陰，高宗親書《孟子》於屏障，不過為文具美觀而已，烏能道民於善哉？洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝，條成《大誥》三編，昭示天下，褒善之言，藹乎春温，誠有以感發人之善心矣。觀其申明五常、知報獲福之條，與夫正婚姻、行鄉飲之數，則所以道民之要，亦不出乎民生日用彛倫之外。其克綏厥猷，豈不與堯、舜、湯、武同一揆歟？太宗文皇帝纘承丕緒，慮民之逸居而無教也，著《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書，拳拳勸人為善行孝，而申之以報應之理。其間所載，如鄧禹之不殺，而子孫繼封公侯，作配宫闈；韓琦之德政，而子孫繼登台鼎，光榮累世；蕭固孝謹，而子芝仕至尚書郎；黄香行孝，
translation_en:
When it came down to the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, the rulers during those eras who wished for good governance did not lack the desire to guide the people to do good; yet the methods by which they guided them differed from this. For instance, Emperor Taizong of the Song personally transcribed the Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing) on the reverse of a stone tablet, and Emperor Gaozong personally transcribed the Mencius (Mengzi) onto folding screens; these were nothing more than ornamental formalities for fine appearance—how could they truly guide the people toward goodness?

Reverently considering our dynasty, Emperor Taizu Gaohuangdi compiled the three collections of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) and promulgated them to the empire. His words praising goodness were as mild and genial as the warmth of spring, truly capable of stirring and inspiring people's innate goodness. When we observe his articles reiterating the Five Constant Virtues and knowing how to repay kindness to obtain blessings, along with the regulations for rectifying marriage and conducting the community wine-drinking ceremony, we see that the essentials by which he guided the people likewise did not go beyond the invariable human relationships of the people's daily lives. In being able to tranquilly pursue that moral course, is this not on the very same principle as Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu?

Emperor Taizong Wenhuangdi succeeded to the great enterprise, and, concerned that the people might dwell in idleness without instruction, authored two books: Secret Blessings for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Exemplars of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi). In them, he earnestly exhorted people to do good and practice filial piety, reinforcing this with the principle of moral retribution. Among the accounts recorded therein are examples such as Deng Yu 鄧禹, who refrained from killing, and whose descendants successively received enfeoffment as Dukes and Marquises and became consorts in the imperial palace; Han Qi 韓琦, who practiced virtuous governance, and whose descendants successively ascended to the highest ministerial offices, bringing glory for generations; Xiao Gu 蕭固, who was filially pious and circumspect, and whose son Xiao Zhi 蕭芝 rose in office to become a Secretarial Court Gentleman; and Huang Xiang 黄香, who practiced filial piety…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而子瓊仕為僕射是為善行孝之獲報也
豈不與大誥為善獲報之效同條而共貫
歟
宣宗章皇帝嗣大歷服慮民之忽於倫理也著
五倫一書備人倫之道而各舉其善行其
間所載若洪皓盡忠而三子並中詞科趙
善應純孝而一子卒登相位是其盡臣子
之善行而獲報也又豈不與為善孝順二
書一軌而合轍歟
===
三聖四書掀揭宇宙
宸章奎翰照耀簡策皆道民於善而盡克綏
厥猷之責者也是以四海之內家傳人誦
風移俗易熙熙然相安相樂於雍熈之世
皞皞乎相親相愛於泰和之天於戲盛矣
然先聖後聖本同一心典謨四書實相表
裏大誥之君臣同遊即虞書之元首明哉
股肱良哉也陰隲書之為善獲報即謨訓
之惠迪吉作善降祥也孝順事實之虞舜
punctuated: 而子瓊仕為僕射，是為善行孝之獲報也。豈不與《大誥》為善獲報之效，同條而共貫歟？宣宗章皇帝嗣大歷服，慮民之忽於倫理也，著《五倫》一書，備人倫之道，而各舉其善行。其間所載，若洪皓盡忠而三子並中詞科，趙善應純孝而一子卒登相位，是其盡臣子之善行而獲報也。又豈不與《為善》、《孝順》二書一軌而合轍歟？三聖四書，掀揭宇宙，宸章奎翰，照耀簡策，皆道民於善而盡克綏厥猷之責者也。是以四海之內，家傳人誦，風移俗易，熙熙然相安相樂於雍熈之世，皞皞乎相親相愛於泰和之天。於戲，盛矣！然先聖後聖，本同一心；典謨四書，實相表裏。《大誥》之「君臣同遊」，即《虞書》之「元首明哉，股肱良哉」也；《陰隲書》之為善獲報，即謨訓之「惠迪吉」、「作善降祥」也；《孝順事實》之虞舜
translation_en:
… and his son Qiong 瓊 rose in office to become a Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs (puye 僕射)—these are the rewards obtained for doing good and practicing filial piety. Do they not share the same principles and form a single thread with the efficacy of obtaining rewards for doing good found in the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao)?

Emperor Xuanzong Zhang [the Xuande Emperor] inherited the great dynastic mandate, and, concerned that the people might neglect moral relationships, composed the Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu), which sets forth the principles of human relationships in full and cites exemplary deeds under each. Among the accounts recorded therein—such as Hong Hao 洪皓 fulfilling his loyalty and his three sons all passing the erudite literatus examination (cike 詞科), or Zhao Shanying 趙善應 practicing pure filial piety and one of his sons eventually ascending to the position of Grand Councilor—these are the rewards obtained for fulfilling the virtuous conduct of a subject and a son. Do they not also follow the exact same track as the two books on Doing Good [i.e., the Weishan yinzhi] and Filial Piety [i.e., the Xiaoshun shishi]?

The four books of the three sage emperors are held aloft throughout the universe; their imperial compositions and starry brush-strokes illuminate the historical records. All of them guide the people toward goodness and fulfill the responsibility of "tranquilizing them in their moral course." Therefore, within the four seas, every family passes them down and every person recites them; customs are transformed and morals changed. People live together in peaceful contentment and shared joy in an era of harmonious prosperity, and cherish one another with vast contentment beneath a heaven of supreme harmony. Oh, how magnificent!

Yet the former sages and later sages are fundamentally of one mind, and the Canons and Counsels [of the Book of Documents] and these four books in fact form the outer and inner aspects of one another. The section "Ruler and Ministers Sharing Fellowship" (Junchen tongyou) in the Grand Pronouncements is none other than "The sovereign is enlightened, the limbs and arms [ministers] are good" in the Book of Yu (Yushu). Obtaining rewards for doing good in the Book of Secret Virtue (Yinzhi shu) is none other than "Compliance with the right leads to good fortune" and "On the doer of good, Heaven sends down all blessings" in the Counsels and Instructions [of the Book of Documents]. The great filial piety of Shun of Yu 虞舜 in the Biographical Accounts of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi)…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
大孝非堯典克諧以孝之謂乎五倫書之
紀載善行非二典九族既睦五典克從之
意乎愚也生長於鳶飛魚躍之天涵泳於
鳳儀獸舞之治服膺
聖訓於茲有年謹掇拾所聞以對
第二問
吳嵩
同考試官教授劉批大小學策人多忽略
此作綱目畢張文義縝密宜在選列
===
考試官教授劉批五策皆有議論此作尤優
考試官教授鄭批此策敷答詳明又以敬之一言
貫二書之旨蓋熟於窮理之學者
聖賢教人之法有小學焉有大學焉始之
以小學所以收其放心養其德性而立大
學之根本終之以大學所以察夫義理措
之事業而收小學之成功二書相因其道
一而已矣且小學一書乃子朱子蒐輯傳
記纂成有內篇以立本原有外篇以衍支
punctuated:
大孝，非《堯典》「克諧以孝」之謂乎？《五倫書》之紀載善行，非《二典》「九族既睦」、「五典克從」之意乎？愚也生長於鳶飛魚躍之天，涵泳於鳳儀獸舞之治，服膺聖訓，於茲有年，謹掇拾所聞以對。

第二問
吳嵩
同考試官教授劉批：大小學策，人多忽略，此作綱目畢張，文義縝密，宜在選列。
考試官教授劉批：五策皆有議論，此作尤優。
考試官教授鄭批：此策敷答詳明，又以「敬」之一言貫二書之旨，蓋熟於窮理之學者。

聖賢教人之法，有小學焉，有大學焉。始之以小學，所以收其放心，養其德性，而立大學之根本；終之以大學，所以察夫義理，措之事業，而收小學之成功。二書相因，其道一而已矣。且《小學》一書，乃子朱子蒐輯傳記纂成，有內篇以立本原，有外篇以衍支
translation_en:
…great filial piety—is this not what the Canon of Yao (Yaodian) calls "being able to live in harmony through filial piety"? The recording of virtuous deeds in the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu)—is this not the meaning of "the nine branches of the kin having become harmonious" and "the five cardinal duties being earnestly observed" in the Two Canons (Erdian)? In my ignorance, I was born and raised beneath a sky where kites fly and fish leap, and have been immersed in an era of governance where phoenixes come with stately儀 and beasts dance. Having cherished the Imperial instructions in my heart for years now, I respectfully gather what I have heard to reply.

Second Question
Wu Song 吳嵩
Associate Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Liu comments: Most candidates neglect the policy question on the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and the Great Learning (Daxue), yet this essay fully sets forth both the main principles and the detailed items, and its literary meaning is tightly woven; it ought to be placed among the selected.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Liu comments: All five policy essays contain sound arguments, and this composition is especially superior.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zheng comments: This policy essay elaborates its reply with clarity and detail, and furthermore threads the purport of both books together with the single word "reverence" (jing); he is surely a scholar well-versed in the exhaustive investigation of principle.

In the method by which the sages and worthies taught people, there is the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) and there is the Great Learning (Daxue). Beginning with the Elementary Learning is the means to recover one's straying mind, nourish one's moral nature, and establish the foundation of the Great Learning; concluding with the Great Learning is the means to examine moral principles, put them into practice in affairs and undertakings, and reap the completed achievement of the Elementary Learning. The two books build upon each other, and their Way is simply one. Moreover, the book of the Elementary Learning was compiled by Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹], who gathered materials from commentaries and records. It has "Inner Chapters" to establish the fundamental source, and "Outer Chapters" to extend the tributary…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
流内篇則立教明倫敬身稽古是也外篇
則嘉言善行是也内篇首之以立教而所
教者洒掃應對之節愛親敬長之道焉次
之以明倫而所明者父子之親君臣之義
夫婦之別長幼之序朋友之交焉次之以
敬身所以明心術之要威儀之則衣服之
制飲食之節也又次之以稽古所以考三
代聖賢已然之迹以證立教明倫敬身之
言也外篇則述自漢以来賢者則嘉言所
===
以廣立教明倫敬身之義又記自漢以来
賢人之善行所以實立教明倫敬身之事
此小學教人之法以為大學脩齊治平之
本三代以後不知此義至先儒北溪陳氏
謂此書綱領甚好切於日用魯齋許氏謂
此書吾信之如神明敬之如父母盖欲學
者篤信而尊崇之也大學則子曾子述孔
子之經傳十章之義外有三綱領内有八
條目三綱領則明德新民止至善是也而
punctuated: 流。内篇則「立教」、「明倫」、「敬身」、「稽古」是也；外篇則「嘉言」、「善行」是也。内篇首之以「立教」，而所教者，洒掃、應對之節，愛親、敬長之道焉；次之以「明倫」，而所明者，父子之親、君臣之義、夫婦之別、長幼之序、朋友之交焉；次之以「敬身」，所以明心術之要、威儀之則、衣服之制、飲食之節也；又次之以「稽古」，所以考三代聖賢已然之迹，以證「立教」、「明倫」、「敬身」之言也。外篇則述自漢以来賢者則「嘉言」，所以廣「立教」、「明倫」、「敬身」之義；又記自漢以来賢人之「善行」，所以實「立教」、「明倫」、「敬身」之事。此《小學》教人之法，以為《大學》脩、齊、治、平之本。三代以後，不知此義。至先儒北溪陳氏謂：「此書綱領甚好，切於日用。」魯齋許氏謂：「此書吾信之如神明，敬之如父母。」盖欲學者篤信而尊崇之也。《大學》則子曾子述孔子之經，傳十章之義。外有三綱領，内有八條目。三綱領則「明德」、「新民」、「止至善」是也，而
translation_en: … streams. The Inner Chapters consist of "Establishing Instruction," "Clarifying Human Relationships," "Revering the Person," and "Examining Antiquity"; the Outer Chapters consist of "Admirable Words" and "Good Deeds." The Inner Chapters begin with "Establishing Instruction," and what is taught therein are the proprieties of sprinkling, sweeping, and responding to calls, as well as the ways of loving parents and respecting elders. Next comes "Clarifying Human Relationships," and what is clarified therein are the affection between father and son, the righteousness between ruler and minister, the distinction between husband and wife, the precedence between old and young, and the trustworthiness between friends. Next comes "Revering the Person," which serves to clarify the essentials of mental disposition, the rules of dignified demeanor, the regulations of clothing, and the moderation of food and drink. Next after that comes "Examining Antiquity," which serves to investigate the actual traces of the sages and worthies of the Three Dynasties in order to substantiate the teachings on "Establishing Instruction," "Clarifying Human Relationships," and "Revering the Person." The Outer Chapters recount the "Admirable Words" [?; 則 appears to be a scribal error for 之] of worthies since the Han dynasty, in order to broaden the meaning of "Establishing Instruction," "Clarifying Human Relationships," and "Revering the Person"; and they also record the "Good Deeds" of worthy persons since the Han dynasty, in order to give concrete substance to the practice of "Establishing Instruction," "Clarifying Human Relationships," and "Revering the Person." Such is the method by which the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) instructs people, serving as the foundation for cultivating the person, regulating the family, ordering the state, and bringing peace to the world in the Great Learning (Daxue). After the Three Dynasties, this meaning was no longer understood. Eventually, the former Confucian scholar Master Chen of Beixi (Chen Chun 陳淳) said: "The guiding principles of this book are excellent and closely relevant to daily use." Master Xu of Luzhai (Xu Heng 許衡) said: "I believe in this book as in the divine spirits, and revere it as I do my parents." Indeed, they wished for learners to earnestly believe in and venerate it. As for the Great Learning, Master Zengzi transmitted the classic text of Confucius, together with the meanings of the ten chapters of commentary. Externally, it has the Three Guiding Principles; internally, it has the Eight Particular Steps. The Three Guiding Principles are "luminous virtue," "renewing the people," and "abiding in the highest good"; and…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明明德一言又為綱領中之綱領焉八條
目則格物致知誠意正心脩身齊家治國
平天下是也而明明德於天下一言又有
以該體用而無遺焉傳者釋綱領外又有
本末章者釋經文物有本末之義也他章
皆以二事相承而誠意自為一章者以誠
意為自脩之首也此大學教人之方而為
小學入德之門漢儒以来鮮有能知之者
至唐韓愈原道篇止及於正心誠意而無
===
所謂格物致知宋朱子進講是書於寧宗
之前則動以格物致知誠意為言者一則
語道之未詳一則愛君之盡誠也然小學
大學教人之術與夫次第節目雖有不同
而為道豈有二致哉明問又謂二書可一
言以蔽之嘗聞之先儒曰敬者聖學之所
以成始而成終者也為小學而不由乎此
則無以涵養本原而謹夫立藝之教為大
學而不由乎此則無以開發聰明以進德
punctuated:
「明明德」一言，又為綱領中之綱領焉。八條目，則格物、致知、誠意、正心、脩身、齊家、治國、平天下是也；而「明明德於天下」一言，又有以該體用而無遺焉。傳者釋綱領外，又有本末章者，釋經文「物有本末」之義也。他章皆以二事相承，而「誠意」自為一章者，以誠意為自脩之首也。此《大學》教人之方，而為《小學》入德之門。漢儒以来，鮮有能知之者。至唐韓愈《原道》篇，止及於正心、誠意，而無所謂格物、致知；宋朱子進講是書於寧宗之前，則動以格物、致知、誠意為言者，一則語道之未詳，一則愛君之盡誠也。然《小學》、《大學》教人之術，與夫次第節目雖有不同，而為道豈有二致哉？

明問又謂「二書可一言以蔽之」。嘗聞之先儒曰：「敬者，聖學之所以成始而成終者也。為《小學》而不由乎此，則無以涵養本原而謹夫立藝之教；為《大學》而不由乎此，則無以開發聰明以進德…
translation_en:
… the single phrase "manifesting luminous virtue" is, in turn, the guiding principle among the guiding principles. As for the Eight Steps, they are investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, rectifying the mind, cultivating the person, regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world; and the single phrase "manifesting luminous virtue throughout the world" encompasses both substance and function without omission. Aside from the commentary chapters explaining the guiding principles, there is also a chapter on roots and branches, which explains the meaning of the classic text's statement that "things have roots and branches." All the other chapters link two matters together in sequence, whereas "making the intentions sincere" forms a chapter of its own because making the intentions sincere is the beginning of self-cultivation. This is the method by which the Great Learning (Daxue) instructs people, serving as the gateway into virtue building upon the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue). Since the Confucian scholars of the Han dynasty, few have been able to understand this. Down to the Tang dynasty, Han Yu 韓愈 in his essay "Tracing the Way" (Yuan Dao) touched only upon rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere, with no mention of investigating things and extending knowledge; whereas in the Song dynasty, when Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] lectured on this book before Emperor Ningzong 寧宗, he unfailingly spoke of investigating things, extending knowledge, and making the intentions sincere. The former case was a matter of discussing the Way incompletely, while the latter was a matter of utmost sincerity in loving one's ruler. Yet although the methods of instructing people in the Elementary Learning and the Great Learning, along with their sequences and specific items, differ from one another, how could their Way be twofold?

Your brilliant question further asks whether "the two books can be summed up in a single word." I have heard it said by a former Confucian scholar [Zhu Xi]: "Reverent seriousness (jing) is that whereby the learning of the sages accomplishes both its beginning and its end. If one engages in the Elementary Learning without proceeding from this, there is no way to nourish the fundamental source and be attentive to the teachings of establishing oneself and acquiring the arts; if one engages in the Great Learning without proceeding from this, there is no way to open up and develop one's intelligence so as to advance in virtue…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而脩業則敬者二書之要領也愚生雖由
小學而入大學然於道未知嚮方姑摭所
聞以對惟進而教之
第三問
陳謙
同考試官教諭王批此策有考據有断制非
胷中素有定論者不能允宜高薦
同考試官教諭吳批薦舉一策場中答者
率多遺漏惟此作隨問隨答盖留心於策學者也
===
考試官教授劉批文勢滔滔事實不遺策
場之優者
考試官教授鄭批策詳贍明白
為國莫先於薦賢薦賢惟在於至公盖為
國而不薦賢非所以愛其國薦賢而不以
至公豈能得夫賢哉知乎此則可以復明
問矣粤自三代以前俊乂在官薦舉之名
未立成周之時舉能其官而薦舉之名始
聞自是薦者非一人舉者非一途苟材之
punctuated:
而脩業，則「敬」者，二書之要領也。愚生雖由《小學》而入《大學》，然於道未知嚮方，姑摭所聞以對，惟進而教之。

第三問
陳謙
同考試官教諭王批：此策有考據，有断制，非胷中素有定論者不能，允宜高薦。
同考試官教諭吳批：薦舉一策，場中答者率多遺漏，惟此作隨問隨答，盖留心於策學者也。
考試官教授劉批：文勢滔滔，事實不遺，策場之優者。
考試官教授鄭批：策詳贍明白。

為國莫先於薦賢，薦賢惟在於至公。盖為國而不薦賢，非所以愛其國；薦賢而不以至公，豈能得夫賢哉？知乎此，則可以復明問矣。粤自三代以前，俊乂在官，薦舉之名未立；成周之時，舉能其官，而薦舉之名始聞。自是薦者非一人，舉者非一途。苟材之
translation_en:
…and advance in one's studies; thus "reverence" (jing) is the essential principle of both books. Although this ignorant student has progressed from the Elementary Learning (Xiaoxue) to enter the Great Learning (Daxue), I do not yet know the proper direction toward the Way. I have merely gathered what I have heard in order to reply, and I only beg that you admit me and instruct me further.

Question Three
Chen Qian 陳謙
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Wang 王: This policy essay possesses both evidential grounding and decisive judgment. None but someone who has long held settled views in his breast could have produced it; it truly deserves a high recommendation.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Wu 吳: On the policy question concerning recommendation and promotion, most respondents in the examination hall left out many points. This piece alone answers each point as it is asked, showing that the author is someone who has paid close attention to the study of policy questions.
Comment by Examiner Professor Liu 劉: The momentum of the prose flows surgingly, and no historical facts are omitted; it is an outstanding piece from the policy examination session.
Comment by Examiner Professor Zheng 鄭: The policy essay is detailed, rich, and clear.

In governing a state, nothing takes precedence over recommending the worthy, and recommending the worthy lies solely in utmost impartiality. Indeed, to govern a state without recommending the worthy is not the way to love that state; and to recommend the worthy without utmost impartiality—how could one truly obtain worthy men? Understanding this, one may reply to the enlightened question. Prior to the Three Dynasties, men of eminent talent served in office, and the term "recommendation and promotion" (jianju) had not yet been established. In the time of the glorious Zhou, men were promoted according to their ability to fulfill their offices, and the term "recommendation and promotion" was first heard. From then on, those who recommended were not limited to a single person, and those who were promoted did not come through a single path. So long as a person's talent…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
可用雖親亦薦如祁奚之薦祁午吕蒙正
之薦夷簡而人不以為疑者公也雖讐亦
舉如觧狐之舉荆伯抑吕夷簡之舉范仲
淹而人不以為嫌者亦公也漢張釋之之
善聽獄訟于定國之練習法令而袁盎丙
吉薦之唐張九齡之學問該博韓休之行
誼純篤而張說蕭嵩舉之宋吕文靖之薦
包拯非以其同巷不求見乎司馬光之薦
劉元城非以其無書抵政府乎之数君子
===
之所薦雖不同而同出於公也至若李師
錫乃王德用之甥也以德用故而薦者三
十餘人陳琪乃龐籍之婿也以龐籍故而
舉者二十四人是不皆貴要之私耳如公道
何王安國荆公之親弟也託荆公以力薦
之吕惠卿荆公之同巳也犯衆怒而力舉
之是皆親故之私耳如公道何此所以不
能無譏於人也他如自謂我為相無能但
有一能善用人者吕文穆也自言我輔政
punctuated: 可用，雖親亦薦，如祁奚之薦祁午、吕蒙正之薦夷簡，而人不以為疑者，公也；雖讐亦舉，如觧狐之舉荆伯柳、吕夷簡之舉范仲淹，而人不以為嫌者，亦公也。漢張釋之之善聽獄訟，于定國之練習法令，而袁盎、丙吉薦之；唐張九齡之學問該博，韓休之行誼純篤，而張說、蕭嵩舉之；宋吕文靖之薦包拯，非以其同巷不求見乎？司馬光之薦劉元城，非以其無書抵政府乎？之数君子之所薦雖不同，而同出於公也。至若李師錫乃王德用之甥也，以德用故而薦者三十餘人；陳琪乃龐籍之婿也，以龐籍故而舉者二十四人，是不皆貴要之私耳，如公道何？王安國，荆公之親弟也，託荆公以力薦之；吕惠卿，荆公之同巳也，犯衆怒而力舉之，是皆親故之私耳，如公道何？此所以不能無譏於人也。他如自謂「我為相無能，但有一能善用人」者，吕文穆也；自言「我輔政
translation_en:
… are usable, even if they are relatives one recommends them, just as Qi Xi 祁奚 recommended Qi Wu 祁午 and Lü Mengzheng 呂蒙正 recommended [Lü] Yijian 呂夷簡, and people did not regard this with suspicion because it was done out of impartiality; even if they are personal enemies one nominates them, just as Xie Hu 解狐 nominated Jing Boliu 荊伯柳 [written 荆伯抑] and Lü Yijian nominated Fan Zhongyan 范仲淹, and people did not take exception to it because it too was done out of impartiality. In the Han, Zhang Shizhi 張釋之 excelled at hearing lawsuits and Yu Dingguo 于定國 was well-versed in laws and ordinances, so Yuan Ang 袁盎 and Bing Ji 丙吉 recommended them. In the Tang, Zhang Jiuling 張九齡 possessed broad and comprehensive learning and Han Xiu 韓休 had pure and earnest conduct, so Zhang Yue 張說 and Xiao Song 蕭嵩 nominated them. In the Song, when Lü Wenjing 呂文靖 [Lü Yijian] recommended Bao Zheng 包拯, was it not because, though living in the same lane, Bao never sought an audience with him? When Sima Guang 司馬光 recommended Liu Yuancheng 劉元城 [Liu Anshi 劉安世], was it not because Liu never sent a letter to the Administration Chamber? Although the recommendations made by these several gentlemen differed, they all stemmed alike from impartiality.

As for Li Shixi 李師錫, he was the nephew of Wang Deyong 王德用, and on account of Deyong more than thirty people recommended him; Chen Qi 陳琪 was the son-in-law of Pang Ji 龐籍, and on account of Pang Ji twenty-four people nominated him. Are these not all merely the private biases of the noble and powerful? What becomes of the way of impartiality? Wang Anguo 王安國 was the biological younger brother of Duke Jing 荊公 [Wang Anshi 王安石], who relied on Duke Jing [?] to forcefully recommend him; Lü Huiqing 呂惠卿 was a partisan of Duke Jing, who braved public anger to forcefully nominate him. These are all merely private biases for relatives and old associates—what becomes of the way of impartiality? This is why they could not escape criticism from others.

As for other cases: the one who said of himself, "As Grand Councilor I have no abilities, save for one ability—being good at employing men," was Lü Wenmu 呂文穆 [Lü Mengzheng]; the one who said of himself, "In assisting with governance…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
何功惟薦二臺官無愧非唐質肅乎二公
之急於薦人如此其公可知矣身為諫議
未嘗妄薦一人者謝泌也官居執政不敢
私薦一士者非陳升之乎二公之謹於薦
人如此則其公又可知矣方今
聖皇馭極賢路大開當途推轂者皆忠君愛國
之臣拔茅彙征者悉秉德守正之士朝無
倖位而野無遺賢矣執事猶謂山林泉石
尚有遺逸之士百司庶府不無淹滯之才
===
誠過慮也兹欲屈在下僚者悉得擢用誠
如近者臺憲大臣所言在京廷臣各舉所
知在外風憲監司各舉所屬之廉能則才
無淹滯矣欲隱於巖穴者咸得彙進誠如
明詔所言山林懷材抱德之士有司舉送銓
曹擢用則士無遺逸矣然又在於司薦舉
者之各秉至公而後可富鄭公嘗曰有德
者然後知人之德有才者然後知人之才
歐陽公亦曰廉者舉清廉贓者舉貪濁然
punctuated: 何功，惟薦二臺官無愧，非唐質肅乎？二公之急於薦人如此，其公可知矣。身為諫議，未嘗妄薦一人者，謝泌也；官居執政，不敢私薦一士者，非陳升之乎？二公之謹於薦人如此，則其公又可知矣。方今聖皇馭極，賢路大開，當途推轂者，皆忠君愛國之臣；拔茅彙征者，悉秉德守正之士。朝無倖位，而野無遺賢矣。執事猶謂山林泉石尚有遺逸之士，百司庶府不無淹滯之才，誠過慮也。兹欲屈在下僚者悉得擢用，誠如近者臺憲大臣所言，在京廷臣各舉所知，在外風憲監司各舉所屬之廉能，則才無淹滯矣；欲隱於巖穴者咸得彙進，誠如明詔所言，山林懷材抱德之士，有司舉送銓曹擢用，則士無遺逸矣。然又在於司薦舉者之各秉至公而後可。富鄭公嘗曰：「有德者，然後知人之德；有才者，然後知人之才。」歐陽公亦曰：「廉者舉清廉，贓者舉貪濁。」然
translation_en:
… had no merit, save that he felt no shame in having recommended two Censorate officials”—was this not Tang Zhisu (Tang Jie 唐介)? Since these two lords were so eager to recommend men, their impartiality can be known. One who served as Policy Critic-Adviser yet never recklessly recommended a single man was Xie Bi 謝泌; one who held the office of Executive Official yet dared not privately recommend a single scholar—was this not Chen Shengzhi 陳升之? Since these two lords were so cautious in recommending men, their impartiality can likewise be known.

At present, the Sacred Emperor reigns on the throne, and the pathway for the worthy is wide open. Those in power who push the wheel hubs to advance others are all ministers loyal to the sovereign and devoted to the state; those drawn up together like Couch-grass roots are all scholars who uphold virtue and maintain rectitude. At court there are no positions held by undeserving favorites, and in the wilderness there are no overlooked worthies. Yet Your Excellency still suggests that among the mountain forests and spring-fed rocks there remain overlooked scholars in retirement, and that within the hundred offices and myriad bureaus there is no lack of talent languishing in obscurity—this is truly an excessive concern.

Now, if one wishes that those bowed down in minor sub-official or subordinate posts may all be promoted and employed, it should truly be as the Censorate ministers recently proposed: let the court officials in the capital each recommend those whom they know, and let the風憲 (surveillance) and監司 (supervisory) officials in the provinces each recommend the incorrupt and capable among their subordinates; then no talent will languish in obscurity. If one wishes that those hidden away in mountain caves may all advance together as a class, it should truly be as the Imperial Edict has stated: let the scholars among the mountains and forests who cherish talent and embrace virtue be recommended and sent forward by the local authorities to the Ministry of Personnel for promotion and employment; then no scholar will be left overlooked in retirement.

Yet this also depends upon those in charge of recommendations each upholding the utmost impartiality before it can succeed. Duke Zheng of Fu (Fu Bi 富弼) once said: “Only one who possesses virtue can recognize the virtue of others; only one who possesses talent can recognize the talent of others.” Master Ouyang (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩) likewise said: “The incorrupt recommend the pure and incorrupt; the venal recommend the greedy and corrupt.” Thus…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則薦舉不公當嚴連坐之法請以是為執
事獻
第四問
楊茂元
同考試官訓導張批敷演畧無凝滯必博
洽之士也高薦何忝
同考試官教諭周批五策文采爛然其論文
章一策尤有考據他日所就未可量也宜寘魁選
考試官教授劉批敷荅豐贍優於衆作
===
考試官教授鄭批考究詳明必本古能文之士
有義理之文有詞章之文繢章繪句錦心
繡口詞章之文也義本六經文關世教義
理之文也詞章之文膾炙於人口才士皆
可能之義理之文浸漬於人心非有德者
莫之能也三代以上莫非義理之文三代
以下純於義理者盖鮮矣有如孔明韓杜
之流豈非百鳥中之孤鳯歟是故晋之文
章非不多也而歐陽公謂晋無文章惟陶
punctuated:
則薦舉不公，當嚴連坐之法。請以是為執事獻。

第四問
楊茂元
同考試官訓導張批：敷演畧無凝滯，必博洽之士也，高薦何忝！
同考試官教諭周批：五策文采爛然，其論文章一策，尤有考據。他日所就，未可量也，宜寘魁選。
考試官教授劉批：敷荅豐贍，優於衆作。
考試官教授鄭批：考究詳明，必本古能文之士。

有義理之文，有詞章之文。繢章繪句，錦心繡口，詞章之文也；義本六經，文關世教，義理之文也。詞章之文，膾炙於人口，才士皆可能之；義理之文，浸漬於人心，非有德者莫之能也。三代以上，莫非義理之文；三代以下，純於義理者盖鮮矣。有如孔明、韓、杜之流，豈非百鳥中之孤鳯歟！是故晋之文章非不多也，而歐陽公謂晋無文章，惟陶
translation_en:
… then if recommendations are not impartial, the law of joint liability must be strictly enforced. I beg to offer this to Your Excellency.

Fourth Question
Yang Maoyuan 楊茂元
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang: The elaboration has not the slightest stagnation; he must be a scholar of broad learning. What shame would there be in recommending him for a high place!
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhou: The five policy essays are brilliant in literary grace, and his essay discussing literature is especially well-grounded in evidence. His future achievements cannot be measured; he ought to be placed among the top selections.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Liu: The exposition and answers are rich and abundant, superior to the work of the multitude.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: The investigation is detailed and clear; he must be a scholar skilled in composition who grounds himself in antiquity.

There is writing of moral principle (yili), and there is writing of ornate rhetoric (cizhang). Embellishing chapters and painting sentences, with a brocade heart and embroidered mouth—this is writing of ornate rhetoric. Grounding meaning in the Six Classics and having one's writing bear upon the moral teaching of the age—this is writing of moral principle. Writing of ornate rhetoric is relished on people's lips, and any talented scholar is capable of it; writing of moral principle steeps into people's hearts, and none without virtue is capable of it. From the Three Dynasties and earlier, all was writing of moral principle; after the Three Dynasties, those pure in moral principle have been rare indeed. That there were the likes of Kongming [Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮], Han [Han Yu 韓愈], and Du [Du Fu 杜甫]—were they not lone phoenixes among a hundred birds? Therefore, the literature of the Jin dynasty was certainly not scant, yet Lord Ouyang [Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修] said that the Jin had no literature, save ONLY Tao [Tao Yuanming 陶淵明]…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
淵明歸去来辭豈非以其蕭然物外高潔
簡古乎唐之文章非不富也而蘇東坡謂
唐無文章惟李愿歸盤谷序豈非以其善
狀物態宛轉新竒乎孔明出師一表其忠
肝義膽凛乎其不可犯蘇東坡謂其與伊
訓說命相表裏信矣杜子美平生詩集其
忠君愛國藹然見於言外黄山谷謂其得
三百篇之㫖宜矣韓子之文若捕龍蛇急
與之角而不暇豈無所自而然歟良由有
===
得於詩葩易竒盤誥詰屈春秋謹嚴之趣
也柳子之文軋漢周而凌晉宋凛然一王
之法豈無自而爾歟良由上學詩易春秋
下得左氏國語之妙也讀歐之文如遊帝
舜之庭而聆簫韶之樂姑舉一篇以見其
他如本論序所以麾異端之道雍容閒雅
不勞寸兵尺鐵而聞風遠遁真竒文矣讀
蘇之文如駕千里之駒而御以王良造父
姑舉一篇以例其餘如上神宗書所獻三
punctuated: 淵明《歸去来辭》，豈非以其蕭然物外，高潔簡古乎？唐之文章非不富也，而蘇東坡謂「唐無文章，惟《李愿歸盤谷序》」，豈非以其善狀物態，宛轉新竒乎？孔明《出師》一表，其忠肝義膽，凛乎其不可犯，蘇東坡謂其與《伊訓》、《說命》相表裏，信矣。杜子美平生詩集，其忠君愛國，藹然見於言外，黄山谷謂其得《三百篇》之㫖，宜矣。韓子之文，若捕龍蛇，急與之角而不暇，豈無所自而然歟？良由有得於《詩》葩、《易》竒、《盤》《誥》詰屈、《春秋》謹嚴之趣也。柳子之文，軋漢、周而凌晉、宋，凛然一王之法，豈無自而爾歟？良由上學《詩》、《易》、《春秋》，下得《左氏》、《國語》之妙也。讀歐之文，如遊帝舜之庭而聆《簫韶》之樂，姑舉一篇以見其他，如《本論》序所以麾異端之道，雍容閒雅，不勞寸兵尺鐵而聞風遠遁，真竒文矣。讀蘇之文，如駕千里之駒而御以王良、造父，姑舉一篇以例其餘，如《上神宗書》所獻三
translation_en: … Yuanming's (Tao Qian 陶潛) "Rhapsody on Returning Home" (Guiqulai ci 歸去來辭)—is this not because he stood serenely beyond the material world, lofty, pure, concise, and ancient in style? The literary writings of the Tang dynasty were certainly not lacking in abundance, yet Su Dongpo (Su Shi 蘇軾) remarked that "the Tang had no literature, save for the 'Preface on Seeing Off Li Yuan on His Return to Pan Valley' (Song Li Yuan gui Pangu xu 送李願歸盤谷序)"—is this not because it excelled at depicting the states of things, winding with fresh originality? As for Kongming's (Zhuge Liang 諸葛亮) single "Memorial on Deploying the Troops" (Chushi biao 出師表), its loyal heart and righteous courage are so awe-inspiring as to be inviolable; Su Dongpo's statement that it stands as the outer and inner counterpart to the "Instructions of Yi" (Yi xun 伊訓) and the "Charge to Yue" (Yue ming 說命) in the Book of Documents is truly trustworthy. In Du Zimei's (Du Fu 杜甫) lifelong collection of poetry, his loyalty to his sovereign and love for his state shine warmly beyond the words themselves; Huang Shangu's (Huang Tingjian 黃庭堅) remark that he grasped the purport of the Three Hundred Poems (the Classic of Poetry) is fitting indeed. The prose of Master Han (Han Yu 韓愈) is like seizing dragons and serpents, urgently locking horns with them without a moment's pause—how could it be so without a source? Truly, it came from having grasped the spirit of the Classic of Poetry's exuberance, the Classic of Changes' wondrousness, the knotty ruggedness of the "Pan Geng" (盤庚) and "Announcements" (Gao 誥) chapters of the Book of Documents, and the strict rigor of the Spring and Autumn Annals. The prose of Master Liu (柳宗元 Liu Zongyuan) rivaled that of the Zhou and Han and surpassed that of the Jin and Song, possessing the awe-inspiring authority of a true king's laws—how could it be so without a source? Truly, it came from studying the Classic of Poetry, the Classic of Changes, and the Spring and Autumn Annals above, and attaining the subtleties of the Zuo Commentary (Zuoshi 左氏) and the Discourses of the States (Guoyu 國語) below. Reading the prose of Ouyang (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修) is like roaming the court of Emperor Shun and listening to the Xiaoshao (簫韶) music; if we provisionally cite one piece to show the rest, such as how his "On Fundamentals" (Benlun 本論) sets forth the way to repel heterodox teachings—poised, unhurried, and refined, causing them to flee far away at the mere wind of it without expending an inch of weapon or a foot of iron—it is truly marvelous writing. Reading the prose of Su (Su Shi) is like hitching up a thousand-li colt and having it driven by Wang Liang (王良) or Zaofu (造父); if we provisionally cite one piece to illustrate the remainder, such as the three matters presented in his "Letter Submitted to Emperor Shenzong" (Shang Shenzong shu 上神宗書)…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
事廣譬博喻直欲致其君為堯舜湯武而
不犯逆鱗之怒真妙文矣至若制誥之文
得六經簡嚴之體者錢穆父作章子厚之
謫詞范純仁之遺表焉記述之文得六經
紀實之旨者王元之之記待漏院張伯玉
之記六經閣焉奏議之文如頴濱之言條
例張方平之諫用兵皆得伊訓呂誥之意
詩章之文如歐公之詠春帖蘇公之諷水
利皆得周雅商頌之體他如進士之文王
===
曾以賦策第而為賢相張庭堅以經義進
而為名臣豈可以科舉輕視之乎序述之
文程伊川自序易傳游定夫為孫莘老序
周易傳豈可以序體槩論乎之數子者立
言雖不同其所以精乎詞章而根於義理
則一也豈可專以詞章之文目之哉愚也
學古為文未聆其要惟執事恕其狂妄而
教之
第五問
punctuated:
事，廣譬博喻，直欲致其君為堯、舜、湯、武，而不犯逆鱗之怒，真妙文矣。至若制誥之文，得六經簡嚴之體者，錢穆父作章子厚之謫詞、范純仁之遺表焉；記述之文，得六經紀實之旨者，王元之之記待漏院、張伯玉之記六經閣焉；奏議之文，如頴濱之言條例、張方平之諫用兵，皆得《伊訓》、《呂誥》之意；詩章之文，如歐公之詠春帖、蘇公之諷水利，皆得周《雅》、商《頌》之體。他如進士之文，王曾以賦策第而為賢相，張庭堅以經義進而為名臣，豈可以科舉輕視之乎？序述之文，程伊川自序《易傳》，游定夫為孫莘老序《周易傳》，豈可以序體槩論乎？之數子者，立言雖不同，其所以精乎詞章而根於義理則一也，豈可專以詞章之文目之哉？愚也學古為文，未聆其要，惟執事恕其狂妄而教之。

第五問
translation_en:
…matters: drawing wide comparisons and broad analogies, it sought directly to make his sovereign into a Yao, Shun, Tang, or Wu without provoking the wrath of "brushing against the dragon's reverse scales"—truly a marvelous piece of writing! As for imperial edicts and patents of appointment (zhigao) that captured the concise and solemn style of the Six Classics, there were the edict of demotion for Zhang Zihou 章子厚 drafted by Qian Mufu 錢穆父 (Qian Xie 錢勰), and the testamentary memorial of Fan Chunren 范純仁. As for commemorative and narrative writings that captured the Six Classics' purport of recording facts, there were Wang Yuanzhi's 王元之 (Wang Yucheng 王禹偁) "Record of the Courtyard for Awaiting the Clepsydra at Dawn" (Dailou yuan ji 待漏院記) and Zhang Boyu's 張伯玉 "Record of the Pavilion of the Six Classics" (Liujing ge ji 六經閣記). As for memorials and deliberations, such as Yingbin's 頴濱 (Su Zhe 蘇轍) discussions of the Finance Planning Commission's regulations and Zhang Fangping's 張方平 remonstrances against the use of military force, they all captured the intent of the "Instructions of Yi" (Yi xun 伊訓) and the "Announcements of Lü" (Lü gao 呂誥) [in the Book of Documents]. As for poetic compositions, such as Master Ouyang's (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修) verses for spring帖子 (chuntie) and Master Su's (Su Shi 蘇軾) satirical poems on water-conservancy projects, they all captured the form of the Odes of Zhou (Zhou ya 周雅) and the Hymns of Shang (Shang song 商頌) [in the Book of Odes]. As for other writings such as those of metropolitan graduates (jinshi), Wang Zeng 王曾 passed the examinations on the strength of his rhapsodies and policy essays and became a worthy Grand Councilor, while Zhang Tingjian 張庭堅 advanced through his expositions on the Classics and became a renowned minister—how could one look down upon them merely as examination writings? As for prefaces, Cheng Yichuan 程伊川 (Cheng Yi 程頤) wrote his own preface to his Commentary on the Changes (Yi zhuan 易傳), and You Dingfu 游定夫 (You Zuo 游酢) wrote a preface to Sun Xinlao's 孫莘老 (Sun Jue 孫覺) Commentary on the Zhou Changes (Zhouyi zhuan 周易傳)—how could one lump them together under the general category of prefaces? Although these several gentlemen differed in how they established their words, they were one and the same in that their writings were refined in literary expression while rooted in moral principle. How could one regard them solely as works of ornate belles-lettres? In my ignorance, I have studied antiquity in order to compose literature, yet I have not grasped its essentials; I pray only that Your Excellency will pardon my rashness and instruct me.

Question Five

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
黃珣
同考試官學正陳批時務一策正觀士子變
通之學塲中答者多臆說令人厭觀惟此策有考
據有措置足見學識宜冠多士
考試官教授劉批策有定見真識時務者也
考試官教授鄭批時務一策足見有用之學
天下無不可用之人在勸懲之有道天下
無不可為之事在任用之得人盖勸懲有
道則守令將校之繼来新任者皆可盡其
===
用任用得人則風俗水利儲蓄賦役之事
皆可得而理矣執事先生發策而以浙之
切務所宜變通者下詢承學愚何足以知
之然一事不知儒者所耻執事以儒者俊
傑待承學敢不罄一得之愚以復乎夫守
令將校之不得其人在監司之勸懲有道
而風俗水利儲蓄賦役之咸得其理又在
藩臬令守之得人也盖監司所以肅百僚
而貞百度也藩司所以承流而宣化而守
punctuated:
黃珣
同考試官學正陳批：時務一策，正觀士子變通之學。塲中答者多臆說，令人厭觀；惟此策有考據，有措置，足見學識，宜冠多士。
考試官教授劉批：策有定見，真識時務者也。
考試官教授鄭批：時務一策，足見有用之學。

天下無不可用之人，在勸懲之有道；天下無不可為之事，在任用之得人。盖勸懲有道，則守令、將校之繼来新任者，皆可盡其用；任用得人，則風俗、水利、儲蓄、賦役之事，皆可得而理矣。執事先生發策，而以浙之切務所宜變通者，下詢承學。愚何足以知之？然一事不知，儒者所耻。執事以儒者俊傑待承學，敢不罄一得之愚以復乎？夫守令、將校之不得其人，在監司之勸懲有道；而風俗、水利、儲蓄、賦役之咸得其理，又在藩臬、令守之得人也。盖監司所以肅百僚而貞百度也，藩司所以承流而宣化，而守…
translation_en:
Huang Xun 黃珣
Comment by Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (學正) Chen: A policy essay on current affairs is precisely where one observes a scholar's learning in adapting to change. Those who answered in the examination hall mostly offered subjective conjectures, making one weary of reading them; only this policy essay has both textual evidence and practical measures, sufficiently demonstrating scholarship and insight, and it deserves to be placed first among the many scholars.
Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Instructor (教授) Liu: The policy essay shows settled judgment; he is truly one who understands current affairs.
Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Instructor Zheng: This policy essay on current affairs suffices to demonstrate practical learning.

In the world there are no people who cannot be employed—it lies in having the proper way of encouragement and punishment; in the world there are no affairs that cannot be accomplished—it lies in obtaining the right people for appointment. Indeed, when encouragement and punishment follow the proper way, then the prefects, magistrates, and military officers who succeed one another and newly take up office can all be utilized to the fullest; when the right people are obtained for appointment, then the affairs of popular customs, water control, grain reserves, and taxation and corvée can all be successfully put in order. You, the examiners, have posed this policy question, inquiring of us junior scholars about the urgent affairs of Zhejiang that ought to be adapted to changing circumstances. How could I, in my ignorance, be sufficient to know this? Yet to be ignorant of even a single matter is something a Confucian scholar considers shameful. Since you treat us junior scholars as outstanding Confucian talents, how dare I not exhaust my humble insights to reply? Now, when prefects, magistrates, and military officers are not the right people, the remedy lies in the Surveillance Commission officials (監司) having the proper way of encouragement and punishment; and for popular customs, water control, grain reserves, and taxation and corvée all to be properly managed, it in turn lies in obtaining the right people among the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions (藩臬) as well as the magistrates and prefects. For the Surveillance Commission is that by which the hundred officials are kept in awe and the hundred standards are rectified; the Provincial Administration Commission (藩司) is that by which the imperial grace is received and moral transformation is spread, while the prefects and…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
令則民之師帥也彼守令所以牧民當秉
庶潔之操将校所以領軍當有撫馭之才
今守令之貪墨者已罷黜之矣而繼来者
猶未端其操以執守之未定也将校之奸
貪者已更選之矣而新任者猶或非其才
以素習於膏梁也為監司者誠舉憲綱以
戒勵之嚴法令以訓飭之其能改過自新
者待以禮而不究其遂非不悛者置以法
而不貸則守令将校皆将悔禍懼罪之不
===
暇而變為庶潔有用之才矣民風欲淳也
而刁訟日滋民俗欲儉也而奢侈益甚由
積習之所致也為守令者誠能教以孝弟
道以忠信而強梗弗率者齊以刑食之以
時用之以禮而踰禮過用者禁以法則風
俗自淳儉矣浙西地卑而憂澇浙東地高
而憂旱由預防之無備也為守令者誠於
浙西疏大湖瀦蓄之水浚河港泥茭之積
俾遇澇則水由淞江而下流於海於浙東
punctuated:
令則民之師帥也。彼守令所以牧民，當秉庶潔之操；将校所以領軍，當有撫馭之才。今守令之貪墨者已罷黜之矣，而繼来者猶未端其操，以執守之未定也；将校之奸貪者已更選之矣，而新任者猶或非其才，以素習於膏梁也。為監司者，誠舉憲綱以戒勵之，嚴法令以訓飭之，其能改過自新者，待以禮而不究；其遂非不悛者，置以法而不貸。則守令、将校皆将悔禍懼罪之不暇，而變為庶潔有用之才矣。

民風欲淳也，而刁訟日滋；民俗欲儉也，而奢侈益甚，由積習之所致也。為守令者，誠能教以孝弟，道以忠信，而強梗弗率者齊以刑；食之以時，用之以禮，而踰禮過用者禁以法，則風俗自淳儉矣。

浙西地卑而憂澇，浙東地高而憂旱，由預防之無備也。為守令者，誠於浙西疏大湖瀦蓄之水，浚河港泥茭之積，俾遇澇則水由淞江而下流於海；於浙東
translation_en:
…and prefects and magistrates are the teachers and leaders of the people. Those prefects and magistrates, whose role is to shepherd the people, ought to uphold pure and incorruptible integrity [庶潔, reading 庶 as 廉]; military officers, whose role is to command troops, ought to possess the talent to pacify and control them. Nowadays, corrupt and venal prefects and magistrates have already been dismissed, yet their successors still have not rectified their conduct because their moral resolve is not yet firm; treacherous and greedy military officers have already been replaced, yet the newly appointed ones still sometimes lack the requisite talent because they have long been accustomed to a life of luxury. If those serving as surveillance officials truly uphold the disciplinary regulations to admonish and encourage them, and strictly enforce the laws and ordinances to instruct and reprimand them—treating with courtesy those who can reform their faults and renew themselves without pursuing their past offenses, while subjecting to the law without leniency those who persist in wrongdoing and refuse to repent—then prefects, magistrates, and military officers alike will be too preoccupied with regretting disaster and fearing punishment to do otherwise, and will transform into pure, incorruptible, and useful talents.

We wish for popular morals to be simple and honest, yet perverse litigation proliferates daily; we wish for popular customs to be frugal, yet extravagance grows ever more extreme. This is brought about by long-accumulated habits. If those serving as prefects and magistrates can truly teach the people filial piety and fraternal respect, guide them with loyalty and trustworthiness, and regulate the recalcitrant and disobedient with punishments; and if they ensure that resources are consumed in accordance with the seasons and used in accordance with ritual propriety, while prohibiting by law those who transgress ritual and indulge in excessive expenditure, then popular customs will naturally become simple, honest, and frugal.

Western Zhejiang lies on low ground and suffers from flooding, while Eastern Zhejiang lies on high ground and suffers from drought; this is due to a lack of preparedness in prevention. If those serving as prefects and magistrates truly dredge the waters stored in Lake Tai [大湖] in Western Zhejiang and clear the accumulated silt and water-reeds in the rivers and channels, so that when flooding occurs the water flows down through the Song River [淞江] into the sea; and in Eastern Zhejiang…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則浚湮塞之湖藪以瀦水脩廢弛之陂堰
以節流或遇旱則水以桔槔而上運於田
則旱澇可無虞矣自夫水旱之荐臻也民
仰食於公而秋成不足以償之是致倉廩
空虚况今歲水旱相仍何恠乎仰給者道
路相望乎自夫職守之匪人也豪右以富
囑閑而困窮者竭力以供役是致民多貧
乏况比歲軍需悉出於三等之人户又何
恠夫橫歛者項背相接乎今欲廣儲蓄以
===
給民必和糴於鄰封或勸助於富室而又
謹出納之令使羡餘不至於侵欺可也欲
均賦役以息民必停不急之徵蠲公上之
賦而又審貧富之徭使軍需仍復於舊額
可也之数者欲增實效不事虛文固在於
為守令者之得其人然防其奸而革其弊
作其怠而董其成又在於為藩臬者之同
其心如此則兩浙之務無難處者矣變通
之術無踰於此愚生風簷寸晷未暇援古
punctuated: 則浚湮塞之湖藪以瀦水，脩廢弛之陂堰以節流，或遇旱則水以桔槔而上運於田，則旱澇可無虞矣。自夫水旱之荐臻也，民仰食於公，而秋成不足以償之，是致倉廩空虚，况今歲水旱相仍，何恠乎仰給者道路相望乎？自夫職守之匪人也，豪右以富囑閑，而困窮者竭力以供役，是致民多貧乏，况比歲軍需悉出於三等之人户，又何恠夫橫歛者項背相接乎？今欲廣儲蓄以給民，必和糴於鄰封，或勸助於富室，而又謹出納之令，使羡餘不至於侵欺，可也。欲均賦役以息民，必停不急之徵，蠲公上之賦，而又審貧富之徭，使軍需仍復於舊額，可也。之数者，欲增實效，不事虛文，固在於為守令者之得其人；然防其奸而革其弊，作其怠而董其成，又在於為藩臬者之同其心。如此則兩浙之務無難處者矣，變通之術無踰於此。愚生風簷寸晷，未暇援古
translation_en: …they dredge the silted lakes and marshes to store water, and repair neglected dikes and weirs to regulate its flow, so that if a drought occurs, water can be raised into the fields using well-sweeps; then neither drought nor flood need be a cause for worry. Because floods and droughts have struck repeatedly, the people have looked to the public granaries for food, while the autumn harvests have been insufficient to repay the loans. This has caused the granaries to become empty; especially this year, when floods and droughts have followed one upon another, what wonder is it that those looking for relief are seen all along the roads? Because those holding office are not the right men, the powerful and wealthy use their riches to bribe their way into idleness, while the distressed and impoverished exhaust their strength in performing labor services. This has caused the majority of the people to fall into poverty; especially in recent years, when military supplies have been drawn entirely from the three grades of households, what wonder is it that arbitrary exactions follow closely one after another? Now, if we wish to expand reserves to supply the people, we must purchase grain harmoniously from neighboring jurisdictions or encourage contributions from wealthy households, and furthermore strictly enforce the regulations on receipts and disbursements so that surpluses are not embezzled—that will suffice. If we wish to equalize taxes and corvée to give rest to the people, we must halt non-urgent levies, remit public taxes due to the state, and furthermore carefully assess labor services according to poverty and wealth so that military requisitions are restored to their former quotas—that will suffice. In these several matters, if we wish to increase practical results and not engage in empty formalities, it certainly depends on obtaining the right men to serve as Prefects and Magistrates; yet preventing deceit and eradicating abuses, rousing theindolent and supervising their achievements, depends in turn on the Provincial Administration Commissioners and Surveillance Commissioners uniting their hearts. If this is done, there will be nothing difficult to manage in the affairs of Western and Eastern Zhejiang, and the art of adapting to circumstances cannot surpass this. Under the windswept eaves with only an inch of shadow on the sundial, this foolish student has no leisure to cite antiquity…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以對姑述耳之所聞如此倘與而進焉尚
當以天下之務為執事陳之
===
浙江鄉試錄後序
上天純佑我
皇明文運誕興乃今成化七年歲
當賓興賢能巡按浙江監察
御史郭瑞暨藩臬重臣預期
禮聘儒紳以司考試及期合
十一郡士凡三試之拔其尤
punctuated:
以對，姑述耳之所聞如此。倘與而進焉，尚當以天下之務為執事陳之。

translation_en:
… to respond, so I merely recount what I have heard in this manner. Should I be approved and advanced, I shall yet set forth the affairs of the realm before Your Excellency.

Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

High Heaven purely blesses our August Ming, and the fortune of literary culture has grandly flourished. Now, in this seventh year of the Chenghua era [1471], the year scheduled for presenting the worthy and capable as honored guests, Regional Inspector of Zhejiang and Investigating Censor Guo Rui 郭瑞, together with the senior officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions, in advance courteously invited Confucian scholars and gentry to take charge of the examinations. title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者九十人遵
定額也既次第其名氏復集其
文之純雅者為錄將以獻于
上僉謂襄宜序其末欽惟
太祖高皇帝肇開文運科目取士
雖以文藝而學校教人必先
德行盖與舜之命司徒以敷
===
五教命典樂以教胄子同一
揆也
列聖相承率由是道
皇上嗣位益篤前烈既
勅憲臣提督內外學校復命禮
部申示教條皆先德行而後
文藝凡師之所以教弟子之
punctuated: 者九十人，遵定額也。既次第其名氏，復集其文之純雅者為錄，將以獻于上。僉謂襄宜序其末。欽惟太祖高皇帝肇開文運，科目取士雖以文藝，而學校教人必先德行，盖與舜之命司徒以敷五教、命典樂以教胄子同一揆也。列聖相承，率由是道。皇上嗣位，益篤前烈，既勅憲臣提督內外學校，復命禮部申示教條，皆先德行而後文藝。凡師之所以教、弟子之
translation_en:
… [selected the most outstanding] ninety men, in compliance with the fixed quota. Having ranked their names in order, we have further gathered their most pure and refined compositions to compile this record, which is about to be presented to His Majesty. All agreed that I, [Pan] Xiang, ought to write a postface at its end.

I reverently reflect that when Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), first inaugurated the flourishing of literary culture, although the recruiting of scholars through the examination categories was done by means of literary arts, the instruction of men in the schools invariably put moral conduct first. Indeed, this was founded on the exact same principle as when Shun commanded the Minister of Education (situ) to propagate the Five Teachings and commanded the Director of Music (dianyue) to teach the sons of state. The successive Sacred Emperors inherited this tradition one after another, all following this very Way. Since His Majesty succeeded to the throne, he has shown even greater devotion to the achievements of his predecessors. Having issued imperial commands to Censorate officials to serve as Education Intendants for the schools in the capital and the provinces, he further ordered the Ministry of Rites to reiterate and promulgate the regulations for instruction, all of which place moral conduct first and literary arts second. In all by which teachers instruct and disciples…

title: 成化七年浙江鄉試錄
text:
所以學涵育陶鎔無非所以
造成厥德故凡來試者彬彬
然善言德行而登名者則又
盛焉者也
聖天子七八年間德化感人淪肌
浹髓有如是夫孔子嘗曰有
德者必有言程子亦曰德盛

translation_en: …what students study, through nurturing and molding, is nothing other than a means of cultivating their virtue. Therefore, all who came to take the examination were refined and adept at speaking of virtuous conduct, while those whose names were placed on the roster of successful candidates were even more flourishing in this regard. How deeply has the Sage Son of Heaven’s moral transformation over the past seven or eight years moved people, penetrating their very flesh and marrow!
